documents.title: About Shoalrun
documents.summary: Learn what Shoalrun is exploring and where the private prototype stands.
documents.text: I'm CT Smith, and I'm building Shoalrun cause there's no such thing as a perfect doc tool. I have opinions, undirected rage, and curiosity about doc-building tools. I built my first documentation generator back in 2015. It was based on Jekyll and relied heavily (probably too heavily) on general templating and... you guessed it... page metadata . Shoalrun is part art project, part portfolio piece, and part laboratory. I use it to push the limits of content and tooling in whatever domain I'm working in. I had a lot of sources of inspiration (both negative and positive) from my years as a tech writer and tooling lover. I wanted to build something maximally flexible that also could keep things on the rails. I wanted something that uses frontmatter for deterministic features that feel like AI. I also wanted to play with what a BYO search and chat hookup could look like. And also leave room for others to use as much AI as they want. I wanted to chew on how to give human and AI readers content that works for them without cognitive—or contextual???—overload. No, I'm not saying AI has true cognition; stick with me here. I want flashy interactive components that help humans understand a concept. I also want agents to get the useful information without the extra junk—and WITHOUT extra authoring work. I centered the design with this project around making everything for two audiences: humans and agents. Not one above the other because it's honestly trivial to give them both what they need. I guess the more polished marketing-friendly summary is: One source can serve different readers without fuss. Shoalrun lets authors shape the browser experience and choose what enters agent-facing Markdown. Authors can add content for one format when readers need different explanations. The framework also provides settings and extension points for the rest of a documentation site. What makes Shoalrun special What interests me most is the interconnectedness that comes from treating information as a first-class object. Each doc has its own identity, metadata, and relationships. Its stable ID connects links, navigation, cards, and related reading, so I can move the source file without breaking those connections. See how Shoalrun works . I want config to be composable, too. I can keep navigation, API sources, templates, and other settings in small YAML files. Includes and presets combine them; I can trace each value's source. The project can grow without forcing every concern into one config file. See configuration composition . Presenting and linking content for humans and agents are first-class features. A rich component has an explicit form in both the browser and the page's Markdown twin. The build can turn one accepted source into interactive HTML, agent-readable Markdown, /llms.txt , and a document manifest. It rejects unsupported dynamic MDX instead of silently dropping content. Authors can still write a section for just one output when that reader needs a different explanation. See agent-friendly output . This structure also makes workflows easier to connect. An ingredient can be reused in a complete recipe, and a cookbook can assemble the reviewed recipes a reader selects into one path. See recipes and cookbooks . API content follows the same approach. Local OpenAPI files can supply reference pages, examples, and focused contracts for individual operations. A public build requires a review digest for imported API content, so a changed source returns to review before publication. See API review . I'm building Shoalrun for tinkerers like me, who will never be fully satisfied with a mass market docs tool. Docs are never one-size-fits-all, on any level. As for project's current status and future -- right now, only this documentation site is public. The compiler and CLI remain private prototype code and are not available to install. yee haw forever, CT

documents.title: Create a page
documents.summary: Create a page from a template, complete its scaffolded draft, and publish it in navigation.
documents.text: Create a page from a template with scaffold . Templates prompt you for the page's frontmatter, an introduction, the main content, and related pages before you publish. This is the recommended authoring workflow for new pages. This guide assumes you have completed getting started and are working in my-docs/ . Keep SHOALRUN_CLI pointing to the checkout's framework/dist/cli.js . Choose a template Choose the template that matches what the reader needs to accomplish. Template Use it for tutorial A reliable guided exercise for learning by doing. how-to A specific task, with practical actions and a success check. reference Exact syntax, fields, options, examples, errors, and limits. explanation Concepts, context, reasons, and tradeoffs. api-reference Editorial context above generated operation details; requires one known operation ID. recipe A complete task used by recipe and cookbook workflows. ingredient One reusable action or check used in recipes. cookbook A page that helps readers choose complete recipes. These templates ship with the CLI. guide and troubleshooting remain available for compatibility. Projects can register additional templates or override built-ins. The CLI includes a recipe template for a complete customer task, written directly or assembled from ingredients. Built-in ingredient and cookbook templates support reusable steps and workflow selection. The ingredient draft command can start one ingredient from an API example; recipe draft assembles an ordered set of ingredient files for review. Use the project's template for the document type when one exists. Project templates can also override the built-in names. See templates to register or change one. Scaffold the draft From the project directory: node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" scaffold how-to -n content/track-parcel.mdx \ --id how-to.track-parcel --title 'Track a parcel' The command finds docs.config.yaml , creates the file, and adds the template body and draft frontmatter. It refuses to overwrite an existing file. This example sets the stable ID and title explicitly; the CLI derives the slug /track-parcel from the target path. Without overrides, this path would produce ID how-to.track-parcel and title Track Parcel . The generated summary starts with Draft guide for and must be replaced before publication. Publication fields come from your project configuration. Complete the template Open content/track-parcel.mdx and work through its prompts: Read the comments in the frontmatter, fill in the placeholder fields, and delete the comment lines. Set updated to today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Write an introduction of 150 words or fewer and remove irrelevant optional sections. Follow the chosen shape. Write a guided exercise, practical task actions, organized reference facts, or conceptual discussion. For this how-to, write actions and checks. Keep the HTML, Markdown, and agents section when the page uses a component or behavior that changes either output or what an agent reads. Otherwise delete it. Add relationships for the page, or delete Related reading. Verify technical claims before you publish. Replace every TODO prompt enclosed in double square brackets. Adapt the sections to the task rather than leaving irrelevant prompts behind. Templates provide a starting structure; editing a template later does not rewrite this page. The quickstart shows a completed example. Keep the generated access.policy: draft while writing. Drafts are validated but omitted from the published site, even if the starter defaults to public access. Headings in the body begin at level 2 because Shoalrun renders the page title separately. Publish the page After reviewing the content, change the generated access value to: access : { policy : public } Keep the ID how-to.track-parcel and slug /track-parcel for this example. Check the channel, version, and language match an enabled publication. The build rejects public pages with unresolved template prompts or the generated draft summary. See page metadata for shared defaults and publication rules. The generated frontmatter reference lists native fields and this site's project declarations. Put it in navigation Append this item to the existing navigation list in docs.config.yaml : - id : track-parcel doc : how-to.track-parcel Use the page's frontmatter ID for doc ; the navigation item's own id identifies that menu entry. You can nest the item under a group's items list instead. Navigation uses the page title as its label unless you supply label . A public page can have a working URL without appearing in the sidebar. Adding this entry makes it discoverable there. See organize navigation for groups, includes, and links. Verify HTML and Markdown From the project directory: node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" build docs.config.yaml site-dist node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" serve site-dist --port 8765 Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/track-parcel and confirm that the page appears in navigation and that its links work. Then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/track-parcel.md and c

documents.title: Configure the agent discovery block
documents.summary: Choose how early HTML guidance appears, customize its wording, and verify its links.

headings.title: Set the message and link labels

documents.text: Configure the early HTML guidance so readers and agents can find the article, Markdown twin, and documentation index. Work in an existing Shoalrun project with a working local build. Choose the presentation Set site.agentDiscovery to change the early HTML instruction. The default mode: focus hides it visually until keyboard focus enters its links. Choose visible for an always-shown banner, or disclosure for a compact For agents toggle in the header that starts closed. All three modes include the guidance links in the HTML source. Choose off to omit the block from HTML entirely. The mode controls visual presentation and whether the block is included. Screen readers and agents parsing raw HTML can encounter the guidance in both focus and visible modes. The disclosure uses native HTML details and summary , so it works without JavaScript. Agents using screenshots see the same visual presentation as humans and need to open the disclosure to see its links. Some HTML extraction tools discard visually hidden elements; the document head also provides discovery links. This setting does not control access to documentation or make the guidance private. Set the message and link labels docs.config.yaml site : title : Cedar Parcel documentation agentDiscovery : mode : disclosure label : For agents message : Use Markdown for complete examples and nested schemas. links : article : Jump to the article index : Browse documentation markdown : Read Markdown The message and labels are plain text. Shoalrun generates the article, index, and Markdown destinations, including the site's base path. The standard Skip to content link stays first, even with the agent block disabled. The index destination is the compact text index, /llms.min.txt . It links to full Markdown pages and author-declared standalone sections with sizes and full-page fallbacks. The HTML head’s rel="describedby" link and each Markdown page’s index backlink use the same compact index, including when the visible block is off. The detailed /llms.txt index remains linked from the compact index. These settings affect HTML only; the Markdown index link and discovery files remain available. See the configuration reference for defaults and validation rules. Build and check the result Run these commands from the directory containing docs.config.yaml : shoalrun check docs.config.yaml shoalrun build docs.config.yaml site-dist shoalrun serve site-dist --port 8765 Open a documentation page at http://127.0.0.1:8765/ . With focus , press Tab until the guidance links receive focus and the block appears. With visible , confirm the block appears before focusing it. With disclosure , confirm the header toggle starts closed, opens with Enter or a click, and exposes working links. With off , confirm the block is absent and Skip to content still works. Follow the article, index, and Markdown links. The article link should move focus to the main content; the index should open /llms.min.txt , and the Markdown link should open the current page's .md twin. A configured base path prefixes the generated resource URLs. View the HTML source to confirm that all three enabled modes include the links. The Markdown twin and discovery files should remain available in all three modes. If labels or destinations look wrong, check site.agentDiscovery in the resolved config and rebuild. Stop the server with Ctrl+C when finished. Copy the page as Markdown Use Copy as Markdown beside Read as Markdown to copy the current page's published Markdown twin. The button fetches the full file, including metadata and all reader-labeled sections, regardless of the selected HTML reader view. It uses the page's publication and base path. Activate the button with Enter, Space, or a tap. A visible status announces success or failure to screen readers. If fetching or clipboard access fails, use Read as Markdown to open and copy the file manually. The plain link also works without JavaScript; the copy button appears when its script loads. Browser clipboard access requires a secure context and permission. Related reading Reference while working Configuration reference — Look up discovery modes, defaults, labels, and validation rules. Related topics Agent-friendly documentation — Understand how HTML guidance, Markdown, and discovery files serve different readers.

documents.summary: See how interactive docs become readable Markdown, then discover pages and verify their contents.

headings.title: What happens to an unsupported component?
Discover a page with a small context budget

Distinguish examples from a real service
Use the transport your client supports

documents.text: Shoalrun lets people use an interactive documentation page while agents read a Markdown copy of the same instructions. Tabs, closed disclosures, and reader choices should not make essential content disappear from that copy. The build checks that it knows how to turn each component into readable Markdown. If it does not, it stops with an error. Each generated Markdown page also has a SHA-256 digest, a fingerprint of its bytes. An agent can compare it with the fetched file to verify that the bytes match the published manifest. Try the example below. Switch the client tab, open Retry detail , and choose a reader. Then compare what is visible with the Markdown underneath, which retains both clients, the retry advice, and both reader sections. You can also open this page's actual Markdown . Try the page controls Command line Application Command line Send the request from a terminal. Application Send the request from application code. Retry detail Retry only after checking whether the first request succeeded. Open the activity screen to inspect the result. Inspect the response status and returned identifier. What an agent reads Here is the Markdown generated from the example above. An agent does not need to click the tabs, expand the disclosure, or choose a reader to get these instructions. ### Command line Send the request from a terminal. ### Application Send the request from application code. ### Retry detail Retry only after checking whether the first request succeeded. **For Reader: UI reader.** Open the activity screen to inspect the result. **For Reader: Developer.** Inspect the response status and returned identifier. The labels become headings or ordinary text. The controls themselves are omitted. This site's test compares the example's generated Markdown with the text shown here so they cannot drift apart unnoticed. The reader views reference explains how authors configure those choices. What happens to an unsupported component? A component needs rendering support for both HTML and Markdown. The compiler calls that support an adapter . If a page uses an unknown component such as the one below, Shoalrun stops rather than publishing a Markdown file that silently loses its contents. < UnregisteredPanel > This instruction must not disappear. </ UnregisteredPanel > Running shoalrun check docs.config.yaml in the private prototype reports a diagnostic containing: <UnregisteredPanel> has no semantic/Markdown adapter The example is displayed as code here so you can read it. A test also runs it as an actual component, checks that compilation fails, and verifies that the previous successful output remains intact. This check establishes how unsupported components are handled; it does not prove that every supported component or authored instruction is correct. Discover a page with a small context budget An agent does not need to download every discovery artifact. Start with /llms.min.txt , select a matching page, and fetch its supplied Markdown URL. The compact list contains IDs, titles, summaries, publication labels, and full-page Markdown links. Nested section links appear only for author-declared standalone topics and include exact sizes plus a Full page fallback. Default to the full page for setup or broader questions. This site tests a 6,000-token discovery budget with the cl100k_base tokenizer, excluding the selected page. Other sites and tokenizers can differ. Choose another artifact only when the task needs it: Resource When to use it llms.min.txt Find full pages and declared standalone sections from a text list; follow the supplied URL. search-index.min.json Inspect page headings as well as summaries, without article text. llms.txt Browse grouped page links, API downloads, and discovery resources. documents.json Read complete page metadata, digests, relationships, and contract links. documents.sync.json Compare a saved inventory with the current build. build-info.json Check whether the assembled build has changed. Both search indexes are generated when search indexing is enabled. The full /search-index.json includes bounded article text for browser search, CLI search, and custom lexical fallbacks. It remains available, but it is not needed to find a page through the compact list. These files are downloadable indexes, not query endpoints. Shoalrun does not produce llms-full.txt . HTML pages provide a visible Read as Markdown link, a rel="alternate" link, and optional early agent guidance. The guidance links to the article, the compact index, and the current twin. The HTML head’s rel="describedby" link and Markdown index backlinks also point to /llms.min.txt , so entering through either format leads to the same starting list. Follow those supplied links when a fetch tool rejects guessed URLs. Compact-list links are site-relative; resolve them against the fetched index's origin. documents.title: Bundled agent skills
documents.summary: Skill names, locations, workflow behavior, offline documentation, and validation limits.
documents.text: Shoalrun ships five portable skill folders under framework/skills/ . Each folder contains a SKILL.md with instructions for an agent that can read files and run the Shoalrun CLI. A skill supplies guidance; it does not run a separate authoring service. These are authoring skills for Shoalrun. The build does not create a reader-side skill for each published site. Agents reading a generated site use its Markdown twins, /llms.txt , and /documents.json . A non-interactive skill builder is a non-goal : skill creation and maintenance need guidance from a human expert. Skill inventory Each skill supplies instructions for a specific part of the authoring workflow. Skill Use it for shoalrun-setup Start a docs project, choose a working example config, build it, and inspect its first HTML and Markdown pages. shoalrun-author Add or revise pages, navigation, API links, snippets, and project tests with the agent's own model and Shoalrun CLI. It uses normal file edits, project discovery, isolated validation, and snapshot review/preview tools. shoalrun-recipes Write task-oriented how-tos as complete recipes, reuse ingredients where helpful, and configure cookbook choices. shoalrun-component-author Create trusted custom components , validate their schemas and shared content, and review HTML/Markdown parity. shoalrun-walkthrough Turn notes, a tutorial, or project code into a walkthrough that explains code step by step. Each folder name matches its skill name. For example, the author skill's entry file is framework/skills/shoalrun-author/SKILL.md . Installation locations depend on the agent. Use the bundled agent skills describes choosing and invoking one. Workflow behavior The setup skill uses shoalrun init to create a project from the bundled minimal or api-docs starter, then uses config validate , build , and dev to check the result. The author skill uses stable IDs and project config provenance so edits stay attached to the intended publication. The walkthrough skill chooses a mode and layout, prefers code taken from project files, and checks each step's highlight. The recipes skill starts from a reader goal and success check, reuses ingredient source when useful, and distinguishes authoring from browser selection. All five ask the agent to inspect generated HTML and Markdown. They leave deployment decisions with the site owner. The author skill starts with project-wide discovery and policy reads, captures a task baseline, and edits ordinary working-tree files. It validates a separate capture and opens the matching snapshot review/preview. Required companions come from project policy; compiler success does not waive them. Existing local edits are included in the baseline rather than attributed to the new task. No extra authoring model key is needed. Explicit checked-plan clients can still use Apply a checked edit plan . Component-authoring skill shoalrun-component-author guides a coding agent through creating or repairing a trusted component plugin. It asks the agent to inventory essential content and decide what belongs in MDX and data. The agent then writes validation and shared content, adds browser controls where needed, and tests both representations. The agent produces project files, fixtures, usage examples, check results, and a local preview for review. The skill is an instruction file, not a compiler feature or an automatic React-to-Markdown converter. The component author and agent must write the complete static explanation. A passing build does not establish that every interactive choice or warning is represented faithfully. Custom components shows a small copy button with content in MDX, generated Markdown, and a sample agent request. Data-driven React components adds a local policy file and generated explanations. Offline documentation All five skills can consult Shoalrun's bundled docs through a local, agent-neutral tool: shoalrun docs search "API reference navigation" shoalrun docs read guide.api-references Search returns JSON with document IDs and excerpts. Read returns the complete generated Markdown page. The commands work offline and do not require a docs site to be running. They are useful to any agent that can run a CLI, even when it cannot discover SKILL.md files automatically. Limits Skills guide the agent's actions. They cannot establish whether a technical claim is true. Shoalrun's audit checks implemented build and representation rules and any configured external tests. Human review and behavior tests establish whether the instructions work. The recipes skill prefers complete task pages, adds ingredients when instructions are shared, and uses cookbooks when readers need help choosing tasks. It respects an explicitly requested format. Ingredients, recipes, and cookbooks explains those distinctions. Maintain bundled skills covers changes to the shipped workflows and documentation bundle. documents.text: Give an agent a bundled skill when you want it to follow Shoalrun's setup, authoring, recipe, component, or walkthrough workflow. You need an agent that can read the skill file and run commands, plus a Shoalrun checkout or installed CLI. Choose the skill for your task Use shoalrun-setup to start a site, shoalrun-author to add or revise pages, shoalrun-recipes to write a complete task recipe, or shoalrun-walkthrough to explain code in steps. Use shoalrun-component-author to create trusted custom components. The skill reference lists their locations and behavior. Make the instructions available Install the complete folder in your agent's skill directory using that agent's installation process. If it supports reading repository files directly, point it at the entry file instead. For a recipe task, use framework/skills/shoalrun-recipes/SKILL.md . In an installed package, skill folders live under node_modules/@shoalrun/cli/skills/ . These files are portable instructions; the CLI does not install them into your agent automatically. Give your agent the installed shoalrun-author/SKILL.md path and the consumer project's docs.config.yaml path. Use the existing harness's file, terminal, and browser tools. No separate authoring service or model configuration is required. Ask the agent to read the skill before beginning. If it cannot discover installed skills, include the file path. If it cannot read files or run a CLI, follow the page creation workflow yourself. Give the agent a bounded request Name the task, documentation project, relevant source files, and result to check. For example: Read framework/skills/shoalrun-recipes/SKILL.md and use its workflow. Write a complete recipe for previewing a Shoalrun documentation change. Work in this checkout's docs project. Include setup, commands, failure guidance, and a final success check. Reuse existing ingredients where instructions are shared. Preserve IDs and routes when updating pages, and set updated to today's date. Show the diff and verification results. For a page edit, name the stable document ID and the facts that must stay unchanged. Use a coding agent with Shoalrun explains native editing and checks. Check working-tree documentation edits covers baselines, validation, and matching previews. Check the result Ask the agent to show the changed files, rendered HTML and Markdown, and results from the project's checks. Read the diff and verify technical claims against the source or API contract. For an existing page, confirm its ID and route are preserved and updated records the edit date. If the agent lacks product guidance, have it run shoalrun docs search and shoalrun docs read using the offline documentation commands . If a build or audit fails, ask it to fix the reported issue and rerun the check. A passing check covers the implemented rules; review the task instructions and factual claims before committing or publishing. Related reading Reference while working Bundled agent skills — Look up shipped skill names, locations, workflows, and offline documentation behavior. Related topics Frontmatter field reference — Point agents at the local inventory of page fields this project accepts. Apply a checked edit plan — Let an agent run the same draft, check, and apply loop. (Status: experimental.) Maintain bundled skills — Use the workflows in a documentation project. Getting started — Give an agent the same setup and authoring workflow as a bundled skill. Use your coding agent — Give your coding agent the bundled Shoalrun workflow instructions.

documents.title: Bring your own analytics
documents.summary: Send documentation interaction events to your analytics service through an optional browser adapter.
documents.text: Shoalrun sends documentation interactions to an analytics service through an adapter : a browser module you supply to initialize the service and deliver events. Analytics is off by default. Shoalrun includes no service SDK, storage, visitor identity, or delivery queue. Configure an adapter Point analytics.module at a local .js or .mjs file: docs.config.yaml analytics : module : ./analytics.js Paths resolve relative to the declaring config file, including included files. The build copies the module to /assets/analytics-adapter.js without executing or bundling it. Supply a self-contained module or use browser-resolvable imports; relative imports resolve from the copied asset directory. The file becomes public browser code. For example, if your page already initializes a client named myAnalytics , forward events to its capture method: analytics.js export function track (event) { globalThis . myAnalytics .capture ( event .name , event .properties); } Replace the client and method with your service’s API. Set analytics: false , or omit the setting, to exclude the runtime, adapter, and page context. Unknown settings, unsupported extensions, and missing files fail the build. Adapter exports and consent Implement these exports in your browser module: Export Required Contract track(event) Yes Receive an event; may return a promise. The adapter owns delivery, batching, retries, and flushing before navigation. init(context) No Initialize the service or await consent; may return a promise. Events start after it resolves. The read-only context provides page properties, setEnabled(boolean) , and track(name, properties, element?) . Import or initialization failures disable analytics for the page. Thrown or rejected track calls are caught without interrupting controls or navigation; Shoalrun does not retry them. Events are discarded while initialization is pending or delivery is disabled. After initialization, Shoalrun sends page_view if enabled. To delay collection, await consent in init , or call setEnabled(false) and enable delivery from your consent callback. In the latter case, call track('page_view') after enabling to count the current page. You can also disable delivery through the public hook: globalThis . shoalrunAnalytics ?.setEnabled ( false ); Connect consent changes to your SDK too. Disabling Shoalrun does not stop SDK-generated events, unload the SDK, or revoke data already sent. Event format Each event has schemaVersion , name , and properties . For example: { "schemaVersion" : 1 , "name" : "content_tab_change" , "properties" : { "pageId" : "guide.example" , "pageUrl" : "/example" , "documentType" : "reference" , "channel" : "production" , "version" : "current" , "language" : "en" , "navigationSectionId" : "docs" , "componentId" : "clients:tabs:1" , "componentType" : "tabs" , "headingId" : "clients" , "tabIndex" : 1 , "tabId" : "clients-2" } } Every event includes page identity and publication properties; navigationSectionId appears only for pages in a navigation tab. pageUrl is the published path without query or fragment. Custom properties cannot replace page identity. Events associated with an element add component context. componentId uses data-analytics-id , then the element’s HTML ID, then its heading, kind, and position. Generated IDs can change when content moves. componentType is tabs , walkthrough , disclosure , code , or control ; headingId identifies the preceding article heading when available. Built-in events Use these events to measure browser interactions. Each includes the page properties above. Event Additional properties Trigger page_view None Once after adapter initialization, when delivery is enabled. navigation_click region , targetPath , external A section, sidebar, outline, breadcrumb, related-reading, card, hero, footer, header, article, or Markdown-action link is activated. content_tab_change tabIndex , tabId A different content tab is selected by click or keyboard. Initial selection and hash reveals are excluded. disclosure_toggle open A reader opens or closes a Collapsible or article InfoHint through its summary. Programmatic initialization is excluded. walkthrough_step_change stepIndex , stepCount , layout , trigger A different walkthrough step becomes active through click, keyboard, or step scrolling. Initial selection and layout changes are excluded. code_copy language , optional stepIndex A code example or walkthrough pane is successfully written to the clipboard. markdown_copy None The full Markdown twin is successfully written to the clipboard. section_link_copy targetHeadingId A heading's link is successfully written to the clipboard. search_results queryLength , resultCount , status A completed search settles for 300 ms. Status is results , empty , or error ; the count is the displayed result count. search_result_click queryLength , resultIndex , targetPath A search result is activated, including through the keyboard. reader_filter_change scope , filter_<facet> , opti

documents.text: Start with a registered local API from Add an OpenAPI API . Use generation when you want references for many operations without writing an MDX page for each one. The commands below run in your documentation project with SHOALRUN_CLI set as in the quickstart. Choose generated references or MDX Use build-time generated references when the OpenAPI contract already gives readers the method, path, parameters, schemas, and examples they need. The pages update whenever the reviewed source changes, and there are no MDX files to maintain. Use an authored MDX reference when an endpoint needs a reviewed introduction, prerequisites, limitations, or task-specific context that the contract cannot express. The compiler still appends the contract details from OpenAPI, so do not copy field tables and example payloads into MDX. Use a guide for a task spanning several endpoints; link its reference pages with relatedApiReferences . The one-time api materialize command creates draft MDX references for every endpoint or selected source operation IDs or method/path routes. It does not change config or navigation and never rewrites an existing page. For example: node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" api materialize notes docs.config.yaml --all node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" api materialize notes docs.config.yaml --operation getNote node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" api materialize notes docs.config.yaml --route 'GET /notes/{id}' The default destination is content/api/<api-id>/ ; use --output for another directory inside the configured content tree. Selectors use the OpenAPI operationId or exact uppercase method and path. Repeating a command reports the existing matching page as skipped. A file with a conflicting identity stops the job before it writes anything. Existing authored references also count as skipped. Each new page has a stable document ID, slug, operation binding, and access.policy: draft . The draft contains an editorial prompt. While it remains a draft, any already selected build-time reference continues to publish. Review the text, replace the prompt, then set access to public ; that MDX page takes the generated page's place for its publication. This also works when generateReferences is off: the authored page binds to the registered API's local OpenAPI source. The command never enables build-time generation, changes the public review digest, or chooses navigation order for you. Run api review before publishing changed API content, and place the reference with operation: or doc: in navigation if it is not already covered by a generator. Generate many pages selectively For a large API, set generateReferences on its API config. This avoids writing one MDX file and registry entry for every operation. The build scans the local spec and creates HTML and Markdown reference pages for selected operations. An explicit operations entry and authored page take precedence for that operation. The example Create a note page is authored, while its Get a note page is generated. The example below uses this site's two-operation Notes source , which contains createNote and getNote . To try it after the tutorial, replace your one-operation apis/notes/openapi.yaml with that source first. Keep the authored Create a note page and its binding. Store the generation choices in a separate config file: config/api.yaml notes : publicReview : digest : <digest-from-your-api-review> source : { kind : file , path : ../apis/notes/openapi.yaml , publish : true } operations : - { id : notes.create , sourceOperationId : createNote , reference : reference.create-note } generateReferences : { $include : ./notes-pages.yaml } config/notes-pages.yaml pathPrefix : /example-api/generated include : [ getNote ] include lists source operationId values to generate; an empty list generates none. You can use exclude instead to generate all but named operations, or set generateReferences: true to generate every operation without an authored binding. The build rejects unknown selection IDs. Generated IDs and URLs derive from the API ID and source operationId , not the operation summary, so editing a title does not move the page. If an operationId changes, add an authored binding when the old public identity must remain stable. For an API notes and operationId: getNote , the generator creates: Value Pattern Example Stable operation ID <apiId>.<operationId> notes.getNote Page ID reference.<apiId>.<operationId> reference.notes.getNote Slug <pathPrefix>/<kebab-case operationId>-<8-character hash> /example-api/generated/get-note-cbedb319 pathPrefix defaults to /reference/<apiId> . An operationId with characters outside letters, digits, . , _ , and - uses the kebab-case name plus the hash in place of the raw ID. Use the page ID in relatedApiReferences and the stable operation ID in navigation operation: entries. Generated pages pass through global frontmatter defaults and enforced values, so an enforced value or a required custom field applies to them too. The pag

The build scans the local spec and creates HTML and Markdown reference pages for selected operations. An explicit operations entry and authored page take precedence for that operation. The example Create a note page is authored, while its Get a note page is generated. The example below uses this site's two-operation Notes source , which contains createNote and getNote . To try it after the tutorial, replace your one-operation apis/notes/openapi.yaml with that source first. Keep the authored Create a note page and its binding. Store the generation choices in a separate config file: notes: publicReview: digest: <digest-from-your-api-review> source: { kind: file, path: ../apis/notes/openapi.yaml, publish: true } operations: - { id: notes.create, sourceOperationId: createNote, reference: reference.create-note } generateReferences: { $include: ./notes-pages.yaml } pathPrefix: /example-api/generated include: [getNote] include lists source operationId values to generate; an empty list generates none. You can use exclude instead to generate all but named operations, or set generateReferences: true to generate every operation without an authored binding. The build rejects unknown selection IDs. Generated IDs and URLs derive from the API ID and source operationId , not the operation summary, so editing a title does not move the page. If an operationId changes, add an authored binding when the old public identity must remain stable. For an API notes and operationId: getNote , the generator creates: Value Pattern Example Stable operation ID <apiId>.<operationId> notes.getNote Page ID reference.<apiId>.<operationId> reference.notes.getNote Slug <pathPrefix>/<kebab-case operationId>-<8-character hash> /example-api/generated/get-note-cbedb319 pathPrefix defaults to /reference/<apiId> . An operationId with characters outside letters, digits, . , _ , and - uses the kebab-case name plus the hash in place of the raw ID. Use the page ID in relatedApiReferences and the stable operation ID in navigation operation: entries. Generated pages pass through global frontmatter defaults and enforced values, so an enforced value or a required custom field applies to them too. The page title is the operation summary , or the method and path when there is no summary. OpenAPI 3.1 webhooks can us

documents.text: Add one authored API reference to the project created in the quickstart . You will register an operation, write its introduction, add it to navigation, review the imported content, and verify its published files. Run commands from your documentation project directory. SHOALRUN_CLI is the absolute path to framework/dist/cli.js set in the quickstart. Check OpenAPI support and limits before importing a larger specification. Put the spec in your project Create apis/notes/openapi.yaml with this complete fictional API. It documents a response without calling a live service: apis/notes/openapi.yaml openapi : 3.1.0 info : { title : Example Notes API , version : 1.0.0 } paths : /notes : post : operationId : createNote summary : Create a note responses : '201' : description : The note was created. content : application/json : schema : type : object required : [ id ] properties : id : { type : string , description : The new note identifier. } examples : created : summary : A created note value : { id : note_123 } OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 YAML and JSON files are accepted. There is no required directory name; a spec can also reference other local files. Register the operation Add this top-level entry to your existing docs.config.yaml : docs.config.yaml apis : { $include : ./config/api.yaml } Create the config directory if needed and add config/api.yaml : config/api.yaml notes : source : kind : file path : ../apis/notes/openapi.yaml focused : true operations : - id : notes.create sourceOperationId : createNote reference : reference.create-note source.path is relative to the config fragment that declares it. notes names this API, and sourceOperationId selects the spec's operationId . The stable operation ID notes.create connects the operation to authored pages; reference names the page that will present it. focused: true publishes a one-operation contract . If the source lives at a public HTTPS URL, import it into a local snapshot first: node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" api import https://api.example.com/openapi.yaml --output apis/remote Point source.path at ../apis/remote/openapi.yaml from config/api.yaml . Commit the snapshot and its source-lock.json . Normal builds use those local files and make no network request. To check for upstream changes, run api refresh apis/remote --output apis/remote-next . If the source changed, the command reports the changed hashes and writes a complete new snapshot while keeping apis/remote intact. Point source.path to ../apis/remote-next/openapi.yaml , inspect a new api review candidate, and pin its digest before building. The CLI reference lists import limits. Author the reference page Create content/create-note.mdx : content/create-note.mdx --- id : reference.create-note title : Create a note summary : Create a note in the fictional Notes API. type : api-reference slug : /example-api/create-note channel : production version : current language : en operations : [ notes.create ] access : { policy : public } --- This fictional operation returns the identifier of a new note. Its response schema and named example are generated from the local OpenAPI file. The page ID must match the registry's reference value. An api-reference page lists exactly one operation. The compiler appends the method, path, parameters, authentication, schemas, and examples to your authored introduction. Append this entry to the existing navigation array in docs.config.yaml : - id : notes-create doc : reference.create-note If your project includes navigation from another file, add the entry there. Save the page and navigation before the review so the candidate contains the page you intend to publish. Review imported content before publishing Shoalrun requires publicReview.digest for every API whose content appears in a public page, embed, or focused contract. A missing or stale digest stops a normal build. Generate a local candidate in a fresh temporary directory: API_REVIEW_DIR = "$( mktemp -d /tmp/shoalrun-api-review.XXXXXX )" node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" api review docs.config.yaml --output "$API_REVIEW_DIR" The command builds the candidate and reports each API's digest, page URLs, focused contracts, full-source downloads, and input hashes. Inspect the candidate files for private operations, fields, descriptions, examples, and credentials. For this example, check the Create a note HTML and Markdown page and its linked focused contract. Copy the reported digest for notes into config/api.yaml alongside source and operations : notes : publicReview : digest : <paste-the-reported-notes-digest> # Keep source and operations here. Replace the angle-bracket placeholder with the actual digest. Keep the candidate local and remove it after review. The digest records what you reviewed; it does not determine whether content is safe. Changing source bytes, selected operations or embeds, focused contracts, or full-source publication requires another review. Changing only authored page copy does not. Build and verify the output node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" bui

documents.title: Audit a docs project
documents.summary: Run project tests and local API representation checks with one CI command.
documents.text: Run shoalrun audit from a project directory before publishing. The command combines tests that your project configures with Shoalrun's build and API representation checks. It reports each result as JSON and exits with code 1 if any result fails. From framework/ , this example needs no extra setup after npm run build : node dist/cli.js audit example/docs.config.yaml With no audit setting, Shoalrun runs the API source and focused-contract audits and builds the site. No project test commands run until you configure them. Check before pushing Run this from your docs project: shoalrun check shoalrun check docs.config.yaml --json The first command discovers docs.config.yaml in the current directory or a parent and prints PASS/FAIL results. Use --json for a structured report in CI. A failed check exits with code 1. shoalrun audit runs the same checks and retains its JSON output. Checks include configured test commands, local OpenAPI sources, a complete temporary build, focused contracts, and local links. The build validates config, frontmatter, and supported MDX. YAML duplicate keys, excessive alias expansion, and cyclic aliases fail with a source-file diagnostic. OpenAPI inputs must declare a supported 3.0 or 3.1 version, an info title and version, and mapping-shaped paths. Link checks inspect generated HTML and Markdown. They verify local destinations and HTML fragments, including same-origin absolute links. Markdown fragments are not checked because heading rules vary between readers. Links in code samples are ignored. Built-in checks need no browser or running server and do not fetch external URLs. Existing site output is preserved; normal generated metadata can still be written under .shoalrun/ . Add a package script to make the check easy to run: { "scripts" : { "docs:check" : "shoalrun check docs.config.yaml" } } An optional Git pre-push hook can run that script. Put these lines in .git/hooks/pre-push and make it executable with chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push : #!/bin/sh exec npm run docs:check The CLI does not install hooks. Configured test commands can perform their own network requests or writes. To include a dependency check for a project with a package lock, configure: audit : tests : - id : dependencies run : [ npm , audit , --omit=dev ] This optional command contacts the npm registry. Omit --omit=dev to include development dependencies. Commands run beside the docs config; use npm's --prefix option when the package lives elsewhere. Add project tests Add audit to docs.config.yaml . This example assumes your project has a scripts/docs.test.mjs file that Node's test runner can execute: docs.config.yaml audit : tests : - id : project-tests run : [ node , --test , scripts/docs.test.mjs ] api : true focusedContracts : true links : true Each test has a unique lowercase id (letters, digits, and hyphens) and a nonempty run list of strings. Shoalrun starts the executable in the first item and passes the rest as arguments. It does not invoke a shell, so shell operators, pipes, and redirection do not work in run . Tests run in list order from the directory containing the config file. They run before API audits and the build. A failing test does not stop the other tests or audits. Each test has a two minute timeout. Shoalrun captures its output and includes the last 16,000 characters in a failure finding. Successful test output is omitted from the report. Because the commands are executable code, review test entries before running an unfamiliar project. Set audit.api: false to skip local OpenAPI source audits, or audit.focusedContracts: false to skip focused-contract checks. Set audit.links: false to skip local link checks. All three default to true ; the build always runs. Connect a documentation test suite audit.tests is the hookup for an external test suite. We recommend Doc Detective for testing documentation behavior, but you can run any installed command that exits nonzero on failure. Shoalrun passes the arguments and records the process exit status; the tool owns its test specifications, fixtures, assertions, and detailed results. For a project with Doc Detective installed locally and its configuration in .doc-detective.json beside docs.config.yaml : docs.config.yaml audit : tests : - id : doc-detective run : [ npx , --no-install , doc-detective , --config , .doc-detective.json , --exit-on-fail ] The --exit-on-fail flag matters: Doc Detective's standalone CLI otherwise can exit successfully when a test fails . npx --no-install uses the locally installed package without downloading one during the audit. Configure tests and report artifacts with Doc Detective. Shoalrun's audit report only records the command's success or failure and the end of its output on failure. To use another suite, replace the run list with its command and failure-exit option. Configured test commands run before Shoalrun's temporary site build. If a tool needs a built or deployed site, run it as a separate step after building or deployin

documents.title: Authoring tools for your coding agent
documents.summary: Understand project discovery, working-tree editing, snapshot validation, and human review.
documents.text: Shoalrun supplies documentation tools for existing coding agents. Your agent supplies its model, file editing, repository exploration, and execution permissions. Shoalrun supplies canonical writing guidance, templates, project discovery, and checks. The tools make no authoring provider calls. Discover before editing Project discovery works without selecting a page. It lists pages, configured guidance, templates, navigation, relationships, and findings. Topic searches help your agent find candidates across the project. Source reads return bounded passages and file digests. Bundled documentation search and reads explain framework behavior; your project's guidance governs local conventions. Edit and check The default is to edit ordinary working-tree files using your agent's file tools. A baseline records the current files, including earlier local changes. Snapshot validation captures those files and compiles a separate copy, so checking a draft does not rewrite the project. Results identify affected pages, findings, skipped checks, and retained artifacts. A freshness check tells you whether those results still apply after further edits. Existing checked plan/apply commands remain available for clients that need them. Their digest checks and application protections are preserved. Review and release Compiler checks establish structural validity. They do not establish factual accuracy, clear writing, or a successful reader task. Review the diff, supporting evidence, and rendered documentation before using your project's release process. Local previews serve the exact captured build and show its freshness. Review reports list task scope, affected HTML/Markdown, findings, checks, and dependencies. The portable authoring skill guides this working-tree workflow. Independent author trials remain a separate release gate. No public package release is claimed here. Related reading Next steps Check working-tree documentation edits — Discover the project and check a working-tree edit. (Status: experimental.) Reference while working Authoring tools commands — Look up discovery, baseline, validation, and freshness commands. (Status: experimental.) Design a writing guide — Give both people and models useful project writing guidance. Go deeper How snapshot validation works — Understand capture coverage, checks, artifacts, and freshness. (Status: experimental.)

documents.title: How snapshot validation works
documents.summary: Understand captured files, affected-page coverage, freshness, and validation limits.
documents.text: Snapshot validation checks a captured working tree. Your existing coding agent edits files; Shoalrun records and checks the resulting state. Baselines and captures A baseline records source paths, modes, and digests before a task. It includes preexisting dirty and untracked files. Validation compares with that baseline, or uses explicit file and page selectors, to identify affected pages. Configuration, dependency, and deletion changes can expand coverage to all authored pages. The capture excludes generated output, dependencies, repository metadata, credentials, and private archives. Files must fit capture limits. Symlinks and absolute dependency references are rejected. Declared sibling dependencies can be captured within the project's parent directory. Capture races produce a failure rather than an apparently current result. Checks and artifacts The compiler renders affected drafts in the captured project while preserving their publication access metadata. It checks metadata, identities, routes, components, navigation, relationships, and document links. Local HTML and Markdown links and configured API contracts are checked in the captured output. External URLs are not requested. Configured shell checks are skipped by default. With --run-checks , trusted project commands run inside the capture under the harness's permissions. This is not an operating-system sandbox; scripts can still access absolute paths or services. Model evaluators are skipped. Executable metadata and highlighting extensions are currently unavailable to snapshot validation. The result retains the captured project, built site, and JSON report. Remove the reported artifact directory when finished. Compiler success does not replace factual and editorial review. Freshness and scope The report identifies the snapshot and source digests. docs validation-status compares current inputs with the report and returns stale when they differ. A report only applies to its recorded coverage and checks. Review skipped and unavailable checks before accepting a result. Snapshot validation does not apply edits, start a preview server, commit, or publish. Existing checked plan/apply clients retain their own review and freshness protections. Matching previews and review reports docs review reads a retained validation report as JSON or Markdown. It associates changed-file operations and digests with the declared baseline and exposes findings, check status, affected routes, dependencies, and artifacts. Baselines retain digests rather than earlier contents, so your harness must retain the task diff. Evidence, semantic review, and author decisions are not inferred by these tools. docs preview makes a separate private copy of the validated site and starts a foreground loopback server. Every affected rendered page has HTML and Markdown URLs. HTML pages link to a browser review and display freshness; the original Markdown output remains unchanged. Replacing source files does not replace the preview's content. Replacing the report makes its pinned preview stale. Artifact changes prevent startup or stop page serving. After editing, validate again and restart from the new report. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM closes the server and removes only its serving copy. Retained validation artifacts have a separate lifecycle. The preview starts no source watcher or provider requests. Related reading Next steps Check working-tree documentation edits — Capture a baseline and validate a working-tree edit. (Status: experimental.) Reference while working Authoring tools commands — Find commands for discovery and snapshot validation. (Status: experimental.)

headings.title: Read the page and its owners

documents.text: Use this optional workflow when your agent needs a digest-checked replacement plan before writing files. Your agent gathers evidence and writes the candidate; Shoalrun validates and applies the exact plan. For ordinary working-tree editing, follow Check working-tree documentation edits instead. Prepare and apply an update Read the page and its owners shoalrun docs context guide.welcome --config docs.config.yaml Read the returned source files and the project's writing guide. Capture the source digest before drafting. Give your agent the requested change and supporting sources; those can include other repositories, specifications, or links it can inspect with its own tools. Write and review a candidate Have the agent save a complete replacement file separately from the source. Preserve stable IDs, routes, publication fields, and access policy. Update the edit date. Ask for a diff, the evidence supporting changed claims, and any unresolved questions. Run the project's Vale rules and verify code examples. Create an exact edit plan Create edit-request.json with full replacement text and the digest of the source used to draft it: { "edits" : [ { "file" : "content/welcome.mdx" , "baseDigest" : "<SHA-256 digest of the original source>" , "content" : "<complete replacement file>" } ] } The placeholders above must be replaced with actual values. Paths are relative to the project configuration directory. shoalrun docs plan --request-file edit-request.json --out edit-plan.json --config docs.config.yaml shoalrun docs apply edit-plan.json --config docs.config.yaml --check The check builds a temporary copy and leaves source files unchanged. A stale source or failed build stops the edit. Plans support existing authored Markdown files and YAML files loaded by the configuration; use scaffolding for new files. Apply the reviewed plan shoalrun docs apply edit-plan.json --config docs.config.yaml shoalrun audit docs.config.yaml Applying repeats freshness and build checks before writing. Inspect the resulting HTML and Markdown. The plan does not run configured audit tests, commit changes, or deploy; those are separate steps. What checks establish Compiler checks catch problems such as broken document links and invalid components. Vale checks the rules your team configures. Neither establishes factual accuracy or whether a procedure works. Ask your agent to explain what it verified and what still needs review. Ordinary public builds exclude draft pages. Use the separate working-tree docs validate interface to render affected drafts in isolation without changing their authored access policy. This does not change the checked plan/apply contract described above. Related reading Read first Templates — Scaffold a draft page before an agent writes its content. Reference while working Add an OpenAPI API — Review a drafted API page against its operation and contract. Example writing guide — Review this site's example editorial guidance. Related topics Use the bundled agent skills — Let an agent run the same draft, check, and apply loop. Write with agents — Start with the agent authoring workflow. Check working-tree documentation edits — Use the checked edit commands with your existing coding agent. (Status: experimental.) Use your coding agent — Prepare a checked edit to an existing page.

documents.title: Authoring tools commands
documents.summary: Look up provider-free project discovery, reference reads, baselines, and snapshot validation.
documents.text: These commands are available through the private prototype's CLI. They make no authoring provider calls. Discovery and references Use these commands to find the project and retrieve the references needed for an edit. Command Result docs project Project-wide JSON discovery, without requiring a page selector. docs source FILE Bounded project-relative source passage with a whole-file digest. docs search QUERY --json Search bundled framework documentation. docs read ID --json Read a bundled reference by stable ID. Project commands accept --config FILE ; otherwise they find the nearest docs.config.yaml in the current directory or its ancestors. Project sections are pages , guidance , configuration , navigation , relationships , templates , and findings . Choose a section with --section . Pages, navigation, and relationships accept one of --id , --file , or --query . Project pagination uses --offset and --limit (default 20, maximum 100). Follow the returned pagination.nextOffset . --max-tokens bounds the response (default 8192). Source reads use Unicode code-point offsets and default to 4096 tokens; follow nextOffset and verify the digest between reads. Paths must resolve inside the project. Use your harness's tools and permissions for external implementation sources. Validation Use these checks to find source and publication problems before reviewing the result. Command Result docs baseline --out FILE Record the current working tree without running checks. The destination must be new. docs validate --baseline FILE Validate changes since a task baseline in a separate capture. docs validate --file FILE Validate declared file changes; repeat the selector for more files. docs validate --id ID Validate declared pages; repeat the selector for more IDs. docs validation-status REPORT Check whether a retained report still applies to current inputs. Baselines and validation artifacts must be outside the project or inside its excluded .shoalrun directory. --artifacts DIRECTORY selects a new artifact directory; otherwise validation retains a temporary directory. Results contain actual report, capture, and site locations. --run-checks opts into configured trusted shell checks under the harness's permissions; evaluator hooks remain skipped. Declare sibling files and directories needed by a configured check in audit.tests[].inputs . Paths are relative to the project configuration directory and must remain within its parent. Snapshot builds resolve revision dates without writing freshness history. A configured check that changes captured source or history still fails validation. Configured Node checks receive Shoalrun's installed dependency search paths through NODE_PATH for CommonJS resolution. Consumer dependencies are not copied into the snapshot; missing modules produce an unavailable check. ESM imports do not use NODE_PATH . Validation statuses include ok , failed , incomplete , unavailable , and stale . Read findings and coverage alongside status. These commands always return JSON. Snapshot validation requires affected page IDs to match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]* . Review and preview Use these commands to inspect proposed changes and their rendered output. Command Result docs review REPORT JSON review for a retained validation report. docs review REPORT --format markdown A readable report for the same snapshot and task scope. docs preview REPORT --port PORT Foreground local preview of that exact build, with a browser review page. REPORT is the validation report path returned by docs validate . Review accepts --format json or --format markdown ; JSON is the default. It exits 0 only for a current ok result. An error returns the existing JSON failure envelope, even when Markdown was requested. Preview binds only to 127.0.0.1 ; the default port is 8771. Use port 0 to allocate a free port. Its JSON startup record contains the snapshot ID, origin, and review/status URLs. It also includes affected HTML/Markdown URLs, serving-copy directory, validation review, and lifecycle instructions. The process stays running. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM closes it, removes its private copy, and emits a stopped record. Validation artifacts remain. No browser is opened automatically. The review identifies the baseline, changed-file operations and digests, dependencies, and current freshness. It includes checks, findings and source/reference locations, coverage, and affected-page artifacts. Earlier file contents are not retained in a baseline; the report explains why it cannot generate a task diff. Evidence gathering remains with the harness. Reviewer results and author dispositions are explicitly empty; no semantic reviewer ran. Configuration, dependency, and deletion changes conservatively list every rendered page, including generated API operations. Authored-only changes list their affected pages. Each page reports its authored or generated origin. A stale working tree can still be previewed as a clearly labelled historical snapshot. Modified or missin

documents.title: Check working-tree documentation edits
documents.summary: Discover a project, capture a baseline, edit files, and validate an isolated copy.
documents.text: Use this procedure from a project containing docs.config.yaml , with the checkout-built Shoalrun CLI available. The package is still a private prototype. Replace the example page path with your project's path. Your coding agent uses its own model and file tools. Read project guidance shoalrun docs project --section guidance --config docs.config.yaml shoalrun docs project --query "installation" --config docs.config.yaml shoalrun docs source AGENTS.md --config docs.config.yaml shoalrun docs search "page metadata" --json shoalrun docs read guide.frontmatter --json Read applicable instructions and reviewed examples before editing. Discovery works without a selected page. Inspect the findings section when discovery reports findings; follow pagination when a section exceeds its response budget. Record the starting files shoalrun docs baseline --out .shoalrun/task-baseline.json --config docs.config.yaml Choose a new baseline filename for each task. The baseline includes earlier local edits and untracked files; it compares later changes with this starting state rather than Git HEAD. It runs no checks. Edit and validate Edit ordinary MDX and configuration files using your agent's file tools. Preserve unrelated edits and review changes to identity, navigation, relationships, and publication metadata. shoalrun docs validate --baseline .shoalrun/task-baseline.json --config docs.config.yaml For an existing edit without a baseline, declare its scope explicitly: shoalrun docs validate --file content/install.mdx --config docs.config.yaml Validation compiles a separate capture. Read the returned status, coverage, findings, skipped checks, and artifact paths. A failure needs correction and another validation. An incomplete or unavailable result needs investigation; it is not a passing result. Configured shell checks require explicit --run-checks and your harness's execution authorization. Confirm the result still applies shoalrun docs validation-status /path/from/result/report.json Use the actual report path returned by validation. A stale result requires another validation. Review and preview the snapshot shoalrun docs review /path/from/result/report.json --format markdown shoalrun docs preview /path/from/result/report.json --port 8771 The preview command stays running and returns a local review URL plus HTML and Markdown URLs for every affected page that rendered. Open the review URL in your browser. It shows the task baseline, changed files, checks, findings, dependencies, and artifacts. Previewing a failed or incomplete result does not make it pass. A failed compile can leave no site to preview; read its findings with docs review first. The server uses a private copy of the captured build. Each HTML page shows the snapshot status and a link back to the review. Source changes make that preview stale; the displayed content remains the captured version. A baseline contains digests rather than earlier file contents, so retain the task diff with your harness. The report does not attribute all dirty files to your task. After a revision, stop the preview with Ctrl-C, validate again, and start a preview using the new report path. The server never watches or rebuilds source. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM removes its private serving copy; the validation artifacts remain. Remove only the reported validation artifact directory when finished. A forced process kill can leave the serving copy behind; its path is in the startup result. Review facts, examples, supporting sources, and the task diff before accepting the edit. Use your normal review and publication process afterward. Related reading Read first Authoring tools for your coding agent — Understand how your coding agent uses Shoalrun tools and human review. (Status: experimental.) Reference while working Authoring tools commands — Look up discovery and snapshot validation commands. (Status: experimental.) Example writing guide — Review the example guidance before approving a writing plan. Related topics Apply a checked edit plan — Use the checked edit commands with your existing coding agent. (Status: experimental.)

documents.title: Cards and collections
documents.summary: Link to documents by stable ID and build filtered card collections.
documents.text: A card is a linked preview of another documentation page: it shows a title and short preview so readers can decide where to go next. Cards use the target page's title, the project's configured outputs.text.card field, and its current URL. The target is the page the reader will open when they select the card. Authors maintain those details in the target page's frontmatter, the YAML metadata at the top of the file. A card references the page's stable id , so renaming its file or changing its URL does not break the card. HTML displays a card layout; Markdown displays the same links, descriptions, subject lifecycle status, and relationship reasons as a readable list. Use these components as standalone, empty blocks in .md or .mdx pages or registered snippets. Literal attributes are accepted; arbitrary JavaScript expressions are not evaluated. Link to one document < DocCard doc = "guide.frontmatter" /> Page metadata Set page identity, publication, and presentation fields before publishing. The target must be public and available in the current publication: the channel, API version, and language of the page displaying the card. An unknown, draft, or unavailable target stops the build with a diagnostic. There is no automatic fallback to another publication. Curate a reading list Use a curated list when you want to choose exactly which pages readers see and in what order. DocCards displays one card for each document ID you supply. For example, this list offers the content guide followed by the templates guide: < DocCards docs = {[ "guide.content-identity" , "guide.templates" ]} /> Content and stable IDs Give each page a durable identity and publish explicit variants. Templates Create and edit page starting points, then scaffold drafts from them. The array controls the order. Duplicate IDs fail validation. An empty array renders “No matching documents.” Set empty="Your message" to replace that text. Add an ordinary Markdown heading before a card group when it needs a section title. Cards themselves use list and link semantics rather than inserting heading levels. DocCards can also show cards from a declared relationship. Supply either docs or relation : < DocCards relation = "next-step" relatedTo = "guide.cards" /> Attribute Required Meaning docs For a curated list Literal array of unique document IDs in display order. relation For relationship cards One declared relationship type; cannot be combined with docs . relatedTo No Source document for relation ; defaults to this page. empty No Message for no results; default is “No matching documents.” Use RelatedReading when a plain link list grouped by purpose fits better than cards. Override card text By default, a card shows the target page's title and summary . These are the resolved values after global defaults, page frontmatter, and enforced values have been applied. Add an optional card object to the target page's frontmatter when its card needs different wording. An eyebrow is a short label above the card title, such as “Integration guide” or “Tutorial.” It helps readers recognize the kind of content before reading the title. It is optional display text; it does not set the document's type, add a tag, or affect collection filters. In this example, “Integration guide” appears above “Send your first payment”: title : Create a payment summary : Submit a payment and understand the result. card : icon : credit-card title : Send your first payment description : Prepare the request and inspect the response. eyebrow : Integration guide Field What it displays When omitted card.title The linked heading inside the card. Uses the document title . card.description A short explanation of what the reader will find. Uses outputs.text.card , which defaults to the document summary . card.eyebrow A small label above the title. No label. card.icon A decorative Lucide symbol above the text. No icon, unless inherited from global frontmatter. These overrides affect cards only. The page heading, SEO, and navigation keep their existing values. A card's destination always comes from the stable ID; href overrides are not supported. Values must be nonempty strings. Images, arbitrary badges, and other card fields are not implemented and fail with a diagnostic. Subject lifecycle status comes from the target document, including authoritative OpenAPI deprecation. Add a Lucide icon Choose an icon from the Lucide icon browser and put its lowercase name on the target page: card : icon : book-open Names use hyphens, such as book-open , credit-card , terminal , or sliders-horizontal . The pinned Lucide package supplies the icons at build time. An unknown name or URL fails with a file-specific diagnostic, so typos never silently produce an empty icon. New icons from a later Lucide release need a dependency update first. The icon appears in every card for that page, including curated lists, collections, and relationship views. It does not change the page heading or sidebar. Omit card.ico

documents.title: API reference styling lab
documents.summary: Inspect a synthetic API with complex schemas, filters, response formats, and webhooks.
documents.text: Fictional API example. This page demonstrates documentation features; its operations do not describe a live service. The Cedar Parcel API is fictional. Its .example hosts do not accept requests, and its OpenAPI examples have not been executed. We keep it in the Shoalrun docs to check API reference layouts alongside other pages. It uses the same navigation, search, themes, and Markdown output. Use these pages to inspect the hardest layouts: Create a parcel enrollment shows four named request shapes with overlapping nested objects and required fields. In Bulk dispatch , monthlyParcelEstimate demonstrates an exclusive lower bound and schema-level examples, while customMetadata accepts any JSON value. List parcel records shows direct query filters, three response formats, and the new object, array, and number constraints: minProperties , maxProperties , uniqueItems , and multipleOf . Get a parcel uses a path-specific server and no authentication. Upload a manifest requires two binary upload fields. Get a parcel through the old route shows OpenAPI deprecation overriding an extension value. Parcel delivered event shows an inbound OpenAPI 3.1 webhook with a nested oneOf proof. The source and standalone test project live at framework/example-configs/reference-stress/ in the repository. The source is not copied into the built site; each operation publishes only its focused contract. How it works for agents Every operation has a complete .md page and a focused OpenAPI contract. Schema fields remain in Markdown even when their HTML disclosure is closed. The site manifest and search index include these pages, and the reader's theme choice does not change what an agent can read.

It uses the same navigation, search, themes, and Markdown output. Use these pages to inspect the hardest layouts: Create a parcel enrollment shows four named request shapes with overlapping nested objects and required fields. In Bulk dispatch , monthlyParcelEstimate demonstrates an exclusive lower bound and schema-level examples, while customMetadata accepts any JSON value. List parcel records shows direct query filters, three response formats, and the new object, array, and number constraints: minProperties , maxProperties , uniqueItems , and multipleOf . Get a parcel uses a path-specific server and no authentication. Upload a manifest requires two binary upload fields. Get a parcel through the old route shows OpenAPI deprecation overriding an extension value. Parcel delivered event shows an inbound OpenAPI 3.1 webhook with a nested oneOf proof. The source and standalone test project live at framework/example-configs/reference-stress/ in the repository. The source is not copied into the built site; each operation publishes only its focused contract. How it works for agents Every operation has a complete .md page and a focused OpenAPI contract. Schema fields remain in Markdown even when their HTML disclosure is closed. The site manifest and search index include these pages, and the reader's theme choice does not change what an agent can read.

documents.title: Agent discovery, verified Markdown, and incremental sync
documents.summary: Find the right page with less context, verify its contents, and fetch only what changed.
documents.text: Agents can now find pages through smaller indexes, check which build they are reading, and compare saved page inventories before fetching updates. Smaller discovery files. llms.min.txt lists page IDs, titles, summaries, and Markdown links. search-index.min.json adds headings without article text. Markdown 404 responses point to these compact files. Incremental sync. Clients can check build-info.json for a new build, then compare documents.sync.json with their saved snapshot to find added, changed, and removed pages. They can fetch only the pages that need updating instead of downloading the full manifest and every page again. shoalrun docs changes CURRENT-SNAPSHOT --since PREVIOUS-SNAPSHOT performs the comparison locally. Verifiable responses. Markdown responses include a fingerprint that lets clients check whether a page changed without downloading it again, plus a link to its manifest record. Focused API contracts now use their actual content digest in the URL, allowing a one-year immutable cache policy. Clearer examples. Fictional pages carry a machine-readable demo flag. The refreshed agent-friendly guide puts working tabs, a disclosure, and reader choices beside the Markdown an agent receives. Try the example and see what an agent reads . The output reference covers the files, digests, and sync workflow.
