documents.title: Agent reading and evaluation
documents.summary: Smaller Markdown reads, clearer lifecycle and change guidance, and exact-output evaluation comparisons.

headings.title: Keep reading paths in section Markdown

documents.text: This entry combines the October 15 changes to the private prototype. It does not announce a package release or a verified deployment. Compare evaluation builds Evaluation reports can now identify which published files changed. New report templates include a file inventory; eval check lists additions, edits, and removals when the evaluated build differs from the current output. Use shoalrun eval snapshot to save an inventory and shoalrun eval compare to compare builds. The check still requires the exact evaluated output. Copying a build to another machine preserves its identity; rebuilding it may produce different bytes. The repository can also capture hosted builds with their tasks and an ungraded report template for later review. Capturing a build does not run the tasks or award a passing grade. The packaged Markdown bundle also stops carrying a whole-site build ID for assets it does not include. Its page digests and metadata remain intact. Evaluate agent tasks against your docs explains the workflow and its limits. Find and read Markdown The manifest and compact search index now expose exact published Markdown byte counts and cl100k_base token counts. Copy as Markdown copies the full published twin, with an accessible status and a plain link fallback. See Markdown metadata and agent discovery . Pages now publish complete Markdown resources for top-level sections, with outlines, exact sizes, and parent/section digests. Use docs outline and docs section , or MCP get_outline and get_section , to retrieve them. Nested reader content stays together. Generated section IDs can change when headings change; see section identity and citations . Search now returns the exact next read call and a direct Markdown URL, with a full-page fallback. Section files are limited to longer pages and must halve both bytes and tokens; short pages no longer produce redundant section files. Compact search records expose eligible section URLs without requiring the full manifest. Search now recommends a smaller section only when the author explicitly lists its heading in standaloneSections ; otherwise the next read fetches the full page. This addresses an observed case where a matching section omitted prerequisite configuration. Declarations are author judgments, not compiler verification of completeness. CLI/MCP search now allows a stronger match missing one meaningful query term to outrank complete matches found only in body text. Complete matches with relevant titles, summaries, or headings keep their preference. Page-title matching also accepts simple final- s query plurals against singular titles. These changes fix an observed discovery miss without project-specific synonyms; browser search is unchanged. See search ranking . For partial CLI/MCP matches, a focused subject match can now outrank a result with one extra incidental term. Only candidates within one meaningful term of the best coverage and at least two matched terms receive this ordering. Sparse matches stay below that group. This corrects an observed MCP client setup query while preserving full-page reads for setup and budget instructions. Fetch-only agents can now reach approved section resources from the small text index. The HTML discovery block opens /llms.min.txt , which lists full pages and author-declared standalone sections with exact sizes and explicit full-page fallbacks. Publication labels distinguish editions. No JSON parsing, CLI or MCP is needed for that reading path; the detailed index remains available. HTML metadata and Markdown page backlinks now point to the same compact index as the visible agent guidance. The full index remains available from that list. The diagram reference also includes complete D2 and Mermaid authoring examples with intact nested code fences. These small private-prototype changes address discovery detours and missing copyable syntax observed during fetch-only evaluations. Follow deprecation and migration guidance This private prototype update adds subjectDeprecation to page metadata. Authors can supply deprecation and sunset dates, a replacement document ID, and a migration guide ID for a deprecated API or feature. Readers see the same guidance in HTML, full-page Markdown, and published section resources. Fetch-only agents can follow the Markdown links directly. The document manifest also exposes the dates and resolved targets. Builds reject invalid dates and references outside the current publication. The guidance describes the documented subject. It does not remove the documentation page or emit HTTP retirement headers. Dates are author declarations, not evidence that a service has retired. See page metadata for syntax and validation rules. Keep reading paths in section Markdown This private prototype update preserves reading guidance when an agent fetches one section of a longer page. Prerequisites and next steps from top-level, current-page RelatedReading views now travel with the section, including the reason to follow each

documents.title: Authoring snapshot previews and review reports
documents.summary: Review affected pages, findings, coverage, and freshness beside an exact snapshot preview.
documents.text: This change concerns the private prototype; no package release or deployment is claimed. docs review REPORT presents a validated snapshot as JSON or Markdown. It identifies the task baseline, changed files and dependencies, findings, check coverage, and affected HTML/Markdown artifacts. Baselines contain digests rather than earlier contents; retain the task diff with your existing harness. docs preview REPORT serves a private copy of that exact build on a loopback address. It returns a browser review URL and routes for every affected page that rendered. HTML pages display freshness and a review link. Source edits make the preview stale rather than replacing its content; validate again and restart from the new report. Changed artifacts prevent startup or serving. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM closes the foreground server and removes its serving copy. Validation artifacts remain available separately. Failed or skipped checks retain their actual status while previewing. The tools make no authoring provider calls and do not apply edits, commit, or publish. Snapshot builds preserve captured freshness history. Configured checks can declare sibling files and directories with audit.tests[].inputs ; validation captures those inputs and tracks their changes. Compiler checks do not replace factual or editorial review. Related reading Next steps Check working-tree documentation edits — Validate working-tree edits and open the matching snapshot review. (Status: experimental.) Reference while working Authoring tools commands — Look up review formats, preview lifecycle, statuses, and limits. (Status: experimental.)

documents.title: MCP hosting, analytics, and component improvements
documents.summary: Serve documentation tools, measure MCP calls, and build custom components with shared HTML and Markdown content.
documents.text: This entry groups the October 17 changes to Shoalrun’s private prototype. It does not announce a package release. Serve documentation tools over HTTP Projects can enable an MCP endpoint for one explicitly public publication. It exposes the existing read-only search, page, outline, and section tools through the Node server. The Vercel build can package an independent function without Ask, embeddings, or a model key. Read-only SDK calls have also been verified on this site’s production Vercel endpoint. The endpoint uses a scoped, byte-verified copy of published Markdown and indexes. Search works independently of browser search settings. Host and origin checks, request limits, deadlines, and publication checks apply before serving documentation. Stdio remains available. See connect an MCP client for configuration, limits, and when MCP helps alongside public Markdown. Measure MCP tool calls An optional mcp.analytics.module server adapter receives tool outcomes, duration, build/publication identity, and published page or section IDs. Analytics is off by default. The adapter is separate from browser analytics and runs on the serving host. The PostHog example emits native MCP events and flushes before the HTTP response completes. Separate opt-ins add supported client/model labels, agent intent, and conversation grouping. Labels are unverified. Intent is limited to fixed categories; free text is replaced before delivery. Unknown model labels are omitted. The example excludes raw queries, complete arguments, results, headers, and exception bodies from outbound events. GeoIP enrichment and person profiles are disabled; session grouping remains pseudonymous. See measure MCP tool usage for the adapter contract, privacy limits, and setup steps. Other services can use the same server adapter interface. Render Mermaid syntax with Pele Pele replaces Mermaid CLI for Mermaid-syntax diagrams. Diagram builds no longer launch Chrome, and production package installs no longer include Puppeteer. Browser development tests still use it. Inline diagrams follow the site’s palette and color mode, support per-diagram width caps, and retain source and summaries in Markdown. Use native Pele CSS variables to override the default theme mapping. The Pele gallery shows the built-in families and 48 flowchart shapes. The D2 gallery adds 17 examples covering shapes, containers, sequence diagrams, tables, classes, and layout engines. Both galleries include source examples you can copy. More interactive documentation components File trees now have expandable folders, keyboard navigation, and optional expand-all controls. Collapsible groups keep related disclosures in one compact stack while allowing multiple items to stay open. Tabs can synchronize matching choices across related examples on a page. Images support captions and an optional expanded viewer; width is optional. The viewer supports keyboard dismissal and returns focus to the image link. Markdown retains all tree nodes, disclosure bodies, tab alternatives, image descriptions, and captions. Native disclosures and original-image links remain useful without JavaScript. Build custom components Projects can register trusted custom components from local files or installed packages through one component manifest. Each component implements a required content() function using shared content helpers. Shoalrun renders that content as HTML and Markdown, including links, search content, and section resources. Attribute and child validation report authoring errors during the build. Optional browser modules add interactive controls, including React, with explicit data from the same content function. Shoalrun bundles imports and JSX, publishes browser assets, and tracks dependencies for rebuilds and isolated authoring validation. Shared documentation remains readable without JavaScript. Configured component code is trusted; arbitrary MDX imports and React page rendering remain outside this API. The bundled shoalrun-component-author skill guides agents through the component contract, implementation, and focused validation.

documents.title: Navigation, page layouts, and browser analytics
documents.summary: Navigation sections, reader controls, page layouts, and optional browser interaction analytics.
documents.text: This entry groups the October 16 changes to Shoalrun's private prototype and documentation. It does not announce a package release or a verified deployment. Navigate between sections Top-level navigation groups can now become tabs, each with its own landing page and sidebar. This site uses Docs , Project updates , and Changelog . API documentation and recipes remain in Docs. Tabs use ordinary page links. Direct links select the correct section without a saved browser choice, and navigation works without JavaScript. On smaller screens, a Sections disclosure holds the links. Existing navigation lists continue to work without tabs. Agents receive the same structure through explicit section membership in Markdown, the document manifest, and both search indexes. Each tab has a scoped text index that links to its member pages and back to the global index. The global indexes still list every published page, including shared pages and pages omitted from navigation. The offline agent documentation bundle includes the scoped indexes. See navigation configuration and the published-output contract . Give readers more room Documentation pages keep their table of contents visible at laptop widths. Readers can hide it to widen the article, including paragraphs and code examples, without moving the article's left edge. Restoring the contents restores the original width, and the browser remembers the choice across pages. The navigation uses aligned chevrons, lighter group headings, quieter selection styling, and consistent spacing. Projects can omit group page counts with outputs.html.navigation.showCounts: false ; counts remain visible by default, and filtering works with either setting. Header spacing and title sizing are tighter. The Reef theme keeps equal padding around text and examples, and its Contents control follows the panel's inset. Wide pages retain their wider content area. The reading and navigation changes work across all four themes. Keep entry pages focused Navigation tabs show by default on docs and wide pages and stay hidden on landing and splash pages. Page frontmatter can override that choice with showNavigationTabs: true or false . This site's splash homepage hides the tab bar. Pages led by a Hero omit the page-level Markdown action row. Markdown twins and discovery links remain available. Hiding the tab bar changes only its HTML presentation; section membership and agent indexes remain intact. See page layouts . Measure browser interactions Projects can now connect browser analytics through the top-level analytics.module setting. Shoalrun supplies versioned events for navigation, content tabs, disclosures, clipboard successes, search outcomes, and reader selections. Events include stable page IDs and publication context. Site scripts can emit additional events through the same hook. The browser adapter owns service initialization, consent, and delivery. Analytics is off by default, and disabled builds omit its runtime and adapter. SDK failures do not interrupt the site. Browser instrumentation leaves Markdown and agent discovery unchanged; agent request measurements belong at the host or server. See bring your own analytics . Add contributor documentation Repository contributors now have a separate maintainer guide covering architecture, development, validation, hosting, and release work. It is separate from the public documentation and packaged agent bundle. Related reading Reference while working Organize site navigation — Configure navigation tabs, landing pages, and optional group counts. Publishing and agent representations — Inspect section membership and scoped text indexes for agents. Page layouts, landing pages, and splash pages — Choose a page layout and control whether its tab bar appears. Bring your own analytics — Connect your analytics service to documented browser interaction events. Related topics Project status — Check the private prototype's capabilities and remaining release limits.

Projects can omit group page counts with outputs.html.navigation.showCounts: false ; counts remain visible by default, and filtering works with either setting. Header spacing and title sizing are tighter. The Reef theme keeps equal padding around text and examples, and its Contents control follows the panel's inset. Wide pages retain their wider content area. The reading and navigation changes work across all four themes. Keep entry pages focused Navigation tabs show by default on docs and wide pages and stay hidden on landing and splash pages. Page frontmatter can override that choice with showNavigationTabs: true or false . This site's splash homepage hides the tab bar. Pages led by a Hero omit the page-level Markdown action row. Markdown twins and discovery links remain available. Hiding the tab bar changes only its HTML presentation; section membership and agent indexes remain intact. See page layouts . Measure browser interactions Projects can now connect browser analytics through the top-level analytics.module setting. Shoalrun supplies versioned events for navigation, content tabs, disclosures, clipboard successes, search outcomes, and reader selections. Events include stable page IDs and publication context. Site scripts can emit additional events through the same hook. The browser adapter owns service initialization, consent, and delivery. Analytics is off by default, and disabled builds omit its runtime and adapter. SDK failures do not interrupt the site. Browser instrumentation leaves Markdown and agent discovery unchanged; agent request measurements belong at the host or server. See bring your own analytics . Add contributor documentation Repository contributors now have a separate maintainer guide covering architecture, development, validation, hosting, and release work. It is separate from the public documentation and packaged agent bundle. documents.title: Search results and tooltips
documents.summary: Improve search results with a prepared index and add separate hover and focus tooltips.

headings.title: Show supporting text on hover or focus

documents.text: These October 18 changes improve search and supporting explanations in Shoalrun’s private prototype. This entry does not announce a package release. Find useful search results Search results now select substantive passages instead of generated related-reading lists or source-only fragments. An exact page-title query opens that page’s introduction. Large galleries no longer crowd other pages out of the search candidates. Explicit identifiers and commands remain searchable in code and tables. Matching pages keep their retrieved order. They open the passage containing the exact match, and the result description shows its code line or table row. The passage index prepares result paragraphs, code lines, and table rows during indexing. Search requests no longer parse the Markdown passages to prepare these results. Preparing this data does not change the embedding input, so unchanged passages reuse their existing vectors. Queries such as “charts” and “graphs” lead to chart and diagram examples with readable descriptions. Searching “diagrams” opens the Diagrams guide . Semantic search retains its keyword fallback when embeddings are unavailable; Ask passage retrieval is unchanged. Distinguish short definitions from tooltips The former Tooltips reference is now Short definitions . <InfoHint> keeps its native click-to-expand disclosure, including keyboard and touch support without JavaScript. <Tooltip> previously named the same disclosure. If you used it for click-to-expand definitions, replace it with <InfoHint> to retain that behavior. Show supporting text on hover or focus The separate Tooltip component now shows brief supporting text when readers hover over or focus its label. It works inline or as a standalone block. Readers can move the pointer onto the popup, dismiss it with Escape, or tap the label to open and close it on touch screens. Without JavaScript, the label and explanation remain visible together. Markdown includes the full label and explanation, so agents can read both without interaction. Keep essential warnings and instructions in visible page content.

documents.title: Portable working-tree authoring workflow
documents.summary: Guide existing coding agents through discovery, native editing, validation, and snapshot review.
documents.text: This change concerns the private prototype; no package release or deployment is claimed. The shoalrun-author skill now uses ordinary working-tree edits by default. It guides project discovery, policy and evidence reads, baseline capture, native edits, and required companions. The agent then validates a separate capture and presents its matching HTML/Markdown preview for review. It preserves earlier local edits and keeps task-diff attribution with the harness. Affected drafts render in snapshot validation without changing their access policy. Existing checked plan/apply clients can still choose that workflow explicitly. The authoring guides now distinguish these two paths and remove obsolete instructions to change draft access for a review copy. Give your coding agent the installed skill file and use the public CLI alongside its usual editing tools. No separate authoring service or model configuration is required. documents.title: Check and speed up answers
documents.summary: Understand answer checks, direct excerpts, caching, and the limits of each.
documents.text: Use this page after local chat setup to understand which checks run, which need a scorer, and when Shoalrun can reuse an answer. The settings reference defines the corresponding fields. Citations and code are checked by default. Coverage gating, claim verification, direct excerpts, cards, and caching need their own configuration. None of these checks proves an answer is correct. How an answer is checked The coverage gate runs before generation. The other checks inspect the generated answer. Check What it catches Needs Gate A question the docs don't cover. The model is never called. rerank: jev and gate Citations A citation to a passage the model wasn't given. Always on Code A command or config that isn't in the passages. Always on Claims A sentence that its cited passage doesn't support. rerank: jev and verify Citations The model sees numbered passages and cites them as [1] , [2] . A citation to a number it wasn't given is removed. The rest are renumbered in order of first appearance, so a reader sees [1] , [2] , [3] . An answer with no citation is flagged. Code A line of code must appear in the passages word for word, or every word in it must appear there. That allows a shorter form of a documented example, such as <Table filter> for <Table filter sticky> . It catches an invented flag, subcommand, or config key, and a glued path such as docs.config.yaml.vercel/output , where the model dropped a space. Some differences are allowed. Sample content in a language that illustrates, such as a Mermaid diagram or plain output, isn't checked. A path or file name that a reader would choose, such as content/my-page.mdx , is accepted even when the docs never use it. Inline code may flatten a nested example. Numbers and comments are ignored. The check can't catch the right words in the wrong order. Claims Jev reads each sentence that carries a citation, together with the passage it cites. It scores from 0 to 1 how well the passage supports the sentence. A sentence with no citation of its own uses the citations on its line. Fenced code, lead-ins that end in a colon, and statements that the docs lack something are skipped, because no passage can support an absence. That covers phrasings such as "the docs don't specifically describe", "no other information is given", and "it only shows". A sentence below verify.threshold is flagged in the notes, or removed when onUnsupported is remove . If removal leaves no supported sentence, the answer becomes "The documentation does not cover that." The check costs one more Jev call for each answer. Start with flagging while you review the results. Choose a threshold using questions and source passages from your own project; scores and useful thresholds vary by scorer. Removing sentences can leave an answer incomplete. The claims check can't catch a wrong sentence that a passage loosely supports, or a passage that is itself wrong. It reads only the passage a sentence cites. Answer without a model For a question answered by one passage, chat.direct can show the source text instead of generating an answer. This avoids a chat-model call, but the excerpt is only as accurate as the documentation behind it. docs.config.yaml chat : rerank : jev direct : { threshold : 0.9 , margin : 0.1 , others : 1 } A passage is shown only when all of these are true: Jev scores the best passage at threshold or higher. At most others other passages score within margin of the best. A broad question has many strong passages and needs a model to combine them. It is a question that stands on its own. A follow-up, which needs the conversation to make sense, always goes to the model. Every other question goes to the model as usual. A passage longer than maxChars (default 1,200) is cut to the block that answers the question. The cut keeps the sentence that introduces a code example, or the example that a sentence introduces. If trimming fails, the whole passage is shown. The answer begins with From the docs and the page and section, and the result's decision is excerpt . --no-direct on ask turns the mode off for one run. A higher threshold , a smaller margin , or fewer allowed others produces fewer excerpts and sends more questions to the model. Test both narrow questions and broad how-to questions; one relevant passage may answer only part of a request. Answer ahead of time Some questions are asked so often that they deserve a reviewed answer. An answer card is generated and reviewed ahead of time, then served without a new chat-model answer. Matching still needs a query embedding and scorer confirmation. A card is used only while the passages behind it are unchanged. See Prepared answers to make them. Reuse answers People ask the same questions. With chat.cache , serve --ask keeps recent answers in memory and returns a stored one when the same question comes back, with no model call. The question is compared after ignoring case, extra spaces, and closing punctuation, and separately for each publication a

documents.title: Retrieval and chat settings
documents.summary: Look up embedding, chat-model, scoring, and answer-reuse configuration.
documents.text: Use this reference to look up fields after choosing a setup. For a working sequence, start with local chat setup . retrieval configures embeddings; chat configures answer generation and optional checks. Both sections are optional. A normal site build validates them without calling these providers. Configure retrieval retrieval.embeddings supplies embeddings for passage indexing, semantic queries, and hosted chat builds. Choose a provider and model when you need meaning-based retrieval. docs.config.yaml retrieval : embeddings : provider : voyage model : voyage-4-large dimension : 1024 queryModel : voyage-4-lite To use OpenAI's embeddings, or a server that copies its API, such as Ollama, vLLM, or a LiteLLM proxy, name the openai provider: docs.config.yaml retrieval : embeddings : provider : openai model : text-embedding-3-small keyEnv : OPENAI_API_KEY Key Meaning provider Required. voyage or openai . model Required. The embedding model ID. dimension The vector size. Voyage accepts 256, 512, 1024, or 2048. Other models need it unless Shoalrun knows the model's size. queryModel The model that embeds queries. It must share an embedding space with model , as the Voyage 4 models do. Without it, queries use model . baseUrl openai only. An OpenAI-style server, such as http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama. keyEnv The name of the environment variable that holds the key. It defaults to VOYAGE_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY . The config never holds a key. A key setting fails validation, and keyEnv fails if its value isn't a variable name. Command-line flags on shoalrun index override these settings. See Passage index for the files that --embed writes. Configure chat chat configures the OpenAI-compatible service that writes answers. Choose a provider and model; there is no default model. Start with these fields, then add optional checks or reuse settings as needed. docs.config.yaml chat : provider : openai model : deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash baseUrl : https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 keyEnv : OPENROUTER_API_KEY These fields configure the service and answer limits: Key Meaning provider Required. openai , which covers any OpenAI-style service. model Required. The model ID that your service uses. baseUrl The service's API address. It defaults to https://api.openai.com/v1 . keyEnv The name of the environment variable that holds the key. It defaults to OPENAI_API_KEY . Services on localhost need no key. body Extra fields to send with every request, such as OpenRouter's reasoning . See Send extra request fields . passages How many passages the model sees, from 1 to 20. maxTokens The longest answer the model may write. Reasoning models need a larger value. temperature A number from 0 to 2. Without it, the service's default applies. Optional layers Add these fields to chat when the corresponding capability is needed. Scorer-dependent fields require rerank: jev or an equivalent scorer mapping. Key Meaning readerView Whose questions the chat answers, as reader filter choices. See Answer for one audience . rerank jev reorders the top 24 results with a relevance scorer. It needs JEV_API_KEY . To use a different service, give a mapping instead. See Choose the scorer . gate Needs rerank: jev . decline and hedge are Jev scores from 0 to 1, and decline must be lower. verify Needs rerank: jev . threshold is a Jev score above 0 and below 1. onUnsupported is flag (the default) or remove . See How an answer is checked . direct Needs rerank: jev . Shows a passage word for word instead of calling the model. See Answer without a model . fallback A list of one to five other models to try, in order, when the main one fails. See Use more than one model . escalate A second model to ask when the checks flag an answer, with an optional when list. See Use more than one model . budget Daily caps on questions that reach the model. See Cap the daily spend . challenge A Turnstile check for a hosted chat. See Host the chat on Vercel . log Records questions on a hosted chat. See Host the chat on Vercel . cache Keeps clean answers so a repeated question costs nothing. maxEntries (default 500) and ttlMinutes (default 1,440) set the size and the age. See Reuse answers . cards Needs rerank: jev . Serves answers written ahead of time. threshold (default 0.75) shortlists a card by similarity, and confirm (default 0.9) is the Jev score that must confirm it. See Prepared answers . The gate uses the best passage score: Below decline : return a not-covered response without a chat-model call. Between decline and hedge : generate an answer with a partial-coverage warning. At or above hedge : generate an answer normally. The config never holds a key. A key setting fails validation, and keyEnv fails if its value isn't a variable name. The --model flag on shoalrun ask overrides model , so you can try another model without editing the config. documents.summary: Every shoalrun command, its arguments and defaults, what it prints, and when it fails.

headings.title: eval prepare , eval check , eval snapshot , and eval compare
docs context , docs plan , and docs apply
Audit a project and API sources

documents.text: The private @shoalrun/cli package supplies the shoalrun command. It needs Node.js 22.12 or newer. Follow Getting started to install it from GitHub Packages, then run commands as npx --no-install shoalrun <command> . Framework contributors can build the source checkout and run node framework/dist/cli.js <command> from its root. Commands that return data print JSON to standard output. On an error, the CLI prints {"status":"error","message":"..."} to standard error and exits with code 1. A config argument defaults to docs.config.yaml in the current directory unless noted. Diagrams render without a browser: Pele handles Mermaid syntax, and D2 handles D2 source. Development installs include Puppeteer for browser UI tests; production package installs do not need it. Start a project init shoalrun init [directory] [--starter minimal | api-docs] Copies a bundled starter into directory (default . ). minimal is the default; api-docs includes the fictional Cedar Parcel API, an overview and quickstart, a local OpenAPI file, generated references, search, and a color-mode toggle. Its README explains customization and deployment. Existing unrelated files stay in place, but any destination file collision stops the command before it copies anything. Existing destination directories must be real directories, not symlinks or files. The command prints JSON with the starter, absolute directory, copied files, and the next validate and build commands. Run those commands from the created directory, then replace fixture content and example domains. init does not install packages or deploy the site. Build and serve build shoalrun build [config] [output] [--source-commit SHA] [--release-label LABEL] Compiles the site. output defaults to site-dist . Prints { "status": "ok", "documents": <count>, "operations": <count> } . The build writes to a temporary directory, then deletes output and replaces it . Don't point it at a directory with other files. The build stops before deleting anything if output contains the project or content directory, sits inside the content directory, or holds a file the build reads. It also writes the frontmatter reference to .shoalrun/ beside the config; add .shoalrun/ to .gitignore . Every build writes /build-info.json with the build ID and resolved config digest. --source-commit adds a full 40- or 64-character Git commit hash; --release-label adds a short, public release name. The command uses only the values you pass. Neither flag selects a publication or deployment destination. See use Git branches for separate docs sites . docs changes shoalrun docs changes CURRENT-SNAPSHOT --since PREVIOUS-SNAPSHOT Compares two local documents.sync.json files and prints JSON with build IDs, buildChanged , metadataChanged , and added , changed , and removed page records. Page identity includes its publication variant. The command validates both snapshots and rejects unsupported schema versions, invalid records, and duplicate identities. It reads files only; it does not fetch pages or modify a cache. Keep saved snapshots outside the replaced build directory. See incremental sync . serve shoalrun serve < site-director y > [--host HOST] [--port PORT] Serves a built site. --host defaults to 127.0.0.1 . The port comes from --port , then the PORT environment variable, then 8765 . The server: Returns the Markdown twin when a request asks for text/markdown . See content negotiation . Applies redirects.json and the content types in resource-headers.json . Sends / to the home page when no page has the slug / : the page with ID guide.overview , then /reference , then the first page. Adds a trailing slash to page paths with a 301, and returns a plain-text 404 for missing files. It serves plain HTTP with no compression or cache headers. To host it publicly, bind a public --host such as 0.0.0.0 and put a TLS proxy in front. dev shoalrun dev [config] [output] [--port PORT] Builds the project, serves it at 127.0.0.1:8765 by default, watches the directory containing the config, and refreshes open pages after a successful rebuild. output defaults to site-dist ; --port overrides PORT . A failed rebuild prints its error and keeps serving the last successful build. Fix the source to trigger another build. Restart the command after changing framework TypeScript or files outside the config directory. Also restart after editing a metadata.provider module or a custom highlighting module, because Node loads each module once. search shoalrun search < site-director y > < quer y > [--channel C] [--version V] [--language L] [--limit N] Searches a built site's search-index.json without a server. Quote queries with spaces. It returns JSON with the selected publication, total matches, and up to eight ranked results by default. Each result includes a page ID, HTML URL, Markdown URL, title, summary, type, score, and a short body excerpt. A section match links to its heading in the HTML URL. shoalrun search docs/dist "nulla

On an error, the CLI prints {"status":"error","message":"..."} to standard error and exits with code 1. A config argument defaults to docs.config.yaml in the current directory unless noted. Diagrams render without a browser: Pele handles Mermaid syntax, and D2 handles D2 source. Development installs include Puppeteer for browser UI tests; production package installs do not need it. Start a project init shoalrun init [directory] [--starter minimal|api-docs] Copies a bundled starter into directory (default . ). minimal is the default; api-docs includes the fictional Cedar Parcel API, an overview and quickstart, a local OpenAPI file, generated references, search, and a color-mode toggle. Its README explains customization and deployment. Existing unrelated files stay in place, but any destination file collision stops the command before it copies anything. Existing destination directories must be real directories, not symlinks or files. The command prints JSON with the starter, absolute directory, copied files, and the next validate and build commands. Run those commands from the created directory, then replace fixture content and example domains. init does not install packages or deploy the site. Build and serve build shoalrun build [config] [output] [--source-commit SHA] [--release-label LABEL] Compiles the site. output defaults to site-dist . Prints { "status": "ok", "documents": <count>, "operations": <count> } . The build writes to a temporary directory, then deletes output and replaces it . Don't point it at a directory with other files. The build stops before deleting anything if output contains the project or content directory, sits inside the content directory, or holds a file the build reads. It also writes the frontmatter reference to .shoalrun/ beside the config; add .shoalrun/ to .gitignore . Every build writes /build-info.json with the build ID and resolved config digest. --source-commit adds a full 40- or 64-character Git commit hash; --release-label adds a short, public release name. The command uses only the values you pass. Neither flag selects a publication or deployment destination. See use Git branches for separate docs sites . docs changes shoalrun docs changes CURRENT-SNAPSHOT --since PREVIOUS-SNAPSHOT Compares two local documents.sync.json files and prints JSON with build IDs, buildChanged , metadataChanged , and added , changed , and removed page records. Page identity includes its publication variant. The command validates both snapshots and rejects unsupported schema versions, invalid records, and duplicate identities. It reads files only; it does not fetch pages or modify a cache. Keep saved snapshots outside the replaced build directory. See incremental sync . serve shoalrun serve <site-directory> [--host HOST] [--port PORT] Serves a built site. --host defaults to 127.0.0.1 . The port comes from --port , then the PORT environment variable, then 8765 . The server: Returns the Markdown twin when a request asks for text/markdown . See content negotiation . Applies redirects.json and the content types in resource-headers.json . Sends / to the home page when no page has the slug / : the page with ID guide.overview , then /reference , then the first page. Adds a trailing slash to page paths with a 301, and returns a plain-text 404 for missing files. It serves plain HTTP with no compression or cache headers. To host it publicly, bind a public --host such as 0.0.0.0 and put a TLS proxy in front. dev shoalrun dev [config] [output] [--port PORT] Builds the project, serves it at 127.0.0.1:8765 by default, watches the directory containing the config, and refreshes open pages after a successful rebuild. output defaults to site-dist ; --port overrides PORT . A failed rebuild prints its error and keeps serving the last successful build. Fix the source to trigger another build. Restart the command after changing framework TypeScript or files outside the config directory. Also restart after editing a metadata.provider module or a custom highlighting module, because Node loads each module once. search shoalrun search <site-directory> <query> [--channel C] [--version V] [--language L] [--limit N] Searches a built site's search-index.json without a server. Quote queries with spaces. It returns JSON with the selected publication, total matches, and up to eight ranked results by default. Each result includes a page ID, HTML URL, Markdown URL, title, summary, type, score, and a short body excerpt. A section match links to its heading in the HTML URL. shoalrun search docs/dist "nullable response" --limit 5 If the index contains

documents.title: Use your coding agent
documents.summary: Give your agent project guidance and draft a new documentation page.
documents.text: Use an agent that can read project files and run commands. It writes with its own model; Shoalrun requires no additional authoring API key. Prepare your agent Install the portable authoring skill using your agent's supported skill setup. If it cannot load skills, give it the same project instructions and commands directly. Tell it where to find docs.config.yaml , your writing guide, and reviewed examples. The example writing guide is a starting point you can adapt. The CLI's docs search and docs read commands read bundled Shoalrun guidance. The MCP server offers documentation search and reads for agents that support MCP; it does not write project files. Your agent uses its own file tools and the CLI for edits. Give a working-tree task Name the reader outcome and documentation project. Let the agent discover the relevant pages and required supporting changes from project policy. For example: Read the installed shoalrun-author/SKILL.md and work in this documentation project. Revise the authoring procedure so readers can write titled steps and inspect both outputs. Read project policy and supporting evidence first, preserve earlier local edits, capture a task baseline, edit files normally, and show the matching validation report, preview, and task diff. Do not commit or publish. This uses the harness's own writer and execution permissions. Required navigation, relationships, and changelog entries come from the project instructions rather than an automatic compiler rule. If evidence is missing or policies conflict, the agent should identify the question for review. Draft a new page Define the reader's task Give your agent the audience, goal, intended page type, and supporting sources. Let it gather and evaluate evidence using its own tools. Ask it to identify missing facts rather than invent examples or behavior. Choose and scaffold a template Use the project's templates . Record the starting state before scaffolding: shoalrun docs baseline --out .shoalrun/task-baseline.json --config docs.config.yaml shoalrun scaffold how-to -n content/publish-a-site.mdx --config docs.config.yaml The new file is a draft. Replace the prompts, preserve its identity and publication metadata, and add required companions from project policy. Check and review the page Run the project's style checker and configured checks. Read the draft, verify its examples, and review technical claims against the evidence. shoalrun docs validate --baseline .shoalrun/task-baseline.json --config docs.config.yaml shoalrun docs review /path/from/result/report.json --format markdown shoalrun docs preview /path/from/result/report.json --port 0 Use the actual report path returned by validation. It renders affected drafts in a separate capture while preserving their authored access policy. Review findings, coverage, and skipped checks; use --run-checks only for applicable trusted commands under the harness's permissions. A stale, failed, incomplete, or unavailable result is not a pass. After edits, revalidate and restart the preview from the new report. Stop the foreground preview with Ctrl-C when finished. Prepare publication After the author approves publication, change the page's access policy to public and build to a dedicated output directory. Inspect its HTML, Markdown, navigation, and links before committing or deploying. shoalrun build docs.config.yaml preview-output Related reading Related topics Write with agents — Choose the authoring workflow that fits how you work. Use the bundled agent skills — Give your coding agent the bundled Shoalrun workflow instructions. Apply a checked edit plan — Prepare a checked edit to an existing page. (Status: experimental.)

documents.title: Light and dark mode
documents.summary: Light, dark, and system modes, toggle behavior, storage, and accessibility.

headings.title: Lock the site to one mode

documents.text: Every palette has a light set and a dark set. theme.mode decides which set readers see. Mode Behavior light The default. Readers always see light mode. dark Readers always see dark mode. system Follows the reader's operating system setting. Shows a toggle unless you turn it off. Lock the site to one mode docs.config.yaml theme : mode : dark A locked site writes only the colors for that mode and shows no toggle. The build checks contrast for that mode only. Follow the reader's setting docs.config.yaml theme : mode : system The site starts in the mode the reader's system prefers. A button in the masthead switches between light and dark. The browser stores the choice under the shoalrun-color-mode local storage key on that device, and the choice overrides the system setting. To follow the system setting without a toggle, set toggle: false : docs.config.yaml theme : mode : system toggle : false toggle: true works only with mode: system . The build checks contrast for both modes. Custom callout tones need dark colors before a site can show dark mode. The callout guide explains the dark block. How it works mode: system writes both color sets to /assets/palette.css . The dark set applies inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) . The page sets <meta name="color-scheme"> to light , dark , or light dark , so scrollbars and form controls match. With the toggle on, /assets/mode.js loads in the page head before first paint. It reads the saved choice and sets data-mode="light" or data-mode="dark" on the html element, so the page doesn't flash the wrong colors. The toggle is a button with aria-pressed . Screen readers announce it as "Dark mode", pressed or not pressed. Without JavaScript, the toggle stays hidden and the system setting still applies. If the browser blocks storage, the toggle still works for the current page. Target a mode in project CSS with [data-mode="dark"] , or with prefers-color-scheme for readers who have not used the toggle: styles/project.css @media (prefers-color-scheme : dark) { :root:not ([ data-mode = "light" ]) .doc-card-icon { opacity : .9 ; } } :root [ data-mode = "dark" ] .doc-card-icon { opacity : .9 ; } Code blocks stay dark in both modes. By default, their syntax colors come from the palette's dark set. The code block guide explains how to change it. Related reading Related topics Header links — The dark mode toggle appears in the header beside your links. Color palettes — A palette has one color set for light mode and one for dark mode.

documents.title: Action links
documents.summary: Give a next step a prominent link style while retaining real navigation semantics.
documents.text: <ActionLink> styles a navigation link as a prominent action. <Button> is an alias for authors migrating button-like links. Both render a real <a> element, so they work with keyboard navigation and without JavaScript. < ActionLink doc = "guide.add-page" >Create a page</ ActionLink > < ActionLink href = "https://example.com/download" variant = "secondary" >Download example</ ActionLink > Create a page Download example Attribute Required Meaning doc or href Yes, one A stable document ID, site path, fragment, HTTP(S) URL, or mailto: link. variant No primary (default) or secondary . The body is nonempty inline text, with optional emphasis or inline code. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML renders a real link with a visible focus state. Markdown retains its label and destination, resolving doc IDs to the target Markdown page. An agent can follow the destination without interpreting the visual button style.

documents.title: ApiExample and ApiSchema
documents.summary: Include named OpenAPI examples and selected schemas in authored pages.
documents.text: ApiExample and ApiSchema reuse OpenAPI content in authored pages. Examples stay synchronized with named payloads; schemas expose selected field definitions in HTML and Markdown. ApiExample <ApiExample> copies a named example from the OpenAPI source bound to a stable operation ID. Use it in a guide when the full payload should stay synchronized with the reference. Syntax < ApiExample operation = "notes.create" kind = "response" status = "201" mediaType = "application/json" example = "saved" /> Attribute Required Meaning operation Yes Stable operation ID bound to an API source. kind Yes request or response . mediaType Yes Exact media type in the source. example Yes Key in that media type's OpenAPI examples map. status For responses Response status, such as 201 . The element is standalone and empty, with literal string attributes. It resolves in the page's publication. HTML and Markdown show the example title, original key, context, description when present, provenance, and value. A missing selector fails the build. API includes cannot be nested inside snippets. See API references for source configuration and example presentation in reference pages. The fictional Notes API returns a saved note with its author, labels, and display metadata. The response includes a required but nullable archivedAt field: null means the note is active. Created release note OpenAPI response 201; application/json. Example key: saved. Authored in OpenAPI. An active note with a nested author, two labels, and optional display metadata. { "id" : "note_123" , "text" : "Review the release candidate." , "createdAt" : "2026-10-18T09:30:00Z" , "archivedAt" : null , "author" : { "id" : "usr_42" , "displayName" : "Morgan Lee" } , "tags" : [ "release" , "review" ] , "metadata" : { "source" : "release-checklist" , "pinned" : true } } Markdown twin During the build, Shoalrun selects the named example from the OpenAPI source for this page's publication and replaces <ApiExample> with ordinary content. An agent reading the generated .md page does not need to resolve the component or fetch the OpenAPI file. The example above renders as: ### Created release note OpenAPI response 201; application/json. Example key: saved. Authored in OpenAPI. An active note with a nested author, two labels, and optional display metadata. ```json { "id" : "note_123" , "text" : "Review the release candidate." , "createdAt" : "2026-10-18T09:30:00Z" , "archivedAt" : null , "author" : { "id" : "usr_42" , "displayName" : "Morgan Lee" } , "tags" : [ "release" , "review" ] , "metadata" : { "source" : "release-checklist" , "pinned" : true } } ``` An OpenAPI description appears between the context line and payload when present. JSON-compatible values use a json fence; string values with a text/* media type use a text fence. If the source uses externalValue , the twin shows an External example link instead of an inline payload. A response example's context includes its status, such as response 201; application/json . ApiSchema <ApiSchema> includes a schema from a configured OpenAPI source. It can select a request or response body, a standalone object, or one field. Use it when readers need the exact source definition alongside task instructions. Syntax < ApiSchema operation = "notes.create" kind = "response" status = "201" mediaType = "application/json" /> Attribute Required Meaning operation For a body Stable operation ID bound to an API source. api For a standalone schema Configured API ID. kind With operation request or response . mediaType With operation Exact media type. status For response bodies Response status, such as 201 . schema With api Local OpenAPI $ref selector. With operation , omitted uses the selected media type's schema. Use operation , kind , mediaType , and status for a body schema. To select an object that is not a body, use api and schema without the operation attributes. A pointer ending in /properties/<name> selects a single field. Both forms use the API source for the page's publication. < ApiSchema api = "notes" schema = "#/components/schemas/NoteMetadata" /> < ApiSchema api = "notes" schema = "#/components/schemas/NoteMetadata/properties/source" /> Schema · NoteMetadata object Optional display information for a note. 2 properties source string optional ⓘ Where the note came from. pinned boolean optional ⓘ Whether the note stays at the top. Field · source string Where the note came from. The element is standalone and empty, with literal string attributes. A missing or invalid selector fails the build. API includes cannot be nested inside snippets. See API references for source setup and focused contracts. Response 201 schema · application/json A saved note with its author, labels, and display metadata. 7 properties id string always present ⓘ The generated note ID. text string always present ⓘ maxLength: 280 The saved text. createdAt string always present ⓘ format: date-time When the note was created. archivedAt s

documents.title: Badges
documents.summary: Put a short, labeled status or platform name inside a sentence.
documents.text: <Badge> adds a compact label inside prose, a heading, or a table cell. Write the state in its text; color and the optional icon only reinforce it. The API is < Badge variant = "success" icon = "check" >Stable</ Badge >. The API is Stable . Built-in variants These five variants are available in every Shoalrun project. None has a default icon. Variant Example Color source neutral Platform --color-field-surface , --color-ink , and --color-border from the active palette. info Preview The active palette's callout-note background, text, and line tokens. success Stable The active palette's callout-tip background, text, and line tokens. warning Deprecated The active palette's callout-warning background, text, and line tokens. new New The active palette's purple callout-important background, text, and line tokens. The built-in variants follow the selected palette and color mode. A project can override a built-in variant or add another in badges.variants . Add icon only when it helps the reader. The variant changes presentation only; Markdown keeps the label text. Add a custom color For example, this site registers a teal partner variant. It is a custom example, not one of the built-in variants. Give a custom variant background and text hex colors for light mode, and for dark mode if the site shows dark mode. border is optional and defaults to the text color. The build rejects unknown variant names and checks badge text against its background at 4.5:1 in each shown mode. docs.config.yaml badges : variants : partner : light : { background : '#e5f5f3' , text : '#175b57' , border : '#4c9992' } dark : { background : '#102e2d' , text : '#a6e7df' , border : '#4caaa1' } This feature is < Badge variant = "partner" >Partner</ Badge >. This feature is Partner . Projects can put this mapping in a separate file with $include . To change a built-in variant across a site, register that same name with custom colors. For broad palette changes, edit the palette tokens ; for CSS-level overrides, see the CSS reference . Attributes and output Badge attributes control its label, appearance, and representation in the published outputs. Attribute Required Meaning variant No A built-in or registered name. Defaults to neutral . icon No A lowercase Lucide icon name, such as check . Decorative in HTML. The body must be nonempty plain text. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML renders a styled <span> with the visible label. Markdown keeps the label inline, so an agent receives the status or platform name without relying on color or an icon. There is no JavaScript behavior; the label remains readable without CSS.

Defaults to neutral . icon No A lowercase Lucide icon name, such as check . Decorative in HTML. The body must be nonempty plain text. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML renders a styled <span> with the visible label. Markdown keeps the label inline, so an agent receives the status or platform name without relying on color or an icon. There is no JavaScript behavior; the label remains readable without CSS.

documents.title: Breadcrumbs
documents.summary: Show where a page sits in the configured navigation hierarchy.
documents.text: Shoalrun generates breadcrumbs from the navigation tree . Place a page under its intended groups in navigation; there is no <Breadcrumbs> tag to repeat in each MDX file. Configuration This abbreviated navigation puts Breadcrumbs under the Customize and Navigation groups. Those labels become part of its trail: Customize / Navigation / Breadcrumbs . docs/config/nav.yaml - id : styling label : Customize items : - id : navigation label : Navigation items : - id : navigation-overview doc : guide.navigation-lifecycle label : Overview - id : breadcrumbs doc : guide.component.breadcrumbs A group without a document has a plain-text label in the trail. An ancestor with a document becomes a link. The current page is shown as text, never as a link to itself. Top-level pages have no trail. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML puts a breadcrumb navigation region above the page heading. It uses an ordered list and marks the current page with aria-current="page" . Links remain ordinary keyboard-accessible links, and the trail works without JavaScript. Markdown shows the same path near the title. Ancestors with pages link to their Markdown versions. Each document manifest entry has a breadcrumbs array containing ordered labels and any available URLs. An agent can recover the hierarchy without parsing HTML navigation. Related reading Reference while working Organize site navigation — Place pages in navigation to generate their breadcrumb trails. documents.title: Callouts
documents.summary: Use built-in callouts or register a type with its own label, tone, and icon.
documents.text: <Callout> highlights a short message in the reading flow. Use a type that matches the message's purpose. The type sets the HTML color and decorative icon, while a visible label carries the meaning in both HTML and Markdown. Choose a type Choose a callout type that matches the information readers need to notice. Type Use it for note Helpful context or a clarification. tip A practical suggestion that makes a task easier. important Information readers must notice to complete a task correctly. warning A possible problem readers can avoid. caution A higher-risk action or consequence that needs extra care. < Callout type = "warning" >Use a fresh idempotency key for a new payment.</ Callout > Note: The example API is fictional. Tip: Keep a copy of the response ID for later checks. Important: Check the selected API version before copying a request. Warning: A changed idempotency key can create a second payment. Caution: Review the target environment before deleting data. Attributes and defaults Use these attributes to set the callout type and its visible title. Attribute Required Meaning type No A built-in or registered type. Omitted with no label defaults to note . label No Nonempty literal text that replaces the visible type name. Set both when the message needs a more specific label: < Callout type = "warning" label = "Before retrying" >Reuse the original idempotency key.</ Callout > Before retrying: Reuse the original idempotency key. A label without a type retains the neutral style used by earlier pages. Its label remains visible in Markdown: < Callout label = "Before you begin" >Use a draft page while checking examples.</ Callout > Before you begin: Use a draft page while checking examples. A bare <Callout> uses the note label and style. Unknown types, unsupported attributes, and empty labels fail the build. Note: This uses the default note style and label. Register a type Add callouts.types to the project config. Each new type needs a label and a tone . The tone can be one of the five built-in values or a name registered in callouts.tones . An optional icon names a Lucide icon in lowercase kebab-case. This site's configuration registers an experiment type with its own laboratory tone: docs.config.yaml callouts : { $include : ./config/callouts.yaml } config/callouts.yaml tones : laboratory : line : '#087f8c' background : '#e9f8f8' text : '#075c66' dark : line : '#3cb9c4' background : '#0e2a2d' text : '#8fe3ea' types : experiment : label : Experiment tone : laboratory icon : flask-conical Use the registered name in MDX: < Callout type = "experiment" >Try this flow in a test environment first.</ Callout > Experiment: Try this flow in a test environment first. Each custom tone needs line (left rule), background , and text (label and icon), all as hex colors. Multiple types can share a tone. A tone's dark block sets the same three colors for dark mode . It is optional on a light-only site. When theme.mode is dark or system , every tone in use needs dark , or the build fails. The build checks each tone against the site's palette in every mode the site shows. Body text, links, and the label need 4.5:1 against the tone's background. You can also use callouts.tones to replace a built-in tone's colors. The five built-in types have default labels and Lucide icons; you can override their label , tone , or icon in callouts.types . A registered type without an icon displays its label without an icon. Icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the label stays in HTML and Markdown. Invalid names, colors, icons, and definitions fail the build. HTML, Markdown, and agents The body accepts ordinary Markdown and supported MDX components. HTML renders a styled blockquote with the visible label and optional icon; Markdown renders a labeled blockquote with the full body. Colors and icons never carry the only meaning, and no browser script is needed. Keep the message short. Use a normal section heading for longer instructions. The CSS reference lists the color tokens for each type. See the component index for other supported elements. Related reading Reference while working CSS and theme reference — Restyle callout tones with theme tokens. Related topics Short definitions — Choose a short optional definition or an explanation visible in the reading path.

documents.title: Code blocks
documents.summary: Write fenced examples and configure Shiki or another highlighter.
documents.text: Fenced code is ordinary Markdown rather than an MDX component. It belongs in the component reference because authors use it beside components to show commands, configuration, and payloads. Syntax ```yaml title="Frontmatter fields" filename="config/frontmatter.yaml" fields : agent.intent : type : string ``` Frontmatter fields config/frontmatter.yaml fields : agent.intent : type : string Fence option Required Meaning Language, such as yaml No Chooses a build-time highlighting grammar; unknown languages remain plain. title="Frontmatter fields" No Shows a descriptive heading above the HTML block. filename="config/frontmatter.yaml" No Shows a file path beside the title. Use title , filename , both, or neither. Existing fences that use title for a path still display that text. Code, title, and filename are available before browser scripts run. HTML adds a Copy button when clipboard access is available; it copies the original text without syntax markup. Long blocks scroll horizontally. The Markdown twin keeps both options on the original fence. The settings below explain Shiki, themes, plain code, and custom adapters. Highlighting with Shiki Shoalrun highlights fenced code and OpenAPI example panels while building the site. Shiki is the default provider, with the site theme. The HTML already contains the colored code before browser scripts run. The Markdown twin keeps the original fenced text. Language labels, filenames, and copy controls are covered above. Configure Shiki Add this to the root config or an imported outputs fragment: outputs : html : highlighting : provider : shiki theme : site The default is equivalent to that configuration. The site theme takes code colors from the site palette . Keywords use the accent color. Strings, numbers, and functions use the palette's green, amber, and blue. Code colors change with the palette, including in the theme previewer . A color below 4.5:1 contrast on the code background falls back to plain code text. To use a theme you know from your editor, set theme to a bundled Shiki theme name, such as github-dark , dracula , or one-dark-pro . A dark theme sets the syntax colors, and the palette still sets the block background so it matches the toolbar. A light theme, such as github-light , sets both its colors and its background. Shiki's theme list shows available names. Site typography and surrounding colors still come from CSS tokens . An unknown theme fails the build. The built-in grammars are JSON, YAML, shell, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, HTML, CSS, MDX, Markdown, HTTP, XML, SQL, Go, Java, Ruby, C#, PHP, and Rust. Shiki also recognizes loaded aliases such as sh and js . Unknown or unlabeled code stays plain. JSON-compatible API examples use JSON highlighting; text media currently use plain text. Choose plain code outputs : html : highlighting : provider : none none keeps code readable without syntax colors. Shiki is loaded only when its provider is selected. Code titles, scrolling, and copy behavior still work. Use a custom highlighter outputs : html : highlighting : provider : custom module : ./highlight.mjs The module path is relative to the config fragment that declares it. Export a synchronous function that returns flat text tokens. Each token may have a hexadecimal color: export function highlight (code , language) { // Replace this with tokens from your preferred highlighter. return [{ text : code , color : "#e4f2e9" }]; } The adapter may import an installed library and initialize it with top-level await. Its highlight function must be synchronous. Tokens must reproduce the source code exactly, including whitespace, and colors must use #rgb , #rgba , #rrggbb , or #rrggbbaa . The framework validates tokens and escapes HTML; the adapter does not return raw HTML. Invalid tokens or changed text fail the build. The same adapter handles authored fences and API example panels. The entry module appears in the dependency manifest, while its own imports are not tracked individually. HTML, Markdown, and agents Highlighted code remains selectable without JavaScript. Blocks scroll horizontally without widening the page. Keyboard users can focus a long block to scroll it. The Copy button appears when the browser supports clipboard access in a secure context such as HTTPS or localhost. It copies the original code text rather than the colored spans. Without clipboard access, readers can select and copy manually. The Markdown twin keeps the original fenced code, language, title, and filename. An agent reading it receives the complete source text without syntax-color markup or the Copy control. The publishing guide explains where HTML and Markdown outputs are written. Related reading Reference while working CSS and theme reference — Look up the code color tokens and selectors. Related topics Walkthroughs — Walkthroughs build on code blocks to explain an example one step at a time.

documents.title: Collapsibles
documents.summary: Show optional detail in individual disclosures or compact groups, with full Markdown output.
documents.text: <Collapsible> keeps supporting detail near the main instructions. Use it for material readers may need, but do not need to see before taking the next step. Its body is present in the initial HTML even when closed, and fully expanded in the Markdown twin. Syntax < Collapsible title = "Why is this page a draft?" > Pages with draft access stay out of the public build. </ Collapsible > Why is this page a draft? Pages with draft access stay out of the public build. Attribute Required Meaning title Yes Nonempty literal text for the disclosure summary. open No Bare boolean attribute that starts the disclosure expanded. The body must contain block content. Dynamic MDX expressions and unknown components fail the build. Include Markdown and MDX The body accepts paragraphs, lists, links, fenced code, and supported MDX components such as Callout and DocLink . These render inside the disclosure in HTML and in reading order in Markdown. < Collapsible title = "Check the result" open > - Confirm the response status. - Compare the returned ID. < Callout type = "tip" >Keep the response for troubleshooting.</ Callout > </ Collapsible > Use a normal section heading when readers should see the content as part of the main path. See the component index for other supported elements. Group related items Wrap related disclosures in <CollapsibleGroup> to join their borders and remove the gaps between them. Each item opens independently, so readers can compare more than one answer. The wrapper accepts one or more direct Collapsible children and has no attributes. Use each child's title and optional open attribute as usual. < CollapsibleGroup > < Collapsible title = "What gets published?" > The build includes public pages in the selected publication. </ Collapsible > < Collapsible title = "Can I preview first?" > Yes. Build locally and review the HTML and Markdown before deployment. </ Collapsible > </ CollapsibleGroup > What gets published? The build includes public pages in the selected publication. Can I preview first? Yes. Build locally and review the HTML and Markdown before deployment. Put rich content inside each child. Other direct children fail the build. Groups do not enforce a single open item. HTML, Markdown, and agents Individual disclosures and grouped items use native details and summary , so they work without JavaScript. Every body is present in the initial HTML even when closed. Markdown writes every title as a heading followed by its full body in source order. The group wrapper adds no extra heading or repeated text. An agent can read all details without opening a control. Related reading Often confused with Tabs — A collapsible hides optional detail behind one summary; tabs switch between alternate views of the same content. Short definitions — A short definition contains plain text; a collapsible holds longer rich content.

documents.title: CookbookChooser
documents.summary: Let readers select reviewed recipes and assemble them into one reading path.
documents.text: Use <CookbookChooser> to help a reader choose a complete recipe or combine compatible recipes. The author reviews each recipe and sets its place in the choice list. The browser loads the selected published recipe pages and displays their instructions. The component does not read ingredient files, generate a recipe, or execute commands. Start with how recipes and cookbooks work , then configure a cookbook ; this page lists the component's exact syntax. Syntax Map each option to a public recipe in project YAML, then place the chooser on a page in the same publication: config/cookbooks.yaml site-checks : title : How much validation do you need? mode : single options : - { id : build , label : Build , doc : recipe.build-docs } - { id : audit , label : Audit , doc : recipe.audit-docs } docs.config.yaml cookbooks : { $include : ./config/cookbooks.yaml } < CookbookChooser id = "site-checks" /> Try the live chooser for this documentation project: How much validation do you need? Build and check page artifacts Use when: You want to confirm a documentation edit compiles into HTML and Markdown. You need: A Shoalrun checkout with dependencies installed and the page's stable ID. You will have: A successful build and the checked paths for both page formats. Build and run project audits Use when: You are preparing a change for review and need the configured API and project checks too. You need: A Shoalrun checkout with dependencies installed and the page's stable ID. You will have: A successful build, checked artifacts, and no failed configured audits. Choose one recipe. Link to this path Download Markdown Print this path Recipes in this cookbook: Build and check page artifacts — Build this documentation site Build and run project audits — Build and audit this documentation site Value Rule id Required literal cookbook ID from cookbooks . No child content or other attributes. options Nonempty ordered list of unique lowercase IDs, visible labels, and recipe document IDs. This order controls the assembled path. mode Optional single for alternatives or multiple (default) for compatible recipes. Option descriptions Optional when , needs , and outcome explain the choice in HTML and Markdown. Each is nonempty plain text. Recipe target Must be a public type: recipe page in the chooser's channel, version, and language. The build rejects duplicate IDs, labels, or recipe targets, plus missing, draft, wrong-type, or wrong-publication targets. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML displays checkboxes, or radio buttons for mode: single , after the page script starts. Selecting options loads the published recipe pages and assembles their instructions in configured order under Your path . Each section links to its source recipe. If a page cannot load, the source link remains available. The recipe list below the controls works without JavaScript. The cookbook page and choice list are compiled at build time. Recipe content is fetched when a reader selects it in the browser. The selected option IDs are stored in the page URL. Link to this path preserves that selection; Download Markdown saves all selected recipe instructions, and Print this path prints the loaded path. Downloads fail as a whole if a recipe cannot be fetched. Printing is disabled while any selected recipe failed to load. Markdown lists every recipe with its choice descriptions and a link to its .md page in the same order. An agent can choose a recipe from those descriptions and read its complete Markdown. The cookbook Markdown does not contain the browser-selected recipe bodies. Give an agent the recipe Markdown or downloaded selection to follow a task. A selection URL does not create a published Markdown endpoint. Related reading Related topics Compose and maintain recipes — Let readers assemble reviewed recipes into a path in a cookbook.

documents.title: Definition lists
documents.summary: Pair terms with full explanations in semantic HTML and readable Markdown.
documents.text: Use <DefinitionList> for a compact glossary or configuration reference. Put alternating <Term> and <Definition> children inside it. Add filter when readers need to search a long list by term or definition text. Syntax < DefinitionList filter > < Term >Publication</ Term > < Definition >A channel, version, and language combination.</ Definition > < Term >Slug</ Term > < Definition >The page's public path. See [ Page metadata ](doc:guide.frontmatter) .</ Definition > </ DefinitionList > Filter terms and definitions Publication A channel, version, and language combination. Slug The page's public path. See Page metadata . filter is an optional bare attribute on <DefinitionList> . The other tags have no attributes. Terms and definitions must have content; definitions can contain links and rich text. See the site glossary for a longer filtered list. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML uses <dl> , <dt> , and <dd> , with aligned columns on wide screens and stacked pairs on narrow screens. With filter , JavaScript adds a labeled search input and a live count above the list. It searches both terms and definitions, hides or shows each pair together, and Escape clears the query. Without JavaScript, every pair remains visible and the filter control stays hidden. Markdown keeps each term immediately before its full definition in a list, so an agent can read every pair in order. The interactive filter does not appear in Markdown. Related reading Related topics Glossary — See a long, filterable definition list in use.
