documents.title: Diagrams
documents.summary: Render flowcharts, sequence diagrams, charts, and graphs from D2 or Mermaid source as static SVG.
documents.text: Use <Diagram> for flowcharts, sequence diagrams, charts, and other graphs written as text. D2 is the default engine, with TALA as its default layout. Set engine="mermaid" for Mermaid syntax, rendered by Pele . Diagrams render to SVG during the build, so readers do not need a diagram script in their browser. Set a literal pixel width , such as width="440" , to cap the diagram's displayed width while allowing it to shrink on narrow screens. For the diagram languages themselves, use the official D2 tour and Mermaid syntax reference . Shoalrun's component controls how their source is published; those references cover each language's shapes, connections, and diagram types. Every diagram needs a short title and summary . The summary states the point of the diagram; it does not need to repeat every connection. For a complex diagram, add a fuller explanation in nearby prose so readers can understand its meaning without the graphic. D2 Copy the complete component, including its fenced source: < Diagram title = "Documentation build" summary = "One source produces an HTML page and a Markdown page." > ``` d2 source: MDX source build: Shoalrun build html: HTML page markdown: Markdown page source -> build build -> html build -> markdown ``` </ Diagram > Documentation build — One source produces an HTML page and a Markdown page. Use layout="elk" or layout="dagre" when a directional flow reads better than TALA's architecture layout. D2 accepts only these three layout values. Browse the D2 gallery for containers, tables, classes, sequences, grids, and basic shapes with copyable source. The official D2 layout guide compares the engines. The D2 style guide and theme guide cover source-level shape styles and theme options. Mermaid Set the engine explicitly and keep the fence language mermaid : < Diagram title = "Review flow" summary = "The author submits a page, then a reviewer approves it." engine = "mermaid" > ``` mermaid flowchart LR author[Author] --> review[Review] review --> publish[Publish] ``` </ Diagram > Author Review Publish Review flow — The author submits a page, then a reviewer approves it. Attribute Required Meaning title Yes Short literal name for the diagram. summary Yes Literal explanation of the diagram's point. engine No d2 by default; use mermaid for Mermaid source. layout No D2 only: tala by default, or elk or dagre . width No Pixel width from 1 through 4096 as a literal string, such as "440" ; the diagram still shrinks on narrow screens. Keep the source in one fenced code block inside the component. When quoting a complete example in Markdown, use four backticks around the outer mdx block so its inner three-backtick fence stays intact. See the diagram gallery for examples of every built-in Pele diagram family and 48 flowchart shapes. Use Mermaid’s syntax reference to write the source and Pele’s compatibility guide to check rendering differences. External Mermaid plugins are not supported. Styling and readability Pele diagrams inherit Shoalrun’s active palette, fonts, and corner radius. They update with light/dark mode and the theme switcher without re-rendering. Shoalrun maps Pele’s native CSS variables to its theme tokens; there is no second set of diagram aliases to learn. Override Pele’s variables in project CSS . For example, adjust the nodes and their text together: styles/project.css .content .doc-diagram .pele { --pele-surface : var (--color-field-surface) ; --pele-fg : var (--color-ink) ; --pele-border : var (--color-accent) ; --pele-radius : 8 px ; } See Pele’s styling guide for all variables, series colors, and element classes. Its examples show more diagram variations. Fixed source-level colors do not follow the palette; check their contrast in both modes. Custom fonts can change label widths, so inspect long labels after overriding fonts. Without width , a diagram fills the available content width. Set width="520" to cap one diagram at 520 pixels; it still shrinks on narrower screens. Use .doc-diagram and .doc-diagram figcaption to style the frame and caption. D2 still renders separate light and dark SVG images using themes 0 and 200. Project CSS can style their frames and dimensions, but cannot reach individual nodes inside those image files. HTML, Markdown, and agents Pele generates inline SVG during the build. It needs no browser or client-side renderer, and the diagram works without JavaScript. Each SVG has an accessible name from title and a visible caption with the summary . Published light/dark SVG files remain available for direct links and Markdown readers. The .md page retains the title, summary, SVG link, and original fenced D2 or Mermaid source. Readers and agents can inspect the structure without running a diagram library. Changing the renderer does not remove the source or explanation. Shoalrun disables diagram links, external images, and JavaScript callbacks. It rejects active SVG content before publication. Arbitrary HTML labels and Mermaid’s named the

documents.title: DocLink
documents.summary: Link to a page by stable document ID.
documents.text: <DocLink> resolves a document ID to its URL in the current publication. It is useful in MDX when the link should use a stable target and optionally inherit the target page's title. Which link should I use? Choose a link form based on whether the destination is a document, a section, or an external resource. Link Use it for What happens [Read the guide](doc:guide.frontmatter) Most links to another Shoalrun page. Resolves the stable document ID in the current publication. <DocLink doc="guide.frontmatter">Read the guide</DocLink> An MDX link by ID, especially when you want the target title as fallback text. Resolves the same target as doc: Markdown. [Open the specification](https://example.test/spec) External sites, downloads, or other URLs without a Shoalrun document ID. Keeps the authored URL. [Jump to fields](#fields) A section on the current page. Keeps the fragment link. Prefer doc: Markdown for ordinary prose. Both ID-based forms survive a target slug change and fail the build if the target is unavailable in this publication. A normal Markdown link to a Shoalrun route can work, but the authored URL must be updated if that route changes. Raw HTML or JSX anchors such as <a href="..."> do not have a semantic adapter in this prototype and fail the build; use Markdown links instead. Syntax < DocLink doc = "guide.frontmatter" >Read the frontmatter guide</ DocLink > Attribute Required Meaning doc Yes Stable ID of a page available in the current publication. If the body is empty, the target page title supplies the link text. Keep explicit body text plain. See content and stable IDs . HTML, Markdown, and agents The build keeps only the plain text inside DocLink , so emphasis or code formatting there is dropped. HTML links to the page; the Markdown twin links to its .md URL. An agent following that link receives the target’s Markdown page. Related reading Related topics Content and stable IDs — Link to pages by stable ID so links survive slug changes. Cards and collections — Link to a page inline, or show it as a card with its summary.

documents.title: Fields
documents.summary: Write field lists in MDX with the same readable format as OpenAPI schemas.
documents.text: Use <Fields> and <Field> to describe fields that are not selected from an OpenAPI schema, or to explain a small task-specific subset in your own words. The list uses the same field styling as generated schemas. If the exact contract already exists in OpenAPI, ApiSchema can include the source schema or one of its fields. Syntax < Fields > < Field name = "name" type = "string" required minLength = "1" maxLength = "80" example = "Casey" > The name shown to readers. </ Field > < Field name = "options" type = "object" optional nullable > Extra display settings. < Fields > < Field name = "compact" type = "boolean" optional default = "false" > Use a shorter layout. </ Field > </ Fields > </ Field > </ Fields > name — required string; minLength: 1; maxLength: 80 Example: Casey The name shown to readers. options — optional object; nullable Extra display settings. compact — optional boolean Default: false Use a shorter layout. Fields takes no attributes and needs direct Field children. A Field body accepts ordinary Markdown and supported MDX, including a nested Fields list. A standalone Field or other direct child of Fields fails the build. Attribute reference All values are literal MDX attributes. Text and numbers use quoted strings; flags are bare attributes. These declarations describe fields in the published page. They do not validate user input at runtime. Field attribute Required Meaning name Yes Nonempty field name. type Yes Nonempty type label, such as string , integer , or array of objects . required , optional No Bare presence flags. Omission means optional; the two flags cannot appear together. nullable No Bare flag allowing a null value. It does not change whether the field is present. min , max No Finite numeric value bounds; minimum and maximum are equivalent spellings. minLength , maxLength No Nonnegative integer string-length bounds. minItems , maxItems No Nonnegative integer array-size bounds. format , pattern No Nonempty text for a format name or pattern. example , default No Literal text shown as an example or default value. deprecated No Bare flag marking the field as deprecated. Bounds must be numeric, and each minimum must be no greater than its maximum. min cannot be combined with minimum , nor max with maximum . Keep the declared type, constraints, and examples consistent with the actual contract. < Fields > < Field name = "rank" type = "integer" optional min = "0" max = "10" example = "3" > Position in the list. </ Field > </ Fields > HTML, Markdown, and agents The build writes a normal nested Markdown list. Each item starts with the field name and presence rule, followed by its type and authored body. For the first field above, the twin contains: - `name` — **required** string; minLength: 1; maxLength: 80 Example: `Casey` The name shown to readers. Both formats include every field and description. The authored text is part of the page rather than copied from OpenAPI, so keep it aligned with the contract when it describes an API. Related reading Related topics ApiExample and ApiSchema — Write field lists by hand in the same format as generated schemas.

documents.title: File trees
documents.summary: Show nested files and folders with links and an indented Markdown equivalent.
documents.text: <FileTree> shows a file layout or other hierarchy. <Tree> is an alias. Add <Folder> branches and <File> leaves; folders may contain more folders or files. < FileTree > < Folder name = "docs" > < Folder name = "content" > < File name = "start.mdx" doc = "guide.overview" /> < File name = "configuration.mdx" /> < Folder name = "assets" collapsed > < File name = "overview.svg" /> </ Folder > </ Folder > < File name = "docs.config.yaml" /> </ Folder > < File name = "package.json" /> </ FileTree > docs content start.mdx configuration.mdx assets overview.svg docs.config.yaml package.json Every node needs a nonempty name . Folders and files get icons automatically, and a folder’s icon changes when it opens. Optional doc or href makes its label a link; use only one. Optional icon accepts a lowercase Lucide name to override the default. <File> cannot have children. Expand and collapse folders Folders start expanded. Readers can toggle them with a click, tap, Enter, or Space without JavaScript. Add collapsed to a folder to start it closed, and controls to the tree for optional expand-all and collapse-all buttons: < FileTree controls > < Folder name = "project" > < File name = "README.md" /> < Folder name = "content" collapsed > < File name = "start.mdx" /> </ Folder > </ Folder > </ FileTree > Expand all Collapse all project README.md content start.mdx With JavaScript, Up and Down move through visible controls and links; Home and End jump to the first and last. Right opens a folder or moves forward, and Left closes it or moves to its parent. Type a name to jump to a matching visible item, or press * to expand sibling folders at the current level. Tab still follows normal focus order. Expand-all and collapse-all buttons appear only when JavaScript is available. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML uses nested lists and native folder disclosures. Every file is in the initial HTML, including files in closed folders. Links retain normal keyboard behavior. Markdown is a nested list with every node and destination visible, so an agent can follow the hierarchy and links. Icons are decorative, so names must carry the meaning.

documents.title: Images
documents.summary: Add responsive images with optional width limits, captions, and expanded viewing.

headings.title: Add a caption and expanded view

documents.text: Use <Image> to show an image with optional sizing, a caption, or click-to-expand viewing. Plain Markdown image syntax also works when you only need an image and alt text. Basic image Provide a source and alt text. Local paths are relative to the page's MDX file; Shoalrun copies the image into the build. HTTPS URLs work too. < Image src = "./assets/image-example.svg" alt = "A documentation page with navigation, content, and a table of contents" /> Images fit the content column and shrink on narrow screens. They keep their aspect ratio. Plain Markdown has the same default sizing: ![ A documentation page ] (./assets/image-example.svg) Set a width width sets a maximum in pixels. It does not force an image to overflow a smaller screen. Leave it out to use the available content width. < Image src = "./assets/image-example.svg" alt = "A documentation page layout" width = "480" /> Center an image Use align="center" with a width limit to center an image in the content column. The caption and expanded-view link stay with the image. You can also choose left or right . < Image src = "./assets/image-example.svg" alt = "A documentation page layout" width = "480" align = "center" caption = "A centered image with a width limit." expand /> A centered image with a width limit. Add a caption and expanded view Use caption for visible context below the image. Add the bare expand attribute to let readers open a larger view. Select the example to try it. < Image src = "./assets/image-example.svg" alt = "Navigation beside the main content, with a table of contents on the right" width = "480" caption = "A documentation page has three reading areas." expand /> A documentation page has three reading areas. The expanded view supports Escape to close and returns focus to the image link. Without JavaScript or modal-dialog support, the link opens the original asset. A larger view cannot add detail that is missing from a low-resolution source. Attributes All attributes use literal values. expand is a bare boolean attribute. Attribute Required Meaning src Yes Local .png , .jpg , .jpeg , .webp , or .svg path, or an HTTPS URL. alt Yes Text describing the image's meaning. Use alt="" only for decorative images. width No Maximum width in pixels, from 1 to 4096. align No left , center , or right . Default placement follows the surrounding content. caption No Plain text shown below the image and retained in Markdown. expand No Opens a modal image viewer when supported, with an original-image link as fallback. <Image> is an empty block component. It does not accept children, HTML strings, or dynamic expressions. Keep essential explanations in nearby prose and meaningful alt text. For generated diagrams, use Diagram . HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML contains a normal image with alt text. Captions use figure and figcaption . Expandable images use a link enhanced by a modal viewer; the image remains usable without scripts. Modified clicks still open the link normally. Markdown includes the image and alt text, followed by its caption when present. Expandable images also include a link to the original asset. Width, alignment, and modal state do not hide content from agents. Related reading Related topics Diagrams — Render a diagram from source with a caption and responsive width.

Default placement follows the surrounding content. caption No Plain text shown below the image and retained in Markdown. expand No Opens a modal image viewer when supported, with an original-image link as fallback. <Image> is an empty block component. It does not accept children, HTML strings, or dynamic expressions. Keep essential explanations in nearby prose and meaningful alt text. For generated diagrams, use Diagram . HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML contains a normal image with alt text. Captions use figure and figcaption . Expandable images use a link enhanced by a modal viewer; the image remains usable without scripts. Modified clicks still open the link normally. Markdown includes the image and alt text, followed by its caption when present. Expandable images also include a link to the original asset. Width, alignment, and modal state do not hide content from agents. Related reading Related topics

documents.title: Short definitions
documents.summary: Let readers open a brief definition with a click, tap, or keyboard.
documents.text: Use <InfoHint> for a short definition that readers can open when they need it. It is a click-to-expand disclosure. Use a tooltip for brief text that appears on hover or keyboard focus. Put longer explanations in a callout or a linked page. Syntax Give the disclosure a visible label and one short plain-text definition. < InfoHint label = "Canonical URL" > The preferred address for a page when several addresses show the same content. </ InfoHint > Canonical URL The preferred address for a page when several addresses show the same content. Attribute Required Meaning label Yes Nonempty text shown on the disclosure control. <InfoHint> must be a block element with one plain-text definition. It does not accept links, multiple paragraphs, or other components inside the definition. <Tooltip> previously named this same disclosure. Use <InfoHint> to keep click-to-expand behavior; <Tooltip> now provides hover and focus behavior. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML uses native <details> and <summary> elements. Readers can open the definition with a click, tap, Enter, or Space without JavaScript. The definition is present in the initial HTML even while the disclosure is closed. Markdown writes the label and definition together in ordinary text. An agent can read the explanation without opening a disclosure. Related reading Related topics Callouts — Choose a short optional definition or an explanation visible in the reading path. documents.title: Keyboard shortcuts
documents.summary: Mark up key names and shortcuts inside documentation text.
documents.text: Use <Kbd> to name a key or shortcut in a sentence. Include the action in the sentence; key styling alone does not explain what the shortcut does. Syntax Put each key in its own <Kbd> tag and write any separator as ordinary text. Press < Kbd >⌘</ Kbd > + < Kbd >C</ Kbd > to copy selected text. Press ⌘ + C to copy selected text. <Kbd> takes nonempty plain text and no attributes. It works inside prose, headings, and table cells. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML renders each key as a semantic <kbd> element. There is no interactive behavior or JavaScript requirement. Markdown keeps the key names as ordinary text. An agent receives the same instruction and shortcut without interpreting the visual key style. documents.title: Math
documents.summary: Render inline and display LaTeX expressions at build time.
documents.text: Use <Math> with a literal LaTeX expression. It supports the KaTeX math subset and reports invalid expressions during the build. Energy is < Math expression = "E=mc^2" />. < Math display expression = "c^2=a^2+b^2" /> Energy is E = m c 2 E=mc^2 . c 2 = a 2 + b 2 c^2=a^2+b^2 expression is required and nonempty. Add the bare display attribute on a block element for centered display math. The component does not parse dollar delimiters in ordinary prose or code fences. Escape quotes in MDX attributes as needed. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML contains build-time MathML with the source expression as an annotation. The expression remains available to assistive technology without client JavaScript. Markdown keeps inline expressions as code and display expressions in a latex code block. An agent can read the original LaTeX in either form. Check complicated notation with the screen readers your readers use.

documents.title: Content for one format
documents.summary: Use Only to add content to the HTML page or its Markdown twin alone.
documents.text: Use <Only> to author content for one output format. Shared material stays outside the blocks; a block can contain an instruction, explanation, example, or link that serves only one version: Shared setup steps appear in both formats. < Only format = "html" > Choose a tab below to inspect a response. </ Only > < Only format = "markdown" > The response examples follow as labeled sections. </ Only > The example below is live. This HTML page shows the first sentence; its Markdown twin shows the second. The same mechanism can hold a larger section. An HTML section might teach through a visual walkthrough. Its Markdown counterpart can provide file paths and a command sequence for an agent. Each version should give its reader enough to complete the task, and shared product facts should stay consistent. This sentence appears only on the HTML page. HTML, Markdown, and agents An agent that fetches the direct .md URL, or requests this page with Accept: text/markdown on a host that supports content negotiation , receives the shared text and format="markdown" blocks. It does not receive format="html" blocks. For the live example above, the relevant Markdown line is: This sentence appears only in the Markdown twin. The build validates the contents of both blocks, including their links and supported components. <Only> needs block content and exactly one literal format attribute: html or markdown . Dynamic expressions and other values fail the build. Keep facts, warnings, and task steps that both readers need outside <Only> , or provide suitable versions in both formats. You can add or suppress content in either output when that helps its intended reader. Check that each version remains accurate and usable for its task; see Shoalrun's position on shared and format-specific content . The browser search index uses the HTML output, so Markdown-only text is not included in that search. See publishing and agent representations for the full output contract. Related reading Related topics Content negotiation — Write instructions that apply to only the HTML page or only the Markdown twin. Often confused with Tabs — Tabs show alternate views to every reader; Only limits content to the HTML page or its Markdown twin.

documents.title: Progress
documents.summary: Show a bounded count with a visible label and native progress bar.
documents.text: Use <Progress> for a published count in a tutorial or migration guide. It shows the amount completed as text and as a bar. Update the source and rebuild the site when the shared state changes. Syntax < Progress label = "Migration tasks" value = "3" max = "5" /> Migration tasks: 3 of 5 complete 3 of 5 Attribute Required Meaning label Yes Nonempty name shown beside the count and used as the bar's accessible name. value Yes A number from zero through max . max Yes A number greater than zero. <Progress> is a block element without a body. All three attributes must be literal values. The build rejects a value outside the range or a maximum of zero. When to use it Use this component when a count has a known maximum, such as 3 of 5 migration tasks complete. It is a read-only display: readers cannot mark a task complete or move the bar. For a process with named stages and descriptions, use a timeline . HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML shows “Migration tasks: 3 of 5 complete” alongside a native <progress> element. The text carries the count even without CSS or color. There is no JavaScript behavior or keyboard control. Markdown states the same label and count in a sentence. An agent does not need to estimate completion from the bar. Related reading Often confused with Timelines — Progress reports a bounded count; a timeline names and describes stages.

documents.title: RelatedReading
documents.summary: Display authored relationships as links or cards.
documents.text: <RelatedReading> presents connections declared in the central relationships config. Use it for prerequisites, next steps, references, related topics, and distinctions that need a reason. Syntax < RelatedReading relation = "next-step" /> Attribute Meaning relation Select one relationship type; omit for all types grouped by purpose. relatedTo Source document ID; defaults to this page. It must be available in the current publication. layout list by default, or cards . Card layout includes card overrides, summaries, and reasons. empty Text for no matches; default is “No matching documents.” Empty groups are omitted. This is a standalone empty element. A selected relation has no automatic heading, so give that view a page heading when useful. See related reading for config fields, relationship types, and ordering. HTML, Markdown, and agents With layout="list" , HTML and Markdown show links with the relationship reasons; layout="cards" adds previews. Only connections whose endpoints are public in the current publication appear. Both layouts export ordinary links and reasons to Markdown, with .md destinations, so agents can follow the same reading paths. The HTML wrapper has the related-reading class for project CSS . When a top-level view describes the current page, section Markdown also carries its prerequisite and next-step links if they would otherwise be omitted. A Page reading path label explains the scope. Nested views and views with another relatedTo source stay in their original context. See section reading paths for boundaries and size rules. documents.title: Steps
documents.summary: Show a short procedure as numbered steps with full instructions in both outputs.

headings.title: Step headings and the page outline

documents.text: Use <Steps> when each part of a procedure needs a title and supporting content. For a simple sequence with no step titles, an ordinary Markdown numbered list is enough. For code that changes between steps, use a Walkthrough . < Steps > < Step title = "Create a page" > Add ` content/first-page.mdx ` with frontmatter and a short body. </ Step > < Step title = "Build the site" > Run ` shoalrun build docs.config.yaml dist ` , then open the output. </ Step > </ Steps > Create a page Add content/first-page.mdx with frontmatter and a short body. Build the site Run shoalrun build docs.config.yaml dist , then open the output. Choose a style rail is the default: numbered circles and a connecting line keep a longer procedure easy to scan. Use cards to separate steps with substantial examples or decisions. Use plain for a quiet numbered list. The style changes HTML presentation; all three produce the same complete ordered list in Markdown. < Steps variant = "cards" > < Step title = "Prepare" icon = "file-check-2" >Check the draft page.</ Step > < Step title = "Publish" icon = "upload" >Build and deploy the site.</ Step > </ Steps > Prepare Check the draft page. Publish Build and deploy the site. < Steps variant = "plain" > < Step title = "Prepare" >Check the draft page.</ Step > < Step title = "Publish" >Build and deploy the site.</ Step > </ Steps > Prepare Check the draft page. Publish Build and deploy the site. Attribute Where Meaning variant Steps rail (default), cards , or plain . toc Steps ignore (default) or include . Controls whether step headings appear in the page table of contents. headingLevel Steps Heading level 2 (default) through 6 for every step title in the group. title Step Required, nonempty literal title. icon Step Optional lowercase Lucide name. Decorative beside the title in HTML. <Steps> accepts one or more direct <Step> children with nonempty bodies. The body accepts ordinary Markdown and supported components. The same <Step> tag is also used in Walkthrough . Its parent selects a separate component contract: Parent <Step> attributes Output <Steps> title , optional icon Numbered procedure with configurable heading level and TOC behavior. <Walkthrough> title , optional code source and highlighting attributes Code walkthrough with synchronized explanations. Use the attributes documented for the parent you are writing. The two forms do not share rendering or settings. Step headings and the page outline Each step title renders as a real heading with an anchor ID. It defaults to <h2> ; set headingLevel to match the surrounding page structure. Step headings are omitted from the page table of contents by default, keeping the outline focused when a page contains several procedures. Set toc="include" when readers should be able to jump to individual steps: < Steps toc = "include" headingLevel = "3" > < Step title = "Install" >Install the package.</ Step > < Step title = "Configure" >Add the configuration.</ Step > </ Steps > Install Install the package. Configure Add the configuration. The page's tocDepth frontmatter still applies. For example, tocDepth: 2 omits the level-three steps above, while tocDepth: 0 hides the whole outline. Markdown keeps an ordered list with headings at the chosen level and complete bodies. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML renders a semantic ordered list. Numbers, titles, and full bodies are visible without JavaScript or animation, including when CSS is unavailable. An icon never carries the only meaning. There are no controls, so ordinary link and code-block keyboard behavior applies. Markdown keeps the complete ordered list and each step heading at the chosen level. An agent receives every instruction in sequence without needing the visual rail or cards.

documents.title: Tables
documents.summary: Add optional filtering and sticky headings to long HTML tables while preserving every row in Markdown.
documents.text: Ordinary Markdown tables work without a component. For a long table, wrap one table in <Table> to add a filter box, sticky column headings, or both in HTML: < Table filter sticky > | Name | Environment | Status | | --- | --- | --- | | Accounts | Production | Enabled | | Invoices | Sandbox | Disabled | </ Table > filter and sticky are bare boolean attributes. Use either one alone or both. <Table> takes exactly one Markdown table and no other content. Its complete table, without controls, appears in the Markdown twin . Try the controls Filter this table by a name, environment, or status. Several words must all occur in a row; matching ignores case. Press Escape in the filter box to clear it. Scroll inside the table to keep the headings visible. Filter rows Name Environment Status Accounts Production Enabled Billing Sandbox Enabled Catalog Production Disabled Delivery Sandbox Disabled Events Production Enabled Files Sandbox Enabled Groups Production Disabled History Sandbox Enabled Invoices Production Enabled Jobs Sandbox Disabled Keys Production Enabled Limits Sandbox Enabled Metrics Production Disabled Notes Sandbox Enabled Orders Production Enabled Profiles Sandbox Disabled HTML, Markdown, and agents The filter needs JavaScript. Without it, the filter field stays hidden and all rows remain visible. Sticky headings use CSS and still work without JavaScript. On narrow screens the table scrolls horizontally. Keyboard users can focus the scrollable table region. The Markdown twin contains all 16 rows as a regular table. Agents and text-only readers do not need the filter to find a row. Use an ordinary Markdown table when these HTML controls are unnecessary.

documents.title: Tabs
documents.summary: Group alternate views while retaining every view in Markdown.
documents.text: <Tabs> presents alternate views, such as two output formats. Use it only when the choices are truly alternatives; a normal heading sequence is easier to read when readers need every section. Syntax < Tabs label = "Output format" > < Tab label = "HTML" > The page has navigation and controls. </ Tab > < Tab label = "Markdown" > The page keeps the content as text. </ Tab > </ Tabs > HTML Markdown HTML The page has navigation and controls. Markdown The page keeps the content as text. Element Attribute Meaning Tabs label Required literal name for the whole group, used by assistive technology. Tabs equalHeight Optional bare attribute. Keeps the group as tall as its tallest tab. See Keep the height steady . Tabs sync Optional group name for matching selections across tab groups on this page. Tab value Optional matching key; defaults to the tab label. Values must be unique within a group. Tab label Required nonempty literal name for its control and Markdown heading. Use at least two nonempty, direct Tab children. A Tab cannot stand alone. Other direct children and attributes fail the build. Keep the height steady By default, the group is as tall as its selected tab. When a reader switches between a short tab and a long one, the page jumps. Add equalHeight to size the group to its tallest tab instead. The content below the group stays put. < Tabs label = "Output format" equalHeight > The setting changes the HTML only. Without JavaScript, all panels stay visible. The Markdown twin is the same with or without it. Use it when your tabs differ in length. If one tab is much longer than the rest, leave it off, because every shorter tab then shows blank space. Synchronize related examples Give related groups the same sync name. Choosing a tab updates other groups with a matching value , or a matching label when no value is supplied. Matching is case-sensitive. A group without that choice keeps its current selection; groups without sync stay independent. < Tabs label = "Install a client" sync = "language" > < Tab label = "JavaScript" value = "js" > npm install example-client </ Tab > < Tab label = "Python" value = "py" > pip install example-client </ Tab > </ Tabs > These two examples share a selection. Try choosing Python in either group: JavaScript Python JavaScript Install the JavaScript client with npm. Python Install the Python client with pip. JavaScript Python JavaScript Import the JavaScript client in your application. Python Import the Python client in your application. sync names use up to 64 letters, numbers, dashes, or underscores, starting with a letter or number. Synchronization follows reader choices within this page; it does not store a cross-page preference or move focus to another group. Markdown still includes every tab. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML contains every panel before scripts run. Without JavaScript, all panels remain visible. With JavaScript, Left and Right arrows switch tabs, while Home and End choose the first and last. The build replaces the tab controls with ordinary Markdown sections. Each Tab label becomes a level-three heading, followed by that tab's complete body, in source order. The outer Tabs label is for the HTML control and does not appear in Markdown. The first example on this page renders like this in the Markdown twin: ### HTML The page has navigation and controls. ### Markdown The page keeps the content as text. An agent reading the .md page gets every alternative without choosing a tab. Markdown inside each body stays Markdown; supported MDX components expand to their own Markdown forms during the build. Each Tab body accepts ordinary Markdown, including lists, links, and fenced code, plus supported MDX components such as Callout , DocLink , and Collapsible . Put other content inside a Tab body. Dynamic MDX expressions and unknown components are not supported. Related reading Often confused with Collapsibles — A collapsible hides optional detail behind one summary; tabs switch between alternate views of the same content. Content for one format — Tabs show alternate views to every reader; Only limits content to the HTML page or its Markdown twin.

Add equalHeight to size the group to its tallest tab instead. The content below the group stays put. <Tabs label="Output format" equalHeight> The setting changes the HTML only. Without JavaScript, all panels stay visible. The Markdown twin is the same with or without it. Use it when your tabs differ in length. If one tab is much longer than the rest, leave it off, because every shorter tab then shows blank space. Synchronize related examples Give related groups the same sync name. Choosing a tab updates other groups with a matching value , or a matching label when no value is supplied. Matching is case-sensitive. A group without that choice keeps its current selection; groups without sync stay independent. <Tabs label="Install a client" sync="language"> <Tab label="JavaScript" value="js"> npm install example-client </Tab> <Tab label="Python" value="py"> pip install example-client </Tab> </Tabs> These two examples share a selection. Try choosing Python in either group: JavaScript Python JavaScript Install the JavaScript client with npm. Python Install the Python client with pip. JavaScript Python JavaScript Import the JavaScript client in your application. Python Import the Python client in your application. sync names use up to 64 letters, numbers, dashes, or underscores, starting with a letter or number. Synchronization follows reader choices within this page; it does not store a cross-page preference or move focus to another group. Markdown still includes every tab. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML contains every panel before scripts run. Without JavaScript, all panels remain visible. With JavaScript, Left and Right arrows switch tabs, while Home and End choose the first and last. The build replaces the tab controls with ordinary Markdown sections. Each Tab label becomes a level-three heading, followed by that tab's complete body, in source order. The outer Tabs label is for the HTML control and does not appear in Markdown. The first example on this page renders like this in the Markdown twin: ### HTML The page has navigation and controls. ### Markdown The page keeps the content as text. An agent reading the .md page gets every alternative without choosing a tab. Markdown inside each body stays Markdown; supported MDX components expand to their own Markdown forms during the build. Each Tab body accepts ordinary Markdown, including lists, links, and fenced code, plus supported MDX components such as Callout , DocLink , and Collapsible . Put other content inside a Tab body. Dynamic MDX expressions and unknown components are not supported. Related reading Often confused with

Collapsibles — A collapsible hides optional detail behind one summary; tabs switch between alternate views of the same content. Content for one format — Tabs show alternate views to every reader; Only limits content to the HTML page or its Markdown twin.

documents.title: Timelines
documents.summary: Show the current milestone and overall progress through a process.
documents.text: Use <Timeline> to show progress through an ordered set of milestones. Set current to the id of the milestone in progress. Earlier milestones become complete; later milestones become upcoming. This is a read-only progress display . Readers can see the current stage, but they cannot mark milestones complete or move the bar. Update current in the source and rebuild the site when the shared process advances. Links inside milestone content work normally. When to use it Show which stage a product launch or feature rollout has reached. Show where a proposal sits in a draft, review, and approval process. Show progress through a published migration or deprecation plan. An optional simulation mode could let readers move through the milestones to see each stage of a process. The current component shows only the published state; it has no next, previous, or reset controls. < Timeline current = "review" > < Milestone id = "draft" title = "Draft" > Write the first version of the guide. </ Milestone > < Milestone id = "review" title = "Review" > Check the guide with the team. </ Milestone > < Milestone id = "publish" title = "Publish" > Make the approved guide available to readers. </ Milestone > </ Timeline > 1 of 3 milestones complete · Current: Review Draft Complete Write the first version of the guide. Review Current Check the guide with the team. Publish Upcoming Make the approved guide available to readers. The bar counts completed milestones. In this example it shows 1 of 3 complete; Review is still in progress. The current milestone also has a visible status label, and the HTML list marks it with aria-current="step" . The bar uses a native <progress> element with an accessible name. Markdown includes the same progress summary and status labels. Attribute Where Required Meaning current Timeline Yes The ID of the milestone in progress. id Milestone Yes A unique ID using lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Start with a letter. title Milestone Yes Visible milestone title. date Milestone No A real date in YYYY-MM-DD form. Rendered as <time> in HTML. Add one or more direct <Milestone> children in process order. Each milestone needs body content and can contain ordinary Markdown and supported components. HTML, Markdown, and agents HTML shows the progress bar and milestone list with visible status labels; the current item has aria-current="step" . Markdown includes the same progress summary, status labels, and full milestone bodies. An agent can identify the current stage and read every milestone without interpreting the bar.

documents.title: Tooltips
documents.summary: Show brief supporting text on hover or keyboard focus, with a tap option for touch readers.
documents.text: Use <Tooltip> for brief supporting text beside a term. The text appears when readers hover over or focus the label. Use Short definitions for click-to-expand explanations, or a callout for warnings and instructions that belong in the reading path. Syntax Compare the < Tooltip label = "build digest" >A fingerprint of the published build's content.</ Tooltip > before refreshing your cache. Compare the build digest : A fingerprint of the published build's content. before refreshing your cache. Attribute Required Meaning label Yes Nonempty text shown on the focusable trigger. The body must be one brief plain-text explanation. Links, formatted text, multiple paragraphs, and other components are unsupported. A tooltip may appear inline in a paragraph or as a standalone block. <Tooltip> previously aliased <InfoHint> . Use <InfoHint> for the original native disclosure behavior. HTML, Markdown, and agents With JavaScript, the label becomes a button linked to its explanation through aria-describedby . Hovering or focusing the label opens a popup with role="tooltip" . Readers can move the pointer over the popup without closing it. Escape dismisses it while focus stays on the label. Moving focus and the pointer away closes it. Touch readers can tap the label to open or close it, or tap elsewhere to dismiss it. The popup contains no focusable controls. Use an ordinary link or disclosure when readers need to interact with the explanation. Keep tooltips supplementary; essential warnings, choices, and instructions belong in visible page content. Without JavaScript, the label and explanation remain visible together in the page. Markdown includes the label and full explanation as ordinary text, so agents do not need hover, focus, or browser scripts. For the inline example above, the Markdown twin reads: Compare the build digest (A fingerprint of the published build's content.) before refreshing your cache. The interaction follows the WAI tooltip pattern and its guidance on content shown on hover or focus . Related reading Often confused with Short definitions — Tooltips open on hover or focus; short definitions use native click-to-expand disclosures.

documents.title: Walkthroughs
documents.summary: Build code tutorials that explain code one step at a time, with a scrolling pane in HTML and every step in Markdown.
documents.text: Use <Walkthrough> to explain code step by step. Each step pairs an explanation with code built up across steps or read from a project file. When there is room for two columns, explanations scroll on the left and code stays on the right. Scrolling or selecting a step updates the code pane. At either end, scrolling continues through the page. On narrower screens, each step shows its explanation and code in order. The spotlight layout uses step buttons instead of a scroller. Code that stays the same between steps slides to its new position, so readers can follow the changes. Use a walkthrough when readers build up code or study one file in parts. For steps without code, use an ordinary numbered list. Build up code In the default mode, each <Step> has an explanation and can end with one code fence. Give each step the complete code at that point, not only the new lines. highlight picks lines in the step's code to emphasize. MDX source: build up code This source defines the interactive example below. < Walkthrough title = "Verify a webhook" > < Step title = "Read the raw body" > Signatures cover the exact bytes, so read the body as text. ``` ts export async function handler (request : Request ) { const body = await request .text (); return new Response ( 'ok' ); } ``` </ Step > < Step title = "Check the signature" highlight = "3-5" > Compare the header with a signature of the body. ``` ts export async function handler (request : Request ) { const body = await request .text (); const signature = request . headers .get ( 'x-signature' ); if ( ! verify (body , signature)) { return new Response ( 'invalid signature' , { status : 401 }); } return new Response ( 'ok' ); } ``` </ Step > </ Walkthrough > Verify a webhook Step 1 Read the raw body Signatures cover the exact bytes, so read the body as text. Parsing JSON first can change spacing and key order. export async function handler ( request : Request ) { const body = await request . text ( ) ; return new Response ( ' ok ' ) ; } Step 2 Check the signature Compare the signature header with a signature of the body. Reject the request before doing any work. export async function handler ( request : Request ) { const body = await request . text ( ) ; const signature = request . headers . get ( ' x - signature ' ) ; if ( ! verify ( body , signature ) ) { return new Response ( ' invalid signature ' , { status : 401 } ) ; } return new Response ( ' ok ' ) ; } Step 3 Parse the event Parse the body after the check passes. The event type decides what happens next. export async function handler ( request : Request ) { const body = await request . text ( ) ; const signature = request . headers . get ( ' x - signature ' ) ; if ( ! verify ( body , signature ) ) { return new Response ( ' invalid signature ' , { status : 401 } ) ; } const event = JSON . parse ( body ) ; await route ( event . type , event . data ) ; return new Response ( ' ok ' ) ; } Step 4 Acknowledge quickly Queue slow work and answer at once. Senders retry requests that time out. export async function handler ( request : Request ) { const body = await request . text ( ) ; const signature = request . headers . get ( ' x - signature ' ) ; if ( ! verify ( body , signature ) ) { return new Response ( ' invalid signature ' , { status : 401 } ) ; } const event = JSON . parse ( body ) ; await queue . send ( { type : event . type , data : event . data } ) ; return new Response ( null , { status : 202 } ) ; } Explain one file Put one code fence directly inside <Walkthrough> , before the steps, to explain a single file. Steps then have no code of their own. Each step's highlight picks the lines it explains. MDX source: explain one file This source defines the interactive example below. < Walkthrough title = "Read a retry policy" > ``` yaml title="retry.yaml" retry : attempts : 5 backoff : exponential initialDelay : 2s maxDelay : 5m ``` < Step title = "Set the number of attempts" highlight = "2" > Five attempts cover most short outages. </ Step > < Step title = "Choose the delay" highlight = "3-5" > Each retry waits twice as long, from two seconds up to five minutes. </ Step > </ Walkthrough > Read a retry policy retry.yaml retry : attempts : 5 backoff : exponential initialDelay : 2s maxDelay : 5m retryOn : - 429 - 503 - timeout deadLetter : queue : webhooks - failed keep : 14d Step 1 Set the number of attempts Five attempts cover most short outages without hiding a real failure. Line 2 Step 2 Choose the delay Each retry waits twice as long as the one before, from two seconds up to five minutes. Lines 3–5 Step 3 Pick what to retry Retry rate limits, unavailable services, and timeouts. Other errors fail at once, because retrying won't fix them. Lines 6–9 Step 4 Keep failures Requests that use every attempt go to a separate queue for 14 days, so you can replay them. Lines 10–12 Take code from a file Code in a fence can drift from the code your project ru

documents.title: Component reference
documents.summary: Find a dedicated guide for every supported MDX component and code block.
documents.text: Shoalrun accepts GitHub Flavored Markdown (tables, task lists, strikethrough, footnotes, and autolinks) and the MDX components below. Each component family has a page with syntax, attributes, HTML and Markdown behavior, and limits. Component names and attributes are case-sensitive. Unknown components, dynamic MDX expressions, and exports fail the build because they have no shared HTML and Markdown representation. The build drops import lines, so imported components are not available. Custom components let trusted project plugins lower into the shared content pipeline. Navigation and breadcrumbs are configured site features. Their guides live under Customize. Reading and layout Callouts — notes, tips, important messages, warnings, and cautions. Badges — short inline labels for statuses, platforms, and versions. Keyboard shortcuts — key names inside instructions. Short definitions — brief definitions that readers expand with a click, tap, or keyboard. Tooltips — supporting text shown on hover or keyboard focus. Progress — a bounded count with visible text and a bar. Definition lists — terms and rich explanations in semantic HTML. Action links — prominent next-step and download links. Math — inline and display LaTeX expressions rendered to MathML. File trees — nested files, folders, icons, and links. Steps — numbered procedures with titles and full instructions. Timelines — milestone progress with a current stage and completion bar. Collapsibles — individual disclosures and compact groups for optional detail. Tabs — alternate views and their child panels. Code blocks — fenced examples, filenames, and copy behavior. Images — responsive images, captions, width limits, and expanded viewing. Diagrams — D2 and Mermaid source rendered to SVG with Markdown source preserved. Only — a short block for HTML or Markdown alone. Tables — optional row filtering and sticky headings for long tables. Walkthroughs — code explained step by step beside a scrolling code pane. Hero — a landing page opener with a title, tagline, and action buttons. Section — a full-width band on a splash page. ThemePreview — a live switcher for trying presets, palettes, and color modes. ReaderSection, ReaderChoice, and ReaderFilter — marked sections, choice buttons, and in-page filter controls. FrontmatterReference — publish this project's built-in and declared page fields as a live reference. Links and reading paths DocLink — a link by stable document ID. DocCard, DocCards, and DocCollection — document previews, curated lists, and filtered collections. CookbookChooser — choose among custodian-approved sets of prebuilt recipes. RelatedReading — authored relationships as links or cards. Reuse and API content Snippet and Var — shared content and typed values. ApiExample and ApiSchema — named OpenAPI samples and schemas. Fields — authored field lists that match schema formatting. Code highlighting explains Shiki, theme selection, plain output, and custom adapters. Tabs and collapsibles accept ordinary Markdown and supported MDX components in their bodies; their subpages explain the exact nesting rules. Related reading Read first Content and stable IDs — Write a page with a stable ID before adding components to it. Next steps Custom components — Register trusted components that preserve shared content.

documents.title: How Shoalrun works
documents.summary: Follow a page from source file to published HTML and Markdown, and learn the terms the rest of these docs use.
documents.text: Shoalrun is a static documentation compiler. It reads a project config, Markdown and MDX pages, and local OpenAPI files. It writes an HTML site and a Markdown copy of every page. A build makes no network requests and no model calls, so the same inputs always give the same output. Choose your focus Pick a path to narrow the site's navigation and search. The choice persists across visits; All in the header shows every page again. Both paths keep foundational guides like this one visible. Write documentation Configure & publish Start with adding a page , then use page metadata and components to shape it. Start with project configuration , then explore themes and publishing . The build pipeline examples, schemas, reference pages docs.config.yaml Validate frontmatter and publications Pages (.md, .mdx) Shared content tree OpenAPI files HTML pages Markdown twins Manifests and discovery files Shoalrun build pipeline — Config and sources pass through validation and one shared content tree, which produces HTML pages, Markdown twins, and manifests. Load config. The build reads docs.config.yaml and every file it includes or extends. Unknown top-level keys fail. See the configuration reference . Read pages. Every .md and .mdx file in the content directory is parsed, and its frontmatter is merged with project defaults and checked. Drafts are checked too. Choose publications. A public page can name one publication or list several. One source file can therefore produce several page variants, with optional version-specific sections. Write separate files only when the pages need substantially different content. Build the content tree. MDX components, snippets, doc: links, cards, API embeds, and diagrams become one shared tree. Generated API reference pages join here. Render. The same tree produces the HTML page and its Markdown twin, so the two can't drift apart. Diagrams are rendered to SVG at this step: D2 and Pele both run in-process, without a browser. Write the site. The build writes pages, assets, API contracts, and manifests. See published outputs . Identity: IDs, slugs, and routes A page has a stable ID , such as guide.concepts , and a slug , such as /concepts . Links, cards, navigation, and relationships use the ID, so you can rename a file or change a slug without breaking them. The slug sets the URL path, so changing a slug changes the URL. Add a redirect from the old path if readers or other sites link to it. The route is the final URL. It combines site.basePath , a language prefix for a non-default language, the channel's and version's pathPrefix , and the slug. For example, a German page at /guides/retry in a v2 version with pathPrefix: /v2 has the route /de/v2/guides/retry . API operations have three identifiers: Identifier Example Where it comes from Source operationId createNote The OpenAPI file. Stable operation ID notes.create Your apis config. Pages and navigation refer to this. Reference page ID reference.create-note The page that presents the operation. The stable operation ID keeps pages linked even if the OpenAPI operationId changes. See API references . Publications A publication is one enabled combination of channel, version, and language: A channel is an audience or environment, such as production or sandbox . A version is an API or documentation edition, such as v1 or current . A language is a content language, such as en . publications.enabled lists the combinations to build. A page's frontmatter picks one or several of them; files for other versions or languages can share its id . Links, cards, and related reading stay inside the current publication, so a v1 page never links to a v2 page by accident. Each published copy of a page is a variant . The HTML and Markdown copy for each variant include only content selected for that publication. Git branches and tags select source revisions for a build; they do not select publication channels or preserve earlier deployed sites. The deployment and version guide explains how those choices fit together. For a complete versioning and translation workflow, follow put multiple versions on one site . Drafts and publishing Only pages with access.policy: public are published. Anything else, such as draft , is still validated but never written to the site. New pages from shoalrun scaffold start as drafts with placeholder prompts. A public page fails the build until every placeholder is replaced. See templates . Config composition A project config can be one file or many. Four directives combine files: $include replaces a value with the contents of another YAML file. extends layers the current file over one or more preset files. $concat appends to a list inherited from a preset. $remove drops inherited map keys or list items by id . shoalrun config explain <key> reports which file set a value. Follow configure your project for a worked example of composition, precedence, file paths, and debugging. Glossary Terms such as publication , variant , Markdown

Every .md and .mdx file in the content directory is parsed, and its frontmatter is merged with project defaults and checked. Drafts are checked too. Choose publications. A public page can name one publication or list several. One source file can therefore produce several page variants, with optional version-specific sections. Write separate files only when the pages need substantially different content. Build the content tree. MDX components, snippets, doc: links, cards, API embeds, and diagrams become one shared tree. Generated API reference pages join here. Render. The same tree produces the HTML page and its Markdown twin, so the two can't drift apart. Diagrams are rendered to SVG at this step: D2 and Pele both run in-process, without a browser. Write the site. The build writes pages, assets, API contracts, and manifests. See published outputs . Identity: IDs, slugs, and routes A page has a stable ID , such as guide.concepts , and a slug , such as /concepts . Links, cards, navigation, and relationships use the ID, so you can rename a file or change a slug without breaking them. The slug sets the URL path, so changing a slug changes the URL. Add a redirect from the old path if readers or other sites link to it. The route is the final URL. It combines site.basePath , a language prefix for a non-default language, the channel's and version's pathPrefix , and the slug. For example, a German page at /guides/retry in a v2 version with pathPrefix: /v2 has the route /de/v2/guides/retry . API operations have three identifiers: Identifier Example Where it comes from Source operationId createNote The OpenAPI file. Stable operation ID notes.create Your apis config. Pages and navigation refer to this. Reference page ID reference.create-note The page that presents the operation. The stable operation ID keeps pages linked even if the OpenAPI operationId changes. See API references . Publications A publication is one enabled combination of channel, version, and language: A channel is an audience or environment, such as production or sandbox . A version is an API or documentation edition, such as v1 or current . A language is a content language, such as en . publications.enabled lists the combinations to build. A page's frontmatter picks one or several of them; files for other versions or languages can share its id . Links, cards, and related reading stay inside the current publication, so a v1 page never links to a v2 page by accident. Each published copy of a page is a variant . The HTML and Markdown copy for each variant include only content selected for that publication. Git branches and tags select source revisions for a build; they do not select publication channels or preserve earlier deployed sites. The deployment and version guide explains how those choices fit together. For a complete versioning and translation workflow, follow put multiple versions on one site . Drafts and publishing Only pages with access.policy: public are published. Anything else, such as draft , is still validated but never written to the site. New pages from shoalrun scaffold start as drafts with placeholder prompts. A public page fails the build until every placeholder is replaced. See templates . Config composition A project config can be one file or many. Four directives combine files: $include replaces a value with the contents of another YAML file. extends layers the current file over one or more preset files. $concat appends to a list inherited from a preset. $remove drops inherited map keys or list items by id . shoalrun config explain <key> reports which file set a value. Follow configure your project for a worked example of composition, precedence, file paths, and debugging. Glossary Terms such as publication , variant , Markdown twin , and focused contract are defined in the glossary . It lists more than a hundred terms, sorted A to Z, and links each one to its guide. Related reading Next steps Reference while working Glossary — Look up any term used on this page, and more than a hundred others. Related topics Getting started — Learn the build pipeline and the terms the rest of th

documents.title: Configuration reference
documents.summary: Every top-level setting in docs.config.yaml, with defaults, validation rules, and links to the full guides.
documents.text: A project's config starts at docs.config.yaml . The CLI looks for that name by default, and shoalrun scaffold -n searches parent directories for it. For the configuration workflow, composition rules, and debugging, start with configure your project . This page lists every top-level key. Keys with a dedicated guide link there for the full rules. For complete, working configs, see example configs . The root file must be a YAML mapping with schemaVersion: 1 . YAML is parsed strictly: duplicate keys fail. Any top-level key not listed here fails with unknown setting <key> . Keys nested inside site , apis , publications , and outputs are not all checked yet, so check spelling there carefully. docs.config.yaml schemaVersion : 1 site : title : Example documentation publications : defaults : { channel : production , version : current , language : en } channels : production : { pathPrefix : "" } versions : current : { pathPrefix : "" } enabled : - { channel : production , version : current } navigation : { $include : ./config/nav.yaml } Split and combine config files Four directives let one config span several files. Paths are relative to the file that contains them. $include { $include: ./path.yaml } replaces a value with the contents of another YAML file. The included content becomes the value at that position. If the containing file extends a preset, the normal merge rules then apply to that value. A mapping that uses $include can have no other keys. Included files can include others, and a cycle fails with Configuration cycle and the chain of files. Move a large section into its own file: docs.config.yaml navigation : { $include : ./config/nav.yaml } apis : { $include : ./config/api.yaml } Include a value at any depth, not only at the top level: docs.config.yaml apis : payments : source : { kind : file , path : ./apis/payments/openapi.yaml } operations : { $include : ./config/payment-operations.yaml } An API source path is relative to the file declaring source.path . Here config/api.yaml points one level up to reach apis/ : config/api.yaml payments : source : { kind : file , path : ../apis/payments/openapi.yaml } extends A top-level extends: [./base.yaml] in any config file layers that file over one or more preset files, in order. Mappings merge key by key, and lists and single values replace what came before. Use it to share settings across several sites: docs.config.yaml schemaVersion : 1 extends : [ ../shared/docs-base.yaml ] site : title : Payments documentation List several presets to layer them. Later files override earlier ones, and the current file overrides them all: docs.config.yaml schemaVersion : 1 extends : - ../shared/docs-base.yaml - ../shared/brand-theme.yaml A preset is an ordinary config file, and it can have its own extends : ../shared/docs-base.yaml schemaVersion : 1 site : title : Company documentation header : links : - { label : Support , href : "https://support.example.com" } theme : preset : reef A top-level extends is always read as a list of config files. So a file you $include can't use a top-level extends for any other purpose. See the palette example in palettes . $concat and $remove { $concat: [...] } appends items to a list inherited through extends . Without an inherited list, it becomes the list itself. { $remove: [name, ...] } drops inherited mapping keys, or list items by their id . $remove fails when nothing is inherited. Add pages after the shared navigation, and drop a relationship the shared config declares: docs.config.yaml extends : [ ../shared/docs-base.yaml ] navigation : $concat : - { id : payments , doc : guide.payments } - { id : refunds , doc : guide.refunds } relationships : { $remove : [ legacy-overview-link ] } Remove inherited mapping keys by name. This drops a snippet and a template that the preset registers: docs.config.yaml extends : [ ../shared/docs-base.yaml ] snippets : { $remove : [ legal.beta-notice ] } templates : { $remove : [ troubleshooting-legacy ] } $concat also accepts included lists, so each team can keep its own navigation file: docs.config.yaml extends : [ ../shared/docs-base.yaml ] navigation : $concat : - { $include : ./config/nav-payments.yaml } - { $include : ./config/nav-reports.yaml } Run shoalrun config explain <key> docs.config.yaml to see which file set a value and what it replaced. The CLI reference covers the other config commands. search Optional. search.synonyms is a list of groups of two or more words or phrases. Each term in a group can find the others, with exact matches ranked higher. A term can appear in only one group. Use $include to keep the groups in a project-owned YAML file. The site search guide shows the format and which search paths use it. authoring Optional project guidance and read-only source locations. These settings do not choose a model or read external files during a site build. Key Meaning directives Nonempty project writing instructions. guideFiles Project-relative writing-guide paths. exemplarFile

documents.title: Organize project configuration
documents.summary: Learn how Shoalrun resolves config files, layers presets, tracks path origins, and applies page defaults before building publications.

headings.title: Predict a merge before you make it
Separate config inheritance from page metadata
Publication defaults serve a different purpose

documents.text: docs.config.yaml connects your content, presentation, and publication settings. Start with one file, then extract sections or share defaults when several projects need them. This guide explains how those choices interact and how to inspect the result. Use the configuration reference to look up individual fields. Use example projects for complete configurations you can copy. Understand the three stages Configuration takes effect in three stages: Resolve configuration. Read the entry file, load presets and includes, and merge them into one value. Track which file supplied each setting. Resolve pages. Apply configured frontmatter defaults, the page's own metadata, and enforced metadata. Validate the resulting page fields. Build publications. Select public pages for enabled channel/version/language combinations, resolve links and APIs, then produce HTML, Markdown, and discovery files. A preset changes configuration. A page default changes metadata. An enabled publication selects an edition to build. These mechanisms have separate rules; changing one does not automatically create pages or translations. Find the section you need Start with the configuration sections that control the behavior you want to change. Goal Configuration sections Name the site and locate content site Choose editions and routes publications , redirects Organize pages and related reading navigation , relationships Define page metadata and authoring conventions frontmatter , metadata , templates , authoring Reuse text and semantic content variables , snippets , callouts , badges Register local OpenAPI sources and operations apis Style the site and configure rendering theme , outputs Configure reader views and project checks readerFilters , audit Every entry config resolves to a YAML mapping with schemaVersion: 1 . Duplicate YAML keys and unknown top-level settings fail. Nested settings are not all checked for unknown keys, so verify spelling against the reference. Start with one working file The examples use the compiled CLI from the quickstart . From the Shoalrun checkout root, create a separate minimal project: SHOALRUN_CLI = "$PWD/framework/dist/cli.js" CONFIG_DEMO = "$( mktemp -d )" node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" init "$CONFIG_DEMO/site" --starter minimal cd "$CONFIG_DEMO/site" The starter has two pages and this basic configuration structure: docs.config.yaml schemaVersion : 1 site : title : Acme handbook publications : defaults : { channel : production , version : current , language : en } channels : production : { pathPrefix : "" } versions : current : { pathPrefix : "" } enabled : - { channel : production , version : current } frontmatter : defaults : type : guide channel : production version : current access : { policy : public } navigation : - id : welcome doc : guide.welcome - id : setup label : Setup items : - id : install doc : guide.install Build once before reorganizing: node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" build docs.config.yaml dist This produces the same two pages after each reorganization below. Keep dist/ separate from content and configuration inputs. Extract a section with $include An include substitutes another YAML value at its location. The included file can contain a mapping, list, or scalar, depending on the setting that receives it. Create a config/ directory: mkdir -p config Move the navigation list into this file: config/nav.yaml - id : welcome doc : guide.welcome - id : setup label : Setup items : - id : install doc : guide.install Replace the entire navigation section in docs.config.yaml with: navigation : { $include : ./config/nav.yaml } The included file contains the list itself, without a surrounding navigation: key. Adding that wrapper would supply a mapping where navigation expects a list. An include has no sibling keys. For example, placing both $include and label in the same mapping fails with exactly one directive is required . Include a smaller value or use inheritance to combine settings. Includes work at any depth and can include other files. Paths in $include are relative to the YAML file containing that directive. A cycle fails with Configuration cycle and the file chain. Inspect the substituted value and its source: node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" config resolve docs.config.yaml node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" config explain navigation.0.doc docs.config.yaml The first command prints the effective value, digest, and configuration dependencies. The second identifies config/nav.yaml as the source of guide.welcome . Share defaults through extends Use extends when several projects should inherit shared settings. Presets are ordinary YAML mappings and can extend other presets. Each file's extends list is processed in order; later presets override earlier ones, and the local file overrides them all. Create a shared directory beside the site: mkdir -p ../shared Create the following preset: ../shared/base.yaml schemaVersion : 1 site : title : Company handbook customCss : ./brand.css header : links : - { label : Support , href : "https://support.example

documents.title: Use this site's MCP
documents.summary: Connect your agent to Shoalrun's public documentation and ask it to search, read pages, or fetch sections.

headings.title: Ask the agent to use the documentation

documents.text: Connect an MCP client to Shoalrun's live documentation at https://www.shoalrun.com/mcp . You need an agent application that supports remote HTTP MCP servers. No Shoalrun account, API key, custom header, or local installation is required. This endpoint reads Shoalrun's public documentation. To host an endpoint for your own documentation, use the separate MCP hosting guide . Connect and ask a question The setting names vary by client. Use its remote MCP server connection settings: Add the documentation server Create a remote server connection named shoalrun-docs . Choose HTTP or Streamable HTTP when your client asks for the transport. Enter this server URL: https://www.shoalrun.com/mcp Leave authentication and custom headers unset. The URL is an MCP endpoint, not a web page; opening it directly in a browser may show a method error. Connect and discover the tools Save the connection and enable it. Restart or reconnect the client if it does not refresh its tools automatically. Look for search_docs , get_page , get_outline , and get_section under the connection. Your client may prefix their names with shoalrun-docs . Ask the agent to use the documentation Try this request in your agent: Use the Shoalrun docs MCP to find how to configure analytics. Read the relevant documentation and give me the answer with source links. Inspect the agent's tool activity. It should call search_docs and follow a returned read instruction. Answers and links alone do not prove that it used MCP. What the tools do These tools only read published documentation. They cannot edit your files, change a project, or deploy a site. Tool Use search_docs Find relevant pages and suggested read instructions. get_page Read a Markdown page by its stable document ID. get_outline List a page's sections and their exact IDs. get_section Read one section by page ID and section ID. Use IDs returned by the tools rather than guessing them from a page title or URL. When a tool says the result does not fit its token budget, retry with the recommended maxTokens value. Do not treat an incomplete response as the complete documentation. If the connection fails Check that your client supports remote HTTP MCP and that the URL ends in /mcp . A client that only launches local stdio commands cannot connect directly to this URL. If tools are missing after saving, reconnect the server or restart the client. If the client insists on an API key or OAuth login, check that you selected an unauthenticated remote connection. This endpoint does not provide an OAuth login. This site's MCP analytics measures tool usage, available harness/model labels, and fixed intent categories. It excludes raw queries, free-text intent, returned content, and request headers. Session grouping uses pseudonymous IDs. Hosting access logs are separate; see the analytics safeguards . No private test settings are needed to use the tools or supply supported metadata. Missing or unrecognized labels remain absent; the server does not guess them. Related reading Next steps Connect an MCP client — Host the same documentation tools for your own project. Related topics Agent-friendly documentation — Understand the Markdown and discovery outputs behind the tools.

documents.title: Content negotiation
documents.summary: Understand content negotiation, why it helps agents, and what a hosting provider needs to do.

headings.title: What Shoalrun builds and what the host does
What if the host cannot negotiate?

documents.text: Shoalrun builds two versions of every published page from one authored source. The HTML version is for people using a browser. The generated Markdown version contains shared material in a form agents can read directly. Authors can also add or suppress format-specific content in either version. The versions share a core but need not contain identical text. Content negotiation lets a visitor ask for a format at the page's usual URL. Some agents send the request header Accept: text/markdown . A host that supports negotiation responds with Shoalrun's Markdown version. A browser asking for HTML gets the HTML version. The URL stays the same: Request to /publish/output/ Response Browser sends Accept: text/html HTML page, Content-Type: text/html Agent sends Accept: text/markdown Markdown page, Content-Type: text/markdown Accept says what the visitor can use. Content-Type says what the host actually returned. The .md URL, such as /publish/output.md , also works directly. Why this matters An agent reading HTML may receive navigation, styles, scripts, and interactive controls along with the article. It may then have to extract the useful content or convert the HTML to Markdown. Shoalrun's generated Markdown gives it the article directly, including material inside tabs and collapsibles and resolved OpenAPI examples. This can make the page easier to retrieve and less likely to lose content during conversion. AFDocs checks both .md URLs and content negotiation for this reason. The direct .md links in each HTML page and /llms.txt help agents that know to follow them. Negotiation helps an agent that arrives at the ordinary page URL and requests Markdown without first discovering a second URL. It does not require writers to maintain a separate article. What Shoalrun builds and what the host does Shoalrun creates the HTML page, its .md twin, and a /documents.json manifest listing both URLs. It also writes /resource-headers.json with content types for Markdown and discovery files. The host receives each HTTP request. It must read Accept and select the right built file. Providers use different names for this step: a server handler, a routing rule, or an edge function. The HTTP behavior is the same. A static file alone cannot read a request header. Shoalrun's Node server handles this. The standalone Vercel build generates Vercel rules. On another host, use the contract below to configure its routing feature. The host adapter guide covers adding Shoalrun's files to another build. Hosting contract For each published page, use the two URLs in documents.json . Configure the host as follows: At the page URL, return the Markdown twin when Accept explicitly requests text/markdown with a nonzero quality value. Otherwise return HTML. Keep the URL in the browser unchanged when serving the twin. Use an internal rewrite or server response, not a redirect to .md . On the Markdown response, set Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8 , Vary: Accept , and Content-Location to the .md URL. On both page responses, set Link: <PAGE.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown" . Keep the HTML document's existing alternate link as well. Serve direct .md URLs as text/markdown . Apply the content types in /resource-headers.json to discovery files, especially /.well-known/api-catalog when it is published. Limit the negotiation rule to published documentation pages. Leave assets, API contracts, and /llms.txt alone. Missing routes use the error responses described below.
