documents.text: Use ingredients when several recipes share instructions you want to maintain in one place. This guide follows Shoalrun's Build and audit this documentation site recipe from its source files to its published page. If you only need one task page, you can write a type: recipe page directly. Ingredients and the draft assembler are optional. Start with how the pieces fit for the distinction between authoring a recipe and choosing one in a cookbook. The built-in recipe , ingredient , and cookbook scaffolds are available in any project without registering templates. For example: shoalrun scaffold ingredient -n content/lookup-parcel.mdx shoalrun scaffold recipe -n content/track-parcel.mdx See templates for their outlines and project overrides. 1. Write one reusable step An ingredient is an MDX file with type: ingredient . Its body contains the instructions to reuse. This is a shortened version of docs/content/ingredient-build-site.mdx : docs/content/ingredient-build-site.mdx --- id : ingredient.build-site title : Build the Shoalrun docs site summary : Compile authored documentation into local HTML and Markdown. type : ingredient slug : /ingredients/build-site channel : production version : current language : en access : { policy : public } workflow : inputs : frameworkCli : The CLI compiled from this checkout. outputs : builtSite : The successful site build at docs/dist. prerequisites : - Run commands from the Shoalrun repository root. check : "The build reports status: ok." --- Use the compiled CLI to build the documentation: ``` sh node framework/dist/cli.js build docs/docs.config.yaml docs/dist ``` If the build fails, fix the named source or configuration issue and rerun it. The workflow fields describe the step: Field Meaning inputs Names and descriptions of values or artifacts that must already be available. Here, an earlier step must provide frameworkCli . outputs Names and descriptions of what successful completion makes available to later steps. Here, builtSite means the successful output at docs/dist . prerequisites Setup instructions. The assembler includes identical strings once across the recipe. check An observable condition for the reader to evaluate before continuing. Required whenever workflow is present. These declarations do not run the command or create variables. The body tells the reader or agent what to do. The check tells them what result to inspect. The assembler checks names and order, so a typo such as builtDocs where the next step expects builtSite fails during assembly. An ingredient can be private draft source for a recipe, or a published page readers can inspect. It must have a literal YAML header and match the recipe's default channel, version, and language. Without workflow , the assembler copies its body without checking handoffs. 2. List the steps for one complete goal The recipe spec chooses the ingredients and their order. A shortened version of docs/recipe-specs/audit-docs.yaml is: docs/recipe-specs/audit-docs.yaml schemaVersion : 1 id : recipe.audit-docs title : Build and audit this documentation site summary : Build current documentation and run the configured audits. slug : /recipes/audit-docs inputs : repositoryCheckout : A local Shoalrun checkout with dependencies installed. DOC_ID : Set the stable ID of the page you want to check. ingredients : - ../content/ingredient-compile-framework.mdx - ../content/ingredient-build-site.mdx - ../content/ingredient-inspect-build.mdx - ../content/ingredient-audit-site.mdx outcome : The build succeeds, both page formats exist, and configured audits pass. Paths are relative to this spec file. The initial inputs are available before the first ingredient. The compile ingredient produces frameworkCli ; the build ingredient requires it and produces builtSite ; the artifact-check ingredient requires that build and DOC_ID . The assembler rejects a missing input, repeated output name, repeated ingredient ID, or publication mismatch. It does not choose an order for you or verify that an output has the described value. The outcome is the final check for the complete recipe; omitting it leaves a prompt for the author to complete. 3. Generate a draft and review it From this repository's root, compile the CLI and preview the draft using the existing spec: npm --prefix framework run build node framework/dist/cli.js recipe draft \ --config docs/docs.config.yaml \ --spec docs/recipe-specs/audit-docs.yaml \ --out /tmp/shoalrun-audit-recipe.mdx --check --check prints the proposed content and reports would-create , unchanged , or would-change . Remove --check to create the file. The write command refuses to overwrite an existing file; choose a new output path for a new candidate. The output is a complete MDX draft with setup, ordered ingredient bodies, handoff descriptions, per-step checks, and the final outcome. It also contains a draft notice and a review checklist. No model or API is called, and none of the recipe's commands are executed during generatio

documents.title: Preview semantic search in this checkout
documents.summary: Build the Shoalrun docs, index passages, and verify vector retrieval and lexical fallback locally.
documents.text: Build the Shoalrun docs, index passages, and verify vector retrieval and lexical fallback locally. Before you start repositoryCheckout : A Shoalrun checkout with dependencies installed. Run commands from its root with Node.js 22.12 or newer. embeddingCredentials : A shell-readable environment file at ~/.config/shoalrun/.env containing the key for the embedding provider configured under retrieval.embeddings . This site's current config uses Voyage; the key stays on the server. previewPort : Port 8770, available for the preview server. If occupied, use another port with the CLI and adjust the URL. Build and index the docs Use repositoryCheckout and embeddingCredentials from Before you start . npm run docs:build set -a ; . ~/.config/shoalrun/.env ; set +a npm run docs:index The build writes search-index.json . The index command sends documentation passages to the configured embedding provider and generates or reuses passage vectors. Each semantic query also calls the embedding provider. No chat model is needed for search. If indexing reports a missing key or provider error, check retrieval.embeddings and the environment file, then rerun indexing. The passage index guide explains digests and vector reuse. Save indexedSite : The successful site build and current passage index under docs/dist. Continue when: The build and index commands both succeed. Start the semantic endpoint Use indexedSite from Build and index the docs and previewPort from Before you start . npm run docs:search-preview Open http://127.0.0.1:8770/ . This command occupies the terminal. Restart it after rebuilding the passage index, because the local endpoint reads its files at startup. Vector results include only passages with current embeddings. Reindex after editing pages so semantic results include the changed passages. A literal configuration key or command flag can also recover one word-matching explanation, but this is not a substitute for refreshing vectors. The browser search provider first asks /__shoalrun/search . That endpoint ranks passages by embedding similarity and returns page or section links. Successful semantic queries keep their first two pages ranked by meaning. A question containing dotted configuration keys or command flags can include one exact-identifier prose explanation as the third result. Filenames and requests for fewer than three results keep semantic ranking. It does not call the chat model. If the endpoint has no current vectors, it returns lexical passage results. If the endpoint is missing, slow, or fails, the browser uses search-index.json for lexical page search. Save runningPreview : The local site and search endpoint while the server is running. Continue when: The homepage and its search box load. Verify the retrieval mode Use runningPreview from Start the semantic endpoint . Search for navigation , then describe a task in your own words without copying a page title or sentence. For example, ask about reusing warnings across documentation. Lexical search can now return partial matches for the sentence; returning a result alone does not prove semantic retrieval worked. In the browser Network inspector, inspect /__shoalrun/search . A successful response with "mode": "vector" confirms the endpoint used embeddings. "mode": "lexical" means the endpoint returned word-matching results. It can do this when current document vectors are missing, the embedding budget is exhausted, the provider fails, or the three-second deadline expires. The response mode alone does not tell you whether document vectors exist. A failed request followed by results demonstrates the browser provider's lexical fallback. For a preview without the endpoint, stop this server and run npm run docs:preview . Save modeEvidence : The response mode and relevant page or section links for the queries. Continue when: You can identify the active retrieval mode and open a relevant result. Check the outcome The indexed site serves local search, results open relevant documentation, and the Network inspector distinguishes vector retrieval from the lexical endpoint or browser fallback. Press Ctrl+C to stop the server. Related reading Next steps Passage index — Understand passage digests, embedding input, and vector reuse. (Status: experimental.)

documents.text:
Use this path to check request acceptance. For delivery status and failure handling, follow the complete delivery recipe . Before you start Start the local simulation from the Shoalrun repository root in a separate terminal: node framework/example-configs/notifications/demo.mjs Keep it running. Have cURL and Node.js available, and use a scratch directory for queued.json ; the command replaces that file. The demo sends no email. documents.title: Understand ingredients, recipes, and cookbooks
documents.summary: See how reusable source instructions become complete recipe pages that a cookbook helps readers choose.
documents.text: A recipe is the complete page someone follows to finish a task. An ingredient is a reusable piece of source documentation used to write that page. A cookbook is a page that helps readers choose a recipe. Readers can open a recipe directly. Ingredients help authors maintain instructions shared by several recipes. A cookbook becomes useful when readers need help choosing which complete task to follow. Use recipes for task-oriented how-tos Use the built-in how-to template for a task page, or recipe when the page should participate in Shoalrun's recipe and cookbook features. Both take a reader from a known starting state to a verifiable result. Give it prerequisites, ordered actions, failure guidance, and a final success check. A recipe can be a short, directly authored page; it does not require ingredients, a YAML composition spec, or a cookbook. Use the built-in explanation template to explain a concept or help readers understand a system. Use a reference page to describe fields, commands, or API behavior. Existing how-tos can keep their current type, stable ID, and route until a deliberate content revision calls for a change. A page's type does not prove its instructions have been tested. Writing task Starting format Build this site and verify its output A recipe. Explain how the compiler produces HTML and Markdown An explanation page. Look up CLI flags or configuration fields A reference page. Reuse the same build instructions across several recipes An ingredient included by those recipes. Help a reader choose build, audit, or preview A cookbook pointing to complete recipes. The bundled shoalrun-recipes skill follows these choices. See use the agent skills for a copyable authoring request. One example from Shoalrun Suppose you need two sets of instructions: Build and check a page. Compile the CLI, build the docs, and check the HTML and Markdown files. Build and audit the site. Do those same three steps, then run the project audits. Both recipes need the same build instructions. We keep those instructions in ingredient files and use them in both recipe specs: copied into draft copied into draft added to draft Shared ingredients Compile CLI → Build docs → Check artifacts Audit ingredient Run project audits Recipe page Build and check a page Recipe page Build and audit the site Two recipes reuse the same source instructions — The compile, build, and artifact-check ingredients are used in both recipes. The build-and-audit recipe also includes the audit ingredient. These arrows describe authoring reuse; they do not run commands. The Site workflows cookbook offers these two finished recipes. Choosing the audit path displays all four steps. The reader does not have to find or assemble the ingredients. What each file does These are real files in this checkout: File What the author puts there What it contributes docs/content/ingredient-build-site.mdx The build command, explanation, required inputs, expected outputs, and a success check. Reusable source instructions for one step. docs/recipe-specs/audit-docs.yaml An ordered list of ingredient files, starting inputs, and the final goal. Instructions to the recipe assembler about which steps to copy and how to order them. docs/content/recipe-audit-docs.mdx The assembled, reviewed recipe. The complete page a person or agent follows. docs/config/cookbooks.yaml Choice labels and the published recipe ID for each option. The chooser's options and descriptions. docs/content/cookbook-site-workflows.mdx An introduction and <CookbookChooser id="site-checks" /> . The page where readers choose their task. What happens, and when An author prepares ingredients and a recipe spec. Ingredients contain prose and commands. Their optional workflow metadata names the values or artifacts each step needs and produces. The author runs recipe draft . The assembler copies ingredient bodies into a new MDX draft, combines identical prerequisites, and writes the declared handoffs and checks. It checks that each named input is available from setup or an earlier step. The author reviews and tests the recipe, then publishes it. A normal site build turns the recipe page into HTML and Markdown. It also builds the cookbook page and its choice list. A reader chooses a recipe in the cookbook. The browser fetches the already-published recipe and displays its instructions. The reader or their agent runs the commands and checks the results. Selecting a cookbook option does not assemble ingredients or run a task. It loads finished recipe content. The cookbook's own introduction and choice descriptions come from its page and configuration. What changing an ingredient updates A generated recipe is a snapshot of its ingredients. Editing an ingredient does not immediately change a published recipe. Regenerate the affected recipe, review the changes, and rebuild the site. Shoalrun's five repository recipes have a maintenance script that updates their snapshots together and a test that detects stale snapshots

documents.title: Related reading
documents.summary: Relationship fields, purposes, ordering, validation, and rendered reading paths.
documents.text: A relationship is an authored connection between two pages, with a reason to follow the link. Use related reading for prerequisites, next steps, references, and distinctions that help readers choose where to go. The links use stable document IDs and remain in the current publication. For curated cards and filtered collections, see cards and collections . Declare relationships A relationship is an explicit connection between two pages, with a reason to follow the link. For example, a guide can point to the task readers should do next, a prerequisite they should read first, or a useful reference. These connections express your intended reading path; sidebar position and shared operation IDs do not establish that order. Keep the connections in a central config fragment so pages can display them without repeating the target IDs and reasons in their content: docs.config.yaml relationships : { $include : ./config/relationships.yaml } config/relationships.yaml - id : cards-to-output from : guide.related-reading to : guide.output type : next-step reason : Inspect the HTML, Markdown, and manifests produced by the build. order : 10 Field Meaning id Unique relationship ID. from , to Stable document IDs. type A relationship purpose from the table below. reason Required text explaining why the target is useful. order Optional finite number; smaller values come first, with relationship ID as the tie-breaker. Default is 0 . Relationship types describe why a reader should follow the link: Type Purpose / default group heading Direction prerequisite Read first — knowledge needed before this page. From source to target. next-step Next steps — continue the workflow. From source to target. reference Reference while working — look up details. From source to target. advanced Go deeper — explore a more advanced topic. From source to target. see-also Related topics — parallel or complementary material. Both directions. not-confused-with Often confused with — distinguish two topics. Both directions. Declare symmetric pairs only once and write a reason that makes sense from either page. For not-confused-with , explain the actual distinction in the reason. A prerequisite target is something to read before the source. Unknown document IDs, self-links, duplicate IDs, duplicate edges of the same type, and prerequisite cycles within a public publication fail. Different relationship types can connect the same pair. Next-step cycles are allowed for workflows with a return step; provide meaningful reasons. A relationship is published only where both documents have public variants in the same channel, version, and language. Edges to drafts or unavailable variants are omitted from related reading and the public manifest. A relationship does not publish its target or create a cross-version link. Display related documents Related reading presents centrally maintained connections as lists of links grouped by purpose. Cards are a visual presentation for page previews. The same relationship data can drive either presentation; declaring a relationship does not require a card. Place this under a level-two heading where related reading belongs: ## Related reading < RelatedReading /> This renders nonempty groups in the order shown in the relationship-type table, with level-three headings. Within each group, links follow order , then relationship ID. Each list item uses the target's page title and the relationship reason. Card titles, descriptions, eyebrows, and icons do not change the default link list. Subject lifecycle status remains visible. Titles and URLs come from the target page; maintain only IDs, relationship purposes, and reasons in the central mapping. To show one kind of relationship under your own heading: ## Next steps < RelatedReading relation = "next-step" /> For optional cards, change the presentation: < RelatedReading relation = "next-step" layout = "cards" /> The RelatedReading component page lists every attribute. <DocCards relation="next-step" /> remains supported as an explicit card view; DocCards also supports curated docs arrays. RelatedReading accepts relationship queries only. Reading paths in section Markdown A section resource carries the prerequisites and next steps shown in a top-level <RelatedReading /> view for that page, even when the view appears under a different heading. The added Page reading path block names its page-wide scope and retains target titles, reasons, status labels, and Markdown links. Prerequisites come before next steps; each group keeps its configured order. These are authored suggestions, not an inferred linear sequence or proof that prerequisites have been satisfied. Links already present in the section or repeated page introduction are not copied again. Both list and card views supply the same concise reading-path links. The compiler does not carry other relationship types, views for another relatedTo page, or views nested inside tabs, reader sections, or other components

documents.title: Write release notes and changelog entries
documents.summary: Write flexible release summaries and changelog entries identified by date or version.
documents.text: Release notes and changelog entries serve different reading needs. A release note summarizes a named release, quarter, or other period. A changelog entry records a change identified by date, release version, or both. Both are ordinary Markdown or MDX pages with HTML and Markdown outputs and stable IDs. Write a release note Use type: release-note . Its title and content define the scope; neither a date nor a release version is required. This example covers a quarter without claiming one publication day: content/releases/q3-summary.mdx --- id : release.q3-summary title : Q3 2026 summary summary : Changes grouped for the quarter. type : release-note slug : /releases/q3-summary channel : production version : current access : { policy : public } --- channel and version must name an enabled publication, or come from global frontmatter . A note for one release can instead use releaseVersion: "2.4" and a version in its title. releaseVersion identifies the product release; the ordinary version field selects a documentation publication. The two fields are independent. Add date only when the note has a meaningful publication date. Write a changelog entry Use type: changelog-entry and identify the change with date , releaseVersion , or both. The project sets which field is required. The default accepts either. A date must be a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date; a release version must be nonempty text. content/changelog/example.mdx --- id : change.example title : Example change summary : A short description of the change. type : changelog-entry date : 2026-09-24 slug : /changelog/example channel : production version : current access : { policy : public } tags : [ api-reference ] --- The build shows supplied dates and release versions on pages and cards, and includes them in Markdown twins. Dated changelog entries show their publication date without a separate Updated label in the page header or Markdown body. Revision dates remain in the document manifest and configured Markdown metadata. This site's Markdown metadata also projects the date and release version when present. Set the identifier rule Configure frontmatter.changelogIdentifier in project config: docs.config.yaml frontmatter : changelogIdentifier : either Value Required on each changelog entry either A date, a release version, or both. Default. date A date. A release version is optional. version A release version. A date is optional. This rule does not apply to release notes. It also does not change the documentation publication's version axis. Describe what changed On a changelog-entry , add an optional change block to distinguish an editorial correction from a changed procedure or behavior. This fictional example describes a breaking API change: change : kind : breaking affects : [ reference.create-payment , guide.create-payment ] migration : guide.migrate-payments Replace these IDs with public pages in the entry's channel, version, and language. Use stable IDs without the doc: prefix. Targets resolve to their current titles and URLs. Missing, draft, self, and other-publication targets fail the build; external URLs and references to removed pages are not supported in this increment. Field Required Meaning kind Yes One author-declared classification from the table below. affects Yes Nonempty list of unique document IDs that describe the affected subjects or instructions. Order is preserved. migration No Document ID of the guide explaining how to adapt. Kind Use when editorial Correcting wording or presentation without changing the documented instructions or behavior. procedure Changing instructions, setup steps, or a recommended workflow. behavior Describing a feature or behavior change that the author has not classified as breaking. breaking Existing clients or workflows need adaptation because of the change. Choose the kind deliberately and explain scope and limitations in the entry body. behavior is not a compiler guarantee of compatibility. A missing migration link does not mean migration is unnecessary. When one release contains several distinct changes, agree on the grouping before drafting: one combined entry with clearly scoped sections, or separate entries collected in a release note. Use one change classification only when it accurately describes the combined entry; otherwise leave the entry unclassified and explain each change in its body. change is page-specific: global defaults and enforced metadata cannot set it. It is accepted only on changelog-entry pages, not release summaries or ordinary guides. Unknown keys fail. Use the entry's existing date and releaseVersion fields for its date and release label; this block does not add an effective-date schedule or prove deployment. HTML, full Markdown, and every published section of the entry show an Authored change notice with the kind, affected pages, and migration link when supplied. HTML links open pages; Markdown links open their twins. The corresponding documents.json record includes change.kind , r

Write a release note Use type: release-note . Its title and content define the scope; neither a date nor a release version is required. This example covers a quarter without claiming one publication day: --- id: release.q3-summary title: Q3 2026 summary summary: Changes grouped for the quarter. type: release-note slug: /releases/q3-summary channel: production version: current access: { policy: public } --- channel and version must name an enabled publication, or come from global frontmatter . A note for one release can instead use releaseVersion: "2.4" and a version in its title. releaseVersion identifies the product release; the ordinary version field selects a documentation publication. The two fields are independent. Add date only when the note has a meaningful publication date. Write a changelog entry Use type: changelog-entry and identify the change with date , releaseVersion , or both. The project sets which field is required. The default accepts either. A date must be a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date; a release version must be nonempty text. --- id: change.example title: Example change summary: A short description of the change. type: changelog-entry date: 2026-09-24 slug: /changelog/example channel: production version: current access: { policy: public } tags: [api-reference] --- The build shows supplied dates and release versions on pages and cards, and includes them in Markdown twins. Dated changelog entries show their publication date without a separate Updated label in the page header or Markdown body. Revision dates remain in the document manifest and configured Markdown metadata. This site's Markdown metadata also projects the date and release version when present. Set the identifier rule Configure frontmatter.changelogIdentifier in project config: frontmatter: changelogIdentifier: either Value Required on each changelog entry either A date, a release version, or both. Default. date A date. A release version is optional. version A release version. A date is optional. This rule does not apply to release notes. It also does not change the documentation publication's version axis. Describe what changed On a changelog-entry , add an optional change block to distinguish an editorial correction from a changed procedure or behavior. This fictional example describes a breaking API change: change: kind: breaking affects: [reference.create-payment, guide.create-payment] migration: guide.migrate-payments Replace these IDs with public pages in the entry's channel, version, and language. Use stable IDs without the doc: prefix. Targets resolve to their current titles and URLs. Missing, draft, self, and other-publication targets fail the build; external URLs and references to removed pages are not supported in this increment. Field Required Meaning kind Yes One author-declared classification from the table below. affects Yes Nonempty list of unique document IDs that describe the affected subjects or instructions. Order is preserved. migration No Document ID of the guide explaining how to adapt. Kind Use when editorial Correcting wording or presentation without changing the documented instructions or behavior. procedure Changing instructions, setup steps, or a recommended workflow. behavior Describing a feature or behavior change that the author has not classified as breaking. breaking Existing clients or workflows need adaptation because of the change. Choose the kind deliberately and explain scope and limitations in the entry body. behavior is not a compiler guarantee of compatibility. A missing migration link does not mean migration is unnecessary. When one release contains several distinct changes, agree on the grouping before drafting: one combined entry with clearly scoped sections, or separate entries collected in a release note. Use one change classification only when it accurately describes the combined entry; otherwise leave the entry unclassified and explain each change in its body. change is page-specific: global defaults and enforced metadata cannot set it. It is accepted only on changelog-entry pages, not release summaries or ordinary guides. Unknown keys fail. Use the entry's existing date and releaseVersion fields for its date and release label; this block does not add an effective-date schedule or prove deployment. HTML, full Markdown, and every published section of the entry show an Authored change notice with the kind, affected pages, and migration link when supplied. HTML links open pages; Markdown links open their twins. The corresponding documents.json record includes change.kind , resolved change.affects targets, and optional change.migration . Each target has id , title , url , and markdow

documents.title: Use Git branches for separate docs sites
documents.summary: Build a chosen Git branch for each docs address, add links between sites, and verify the deployed commit.

headings.title: Add another site to the Version menu

documents.text: A deployment takes the docs files from a Git branch or commit, builds them, and serves the result at an address you choose. Your host or CI service chooses the source and destination. Branch names have no special meaning to Shoalrun. For example, either of these mappings can work: Workflow Source Docs address Sandbox and production sandbox sandbox-docs.example.com Sandbox and production main docs.example.com Next and stable next next-docs.example.com Next and stable stable docs.example.com You can use another branch name, a tag, or a fixed commit. You can also use path-based versions within one build instead of separate sites. Branches choose which files to build ; publications choose which editions those files produce . Build and deploy each source Set site.origin in each site's config to its public HTTPS origin. A site at next-docs.example.com , for example, uses site.origin: https://next-docs.example.com . Commit the pages, API sources, and publication settings for that site. After the deployment job checks out its chosen source, build it with the full commit hash: shoalrun build docs.config.yaml site-dist --source-commit "$( git rev-parse HEAD )" Deploy all of site-dist/ to the address assigned to that source. Configure this source-to-address rule in your host or CI service; Shoalrun does not deploy files or infer a branch from channel . See deploy your documentation for hosting options. If two separate domains should both serve /start , use an empty channel pathPrefix in each site's config. Add another site to the Version menu Add an external site when readers should be able to move between addresses. In the current site's publications section, keep its existing defaults , channels , versions , and enabled entries, and add: docs.config.yaml (fragment) publications : externalSites : - label : Next docs baseUrl : https://next-docs.example.com This adds Next docs to the Version menu on every page. The link opens that site's root. Add the corresponding link in the other site's config if readers should be able to switch back. baseUrl can be another domain or an address with a path, such as https://docs.example.com/next/ . To keep a reader on the matching page , provide a local snapshot of the other site's built documents.json : docs.config.yaml (fragment) publications : externalSites : - label : Next docs baseUrl : https://next-docs.example.com manifest : ./config/next-documents.json Shoalrun matches stable document IDs and uses the other site's published paths. Only pages in that manifest appear in the menu. Copy or refresh the manifest as part of your release process when pages change. This extra step is optional; the direct site link above is enough for a simple branch switcher. A baseUrl with a path changes where the menu points. Hosting a whole standalone build under a path also requires the host to handle Shoalrun's root-level assets and discovery files. Path prefixes inside one build already work without that hosting setup. What agents receive Each deployed site has its own Markdown pages, documents.json , search index, and agent discovery files, built from that site's selected Git revision. An agent using the stable site reads its stable artifacts; an agent using the next site reads its next artifacts. The external Version menu helps human readers navigate between sites, but it does not combine their manifests or Markdown copies. Preserve a built release or its tagged source if agents must be able to consult it later. See published outputs for the file list. Check the deployed source Each build writes its source commit to /build-info.json . Run the post-deploy checker with the full hash selected by that site's deployment job: npm --prefix framework run deploy:check -- https://next-docs.example.com/ --source-commit "$DEPLOYED_COMMIT" The checker fails if the address serves a different commit or if its published HTML and Markdown routes fail their HTTP checks. Run it for each site. For a durable release record, tag the source commit and retain the built output with /build-info.json ; a branch moves as new commits arrive. Related reading Read first How Shoalrun works — Understand publications, channels, and versions. Next steps Check a deployed site — Check each deployed revision before you release it. Related topics Share pages across documentation versions — Distinguish content editions from source revisions and retained builds. Often confused with Write release notes and changelog entries — Release notes tell readers what changed; release revisions choose which Git revision of the docs to build and deploy.

documents.title: How documentation answers work
documents.summary: Understand how passages, embeddings, scoring, and a chat model produce cited answers.
documents.text: Documentation chat reads a site you have already built. It is optional: a normal shoalrun build does not call the retrieval or chat providers. Chat first finds relevant passages, then uses them to produce a cited answer. A passage is a short part of a built Markdown page with a link back to its source. Some configurations can return an existing answer or an excerpt instead of generating new text. For commands, start with local chat setup . Search and chat compares chat with the page-search box. How the layers fit Each layer adds a retrieval or answer capability and has its own prerequisites. Layer What it adds It needs Keyword matching Finds the most relevant passages by their words. It is what the chat uses when there are no vectors, or the embedding service is unavailable. The passage index. No key. Semantic search Finds passages by meaning, so a question matches even when it shares no words with the page. An embedding service and key. Relevance scorer Reorders the results and declines a question the docs don't cover. It checks each sentence of an answer, and shows a passage word for word when one is clearly the answer. A scorer service that speaks the Jev protocol. Chat model Writes a cited answer from the best passages. A chat service and key. Hosting Runs the chat beside your site with spending caps and an off switch. Vercel, and a key-value store. The site-search box returns links from its own page index. Chat retrieves passages to answer a question. An embedding service helps match different wording; a scorer rates whether the passages support an answer. The settings reference describes supported providers and the Jev scoring protocol. Choose services and models in config. Keep their keys in the environment variables named by that config. How a question is answered The diagram shows a chat with optional reuse and scoring enabled. A question stops at an existing answer or direct excerpt when the configured checks accept one. asked before new question docs do not cover it one clear winner anything else flagged: ask a second model passes Question Cached answer or answer card Find passages by keyword, and by meaning if set up Answer Relevance scorer decides Not covered List the closest pages One clear passage Show it word for word Chat model Write a cited answer Check citations, code, and claims How a question is answered — A question first looks for a cached answer or an answer card. Otherwise passages are found by keyword and meaning, and the relevance scorer decides. A question the docs don't cover gets a list of pages. One clear passage is shown as an excerpt. Everything else goes to the chat model, whose answer is checked before it is shown. The minimal setup uses keyword retrieval, a chat model, and citation and code checks. Caching, answer cards, scoring, and claim verification need extra configuration. Without a scorer, there is no score-based coverage gate. For an explicit request with up to three action clauses, retrieval can find evidence for each part and include page introductions. This helps keep one topic from filling the passage budget. Answer checks explains that behavior and its limits. Put the model into practice Add optional layers after testing the minimal setup with questions your readers actually ask. Check source coverage and response quality before choosing scoring thresholds or enabling answer reuse. Use set up local documentation chat for commands and verification. The retrieval and chat settings define provider fields and defaults. Passage index describes the files used by retrieval. Related reading Next steps Passage index — See how a built site is split into passages and embedded. (Status: experimental.) Check and speed up answers — Decline questions the docs don't cover and check what the model writes. (Status: experimental.) Host and limit documentation chat — Run the chat beside your site with spending caps and an off switch. (Status: experimental.) Reference while working CLI reference — Look up the index, ask, answers, ask-log, chat, and serve commands. Retrieval and chat settings — Look up every retrieval and chat setting. (Status: experimental.) Related topics Set up local documentation chat — Understand the layers behind cited answers before choosing additional services. (Status: experimental.) Site search — Use retrieved passages to produce cited answers instead of page links.

documents.title: Search and chat
documents.summary: Choose page search, meaning-based search, or cited answers for your documentation.

headings.title: Which index does each feature use?
When an optional service is unavailable

documents.text: Start with site search if readers need links to pages and sections. It is built in, works on a static host, and needs no provider account. Add chat when readers need answers written from your documentation. Choose the result you want These features have different setup and hosting needs. Passage retrieval and chat are experimental. Reader needs Feature Requirements Page and section links Site search A normal site build and a browser with JavaScript. Links that can match different wording Semantic search preview A passage index, embeddings, and a local search endpoint. The provider can fall back to keyword search. An answer with source citations Documentation chat A passage index, a configured chat service, and a terminal or server. Embeddings and a scorer are optional additions. The sidebar's navigation filter only narrows the menu. Its search words do not change site-search results. The search dropdown returns links; it does not call a chat model. Start with a local chat Follow Set up local documentation chat to configure a service, index your pages, and inspect an answer with sources. Once that works, choose the next capability you need: Answer checks explain coverage, citations, code checks, and answer reuse. Answer cards prepare reviewed answers to recurring questions. Hosting adds a Vercel function, shared limits, and an off switch. Settings define the provider fields and optional layers. Which index does each feature use? Shoalrun keeps page search and passage retrieval separate. File Created by Used for search-index.json The normal site build when search indexing is enabled. Browser page search and local documentation search. Contains titles, summaries, headings, and text excerpts. ai/chunks.json shoalrun index after the build. Passage retrieval for semantic search and chat. Contains text from built Markdown pages, with source links. ai/embeddings.json and .bin shoalrun index --embed Comparing the meaning of queries and passages. Requires an embedding provider. An embedding represents text as numbers. Keyword, or lexical , retrieval compares words. Semantic retrieval compares embeddings; hybrid retrieval combines word-based and meaning-based rankings. Neither requires a chat model just to return search links. The passage reference describes these files in detail. The glossary defines the related terms. When an optional service is unavailable Fallback behavior depends on the configured feature. Situation Result Built-in search has no server or provider key Browser keyword search still works. This site's custom search provider cannot reach its endpoint It uses the browser keyword index. A search endpoint has no current vectors, or embeddings fail It returns keyword passage results. Chat has no current vectors Retrieval uses keywords. A configured chat model can still write an answer. A deployment has no chat function The site remains available, but has no chat endpoint. A Vercel build with --chat includes search and answer endpoints. Semantic queries have shared rate and daily limits. When the embedding budget is exhausted, search returns keyword results. A static deployment can use browser search without those endpoints. Related reading Next steps How documentation answers work — Turn passage retrieval into cited answers. (Status: experimental.) Site search — Configure the masthead box, its provider, and searchable index fields. Reference while working Glossary — Look up the search and retrieval terms used in this section. Passage index — Compare the page index with the passage and vector files. (Status: experimental.)

documents.title: Site search
documents.summary: Search settings, keyboard behavior, provider interfaces, and index fields.

headings.title: Read a search result with an agent

documents.text: Site search returns links to pages and sections. It is enabled by default and matches words in the browser, with no provider account or server required. Shoalrun supplies the search box and keyboard controls. A search provider supplies results; you can replace the built-in provider with your own module. Search and chat explains when to add semantic search or cited answers. Choose a provider Set the provider under outputs.html.search : docs.config.yaml outputs : html : search : provider : lexical Provider Behavior lexical The default. Builds /search-index.json and matches it in the browser. custom Loads your browser module. Needs module ; index is optional. none Removes the search box. Writes no index or provider file. The build copies the provider module to /assets/search-provider.js . The search box imports that file when a reader first focuses the box or types. Use the search box Press / or Ctrl + K ( ⌘ + K on macOS) to focus the box. Use the arrow keys to move through results, Enter to open one, and Escape to close the list. When a match falls inside a section, the result names the section and links to its heading. The box needs JavaScript. Without it, both the search box and sidebar filter stay hidden; the published navigation links still work. Lexical search The built-in provider matches words rather than meaning. It lowercases the query and recognizes phrases declared in search.synonyms . The browser provider ranks matches in this order: Pages containing every query term or its mapped synonym. If none match completely, partial results ordered by matched term count, then field score. Common filler words such as “how,” “do,” and “the” do not count toward partial-match coverage. A partial result must match at least one remaining term. This helps sentence-shaped queries but does not infer meaning or handle typos and general stemming. The local search command shares the base index and weights, with additional CLI/MCP ranking rules described below. Synonyms Projects can define their own synonym groups of words and phrases. Put them in a YAML file and include it from the site config: docs.config.yaml search : synonyms : { $include : ./config/search-synonyms.yaml } The included file lists equivalent words or phrases: config/search-synonyms.yaml - [ walkthrough , "walk through" , "code tutorial" , tutorial ] Each group works in both directions. Exact word or phrase matches rank above synonym matches. A term can belong to only one group; groups need at least two distinct terms. Phrase matching respects word boundaries, so walk through is treated as one term. Shoalrun validates the file during config loading and includes its mapping in /search-index.json and ai/chunks.json . Browser search, shoalrun search , and lexical passage retrieval for chat share that vocabulary. Rebuild the site and passage index after editing the file. Custom search providers must read the mapping from /search-index.json if they want to apply it to their own results. Result ordering and limits Pages rank by where the terms appear: Title, highest when the title starts with the term. Summary. Section headings. Body text. The built-in lexical provider returns at most one result per page. It adds a section link when every query term matches one section heading and the query is not already a title match. With a reader view selected, it returns page links because the unfiltered heading list may include hidden sections. Custom providers can return multiple section results from the same page. The list shows the top eight results. The provider downloads the index once, on first focus, and searches only pages in the reader's channel, version, and language. When reader views are configured, it also excludes pages and marked section text outside the selected view. The local CLI search command reads the full index and does not apply a browser's saved view. The navigation sidebar has a separate filter. Its optional node-level search terms help readers find menu items; they do not change /search-index.json or masthead results. See Organize site navigation . Hosted semantic search limits Shoalrun's hosted search endpoint accepts site-specific limits, separate from the Ask budget: docs.config.yaml search : limits : perCallerPerDay : 100 perDay : 1000 perCallerPerMinute : 10 These are the defaults. Each value must be a positive whole number. They apply to Shoalrun's hosted semantic search handler; the built-in browser keyword provider and third-party search services manage their own limits. The Vercel adapter wires these settings into the generated search function when hosted search is included in the build. Configure the embedding provider and shared Redis/KV credentials in the hosting environment. See Publish on Vercel . Other hosting platforms need an adapter that runs Shoalrun's hosted search handler, passes the site's settings, and connects the shared counter store. Shoalrun does not automatically apply these limits to another host or a customer's se

Put them in a YAML file and include it from the site config: search: synonyms: { $include: ./config/search-synonyms.yaml } The included file lists equivalent words or phrases: - [walkthrough, "walk through", "code tutorial", tutorial] Each group works in both directions. Exact word or phrase matches rank above synonym matches. A term can belong to only one group; groups need at least two distinct terms. Phrase matching respects word boundaries, so walk through is treated as one term. Shoalrun validates the file during config loading and includes its mapping in /search-index.json and ai/chunks.json . Browser search, shoalrun search , and lexical passage retrieval for chat share that vocabulary. Rebuild the site and passage index after editing the file. Custom search providers must read the mapping from /search-index.json if they want to apply it to their own results. Result ordering and limits Pages rank by where the terms appear: Title, highest when the title starts with the term. Summary. Section headings. Body text. The built-in lexical provider returns at most one result per page. It adds a section link when every query term matches one section heading and the query is not already a title match. With a reader view selected, it returns page links because the unfiltered heading list may include hidden sections. Custom providers can return multiple section results from the same page. The list shows the top eight results. The provider downloads the index once, on first focus, and searches only pages in the reader's channel, version, and language. When reader views are configured, it also excludes pages and marked section text outside the selected view. The local CLI search command reads the full index and does not apply a browser's saved view. The navigation sidebar has a separate filter. Its optional node-level search terms help readers find menu items; they do not change /search-index.json or masthead results. See Organize site navigation . Hosted semantic search limits Shoalrun's hosted search endpoint accepts site-specific limits, separate from the Ask budget: search: limits: perCallerPerDay: 100 perDay: 1000 perCallerPerMinute: 10 These are the defaults. Each value must be a positive whole number. They apply to Shoalrun's hosted semantic search handler; the built-in browser keyword provider and third-party search services manage their own limits. The Vercel adapter wires these settings into the generated search function when hosted search is included in the build. Configure the embedding provider and shared Redis/KV credentials in the hosting environment. See Publish on Vercel . Other hosting platforms need an adapter that runs Shoalrun's hosted search handler, passes the site's settings, and connects the shared counter store. Shoalrun does not automatically apply these limits to another host or a customer's search service. A static-only deployment can use the built-in browser keyword provider without a s

Preview semantic search in this checkout — Build the passage index and verify hybrid search and lexical fallback in this checkout. Header links — The search box sits in the site header, before your header links. How documentation answers work — Use retrieved passages to produce cited answers instead of page links. (Status: experimental.)

documents.title: SEO and social previews
documents.summary: Give each page a useful title and summary, generate share cards, and verify public preview URLs.

headings.title: Write the page title and summary
Derive revision dates from content changes

documents.text: When someone shares a docs link, Slack and other services fetch the page's HTML and look for a title, description, and image. Shoalrun writes these tags at build time from page metadata and can generate a share image for every page. Start with a clear page title and a one-sentence summary ; you do not need to hand-write Open Graph or Twitter tags. Set the public address Put the address readers actually use in site.origin . This is where crawlers will fetch the page and its image: docs.config.yaml site : title : Acme API docs origin : https://docs.acme.com Check the domain in the built og:image URL. A page may display in a browser while its social preview cannot load an image from that domain. Preview deployments behind sign-in cannot be unfurled by a public crawler. Publish on Vercel explains the production and preview origins for this site's build. Write the page title and summary content/start.mdx (frontmatter) title : Getting started summary : Create your first project and make a request. The title becomes the page heading and browser title. The summary is the default preview description and appears on the generated share image. For short titles, Shoalrun adds site.title to the Open Graph and Twitter titles when the result fits within 70 characters. The browser title and page heading remain unchanged. If a page needs a different browser and social title, or a different description, use seo.title and seo.description in its frontmatter : seo : title : Getting started with Acme API description : Create a project, choose a credential, and make your first request. seo.title sets the exact browser and social title; it skips the automatic site-name suffix. seo.description sets the browser and social description unless the page selects a separate displayText.socialCard . The generated image uses the same selected description, so its copy agrees with the tags. You can configure the text choices site-wide under outputs.text ; see text surfaces for precedence. What the build adds The build derives these metadata and discovery outputs from your site and page settings. Output Default source HTML <title> seo.title , then page title HTML name="description" seo.description , then configured HTML description og:title and twitter:title Browser title, with site.title added for short titles when it fits og:description and twitter:description Selected social description, falling back to the page summary og:url site.origin plus the published page route Canonical URL site.origin plus the published page route XML sitemap lastmod Page updated , then optional site.updated og:image and twitter:image Absolute URL of that page's share image twitter:card summary_large_image when a share image exists The default image is a 1200×630 PNG with the page type, title, summary, site name, and URL. Share images and favicon shows how to replace a page image or the site-wide design. Turning off share images removes image tags on pages without their own image. Check the deployed page Build and deploy, then run the deployment checker with the public origin: npm --prefix framework run deploy:check -- https://docs.acme.com/ It checks page responses, compares og:url and og:image with that origin, and fetches a share image. To inspect one page directly, view its HTML source and open the absolute og:image URL in a private browser window. On Vercel, the deployment's Open Graph tab can show a preview for Slack and other services. When site.origin is set, the build writes /sitemap.xml from public, indexable page routes and advertises it in /robots.txt . Every page gets a self-referencing canonical URL. A page with seo.noindex: true stays public, gets a noindex tag, and is omitted from the sitemap. Set site.indexing: false for a preview: every page gets noindex and the build omits the sitemap. Crawlers can still reach those pages to read noindex. Set updated in a page's frontmatter to the date of a meaningful content update, such as 2026-09-27 . A timezone-qualified ISO timestamp is also accepted. Shoalrun copies it to sitemap lastmod ; it never substitutes build time. site.updated is an optional date fallback for generated pages and other pages without updated . Change it only when the material it covers changes. Dates may repeat across pages when they really changed together. Without site.freshness , the build uses declared dates. It never reads file modification times to determine content updates. Derive revision dates from content changes Opt into a content-digest history: docs.config.yaml site : freshness : history : ./config/content-updates.json The history file must be inside the project and its parent directory must already exist. The first successful build seeds each page with its declared updated , then site.updated , then today's UTC date. Later builds compare the resolved HTML and Markdown content plus displayed page metadata. Unchanged content keeps its recorded Updated date; changed content receives today's UTC date. File touches, AST s

documents.title: Set up local documentation chat
documents.summary: Build a passage index, configure a chat service, and verify cited answers locally.

headings.title: Set up and try the chat
Ask a question from the terminal

documents.text: Set up a local chat panel, then check that its answers cite the right documentation. Start in the root of a Shoalrun project that already builds, with the CLI available in your terminal. You need a chat-service account and its API key. Meaning-based retrieval also needs an embedding provider and key. These commands make provider requests; they do not deploy your site. For keyword-only retrieval, omit retrieval from the example below and omit --embed from the indexing command. You still need the passage index and a chat service. Set up and try the chat This example uses Voyage for embeddings and an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint through OpenRouter. Choose providers and model IDs available to your accounts. Configure the providers Add these sections to docs.config.yaml . Store VOYAGE_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your terminal environment, not in the YAML file. docs.config.yaml retrieval : embeddings : provider : voyage model : voyage-4-large dimension : 1024 queryModel : voyage-4-lite chat : provider : openai model : deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash baseUrl : https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 keyEnv : OPENROUTER_API_KEY Build and index the documentation Build the site, then split its Markdown pages into passages. --embed sends those passages to the configured embedding provider. shoalrun build docs.config.yaml site-dist shoalrun index site-dist --embed --config docs.config.yaml Ask a question from the terminal Replace the sample question with one that your own pages answer. shoalrun ask site-dist "how do I reset my password" --config docs.config.yaml Check the answer's citations and open the source pages. Confirm that the sources support the answer, rather than accepting citations alone as proof. Open the local panel Start the server and open the address it prints. Ask the same question in the panel and follow its source links. Stop the server with Ctrl+C when finished. shoalrun serve site-dist --ask --config docs.config.yaml If something goes wrong A missing-key error names the environment variable to set in the same terminal. For missing or stale sources, rebuild the site and run index again. Keyword-only retrieval can miss questions that use different wording from the pages. This minimal setup has no relevance scorer to decline out-of-scope questions. Before broader use, review answer checks and hosting limits . To record local questions, add --log with a path outside the site output. Logging is optional; read question logging before enabling it. The CLI reference defines the other flags and report fields. Related reading Reference while working Retrieval and chat settings — Look up provider fields, environment variables, and answer settings. (Status: experimental.) Related topics How documentation answers work — Understand the layers behind cited answers before choosing additional services. (Status: experimental.)

documents.title: Share images and favicon
documents.summary: Generated social images, metadata precedence, SVG placeholders, fonts, and favicon settings.

headings.title: Use your own image for a page

documents.text: When someone pastes a page link into Slack, LinkedIn, or X, the preview shows an image. Shoalrun draws one for every page at build time and adds the tags those apps read. It also generates a favicon. Both follow the site's preset and palette, so they need no setup. For the author workflow around page titles, summaries, public URLs, and social metadata, start with SEO and social previews . What the build writes A 1200×630 PNG per page at /assets/share/<page path>.png , such as /assets/share/styling/themes.png . It shows the page type, title, and summary, the site title, and the page URL. og:title , og:description , and og:image tags, plus explicit twitter:title , twitter:description , twitter:image , and twitter:card tags. The description uses the same page text as the image. /favicon.svg , drawn from the preset's brand mark in the accent color, and a 180×180 /apple-touch-icon.png . Set site.origin to the public site address so image and page URLs in the tags are absolute and publicly reachable. A browser can load a page even when a link-preview crawler cannot fetch an image hosted at a different or private address. Run the deployment checker against the public origin to catch a mismatched og:image or a missing image. docs.config.yaml site : title : Acme API docs origin : https://docs.acme.com The preview description comes from the page's displayText.socialCard , seo.description , configured HTML description, or summary , in that order. The same text appears in og:description and on the generated image. Long titles wrap to three lines and long summaries to two, ending in an ellipsis. For a short page title such as Getting started , the social title adds the site name when the result fits within 70 characters. The page heading and browser title stay as authored. Set seo.title on a page when you want to choose its exact social title instead. The build caches rendered images in .shoalrun/cache/share-images/ beside the config file and redraws only pages whose card changed. Add .shoalrun/ to .gitignore . Use your own image for a page Set image in frontmatter to a local .png or .jpg , relative to the page file. It replaces the generated card for that page. 1200×630 works best. Frontmatter image : ./images/launch.png Replace the design Point outputs.html.shareImages.template at a 1200×630 SVG file. The build fills these placeholders on each page: Placeholder Value {{title}} , {{summary}} The full title and summary. {{title.1}} , {{title.2}} , {{title.3}} The title split into lines of about 30 characters. {{summary.1}} , {{summary.2}} The summary split into lines of about 60 characters. {{site}} site.title . {{type}} The page type as words, such as API reference . {{url}} The page URL without https:// , when site.origin is set. docs.config.yaml outputs : html : shareImages : template : ./share/card.svg fonts : [ ./share/AcmeSans-Bold.ttf ] share/card.svg < svg xmlns = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width = "1200" height = "630" > < rect width = "1200" height = "630" fill = "#0b3d2e" /> < text x = "80" y = "220" font-family = "Acme Sans" font-weight = "700" font-size = "64" fill = "#ffffff" >{{title.1}}</ text > < text x = "80" y = "296" font-family = "Acme Sans" font-weight = "700" font-size = "64" fill = "#ffffff" >{{title.2}}</ text > < text x = "80" y = "560" font-family = "Inter" font-size = "26" fill = "#cfe8dd" >{{site}}</ text > </ svg > An unknown placeholder fails the build, so a typo can't publish raw braces. The renderer doesn't load system fonts. It can use Inter, Figtree, Source Serif 4, JetBrains Mono, and Jost, plus any .ttf or .otf files listed in fonts or in theme.fonts . The renderer reads TrueType and OpenType files only. WOFF2 files from theme.fonts still work on the site, but not in share images. To turn generated images off, set shareImages: false . Pages with their own image keep it. Replace the favicon Set site.favicon to a local .svg or .png . An SVG favicon also becomes the touch icon, placed on the palette's inked surface. A PNG favicon is used as is, with no separate touch icon. docs.config.yaml site : favicon : ./brand/mark.svg A missing file or another format fails the build. Related reading Read first Themes — Set the theme that generated share images and the favicon take their look from.

documents.title: Reuse prose across pages
documents.summary: Share validated prose across pages with typed variables.
documents.text: A snippet is a shared Markdown or MDX fragment that the build expands into each page that includes it. Use one when the wording must stay in sync across pages. A template creates a draft once; editing a template does not change existing pages. Register a snippet Import a snippets mapping in project config. Snippet IDs are dot-separated names, such as authoring.build-check . Each entry points to a plain .md or .mdx file and declares its variables: docs/config/snippets.yaml authoring.build-check : file : ../snippets/build-check.mdx variables : command : { type : string , required : true } The snippet file uses <Var name="command" /> in prose: docs/snippets/build-check.mdx < Callout label = "Check the result" >Run < Var name = "command" /> after editing. Confirm the HTML page and Markdown twin contain the same resolved snippet text.</ Callout > A page includes it with literal values: docs/content/snippets.mdx < Snippet id = "authoring.build-check" values = {{ command : "npm test" }} /> See a variable resolve The example project has a second snippet with two variables: example/config/snippets.yaml payment.request-prep : file : ../snippets/request-prep.mdx variables : product : { type : string , required : true } header : { type : string , default : Idempotency-Key } Its source file contains ordinary MDX prose: example/snippets/request-prep.mdx For < Var name = "product" /> requests, choose a unique < Var name = "header" /> and provide the amount in minor currency units. The guide supplies product and leaves header at its declared default: example/content/create-payment-guide.mdx < Snippet id = "payment.request-prep" values = {{ product : "Payments" }} /> Readers and agents get resolved text in their respective page formats: For Payments requests, choose a unique Idempotency-Key and provide the amount in minor currency units. The real snippet also includes a nested retry note. It inherits product from the outer snippet. See example/snippets/request-prep.mdx and example/content/create-payment-guide.mdx in the repository. This page uses that snippet below, so the published HTML and Markdown exercise the same expansion. Check the result: Run npm test after editing. Confirm the HTML page and Markdown twin contain the same resolved snippet text. Values can be strings, numbers, or booleans. A variable can also list allowed values with enum , such as tier: { type: string, enum: [free, pro] } ; its default must be one of them. Snippet defaults, project variables, page variables, and invocation values apply in that order. Set project variables in the top-level variables mapping of docs.config.yaml , and page variables in a page's variables frontmatter: docs.config.yaml variables : product : Payments Unknown names, missing required values, wrong types, and recursive includes stop the build. The document manifest lists snippet IDs used by each page. For this slice, snippets use inline <Var /> in prose. Code blocks are never changed by string replacement. Put headings in the page, and use absolute or doc: links inside snippets. These limits avoid ambiguous anchors and broken relative links until their adapters are built. Component attributes <Snippet> is a standalone empty element in a page or registered snippet. <Var> is an inline empty element inside a snippet file; using it directly in a page fails the build. Element Attribute Required Meaning <Snippet> id Yes Registered snippet ID. <Snippet> values No Literal mapping of invocation values. <Var> name Yes Variable declared for that snippet. The included Markdown and supported MDX components render in both HTML and Markdown. Nested snippets work, but recursive includes fail. API embeds need page-level headings and cannot be placed inside snippets. Keep headings in the page, and use absolute or doc: links in snippets. Check the shared text Build your project and open each page that includes the snippet. Confirm that HTML and Markdown both contain the resolved text and that no variable tags remain. Change the snippet source and rebuild; every including page should receive that change. If validation fails, correct the named variable, include, or type before publishing. Related reading Reference while working Configuration reference — Look up the snippets and variables settings. Often confused with Templates — A template is copied into a new page once; a snippet is shared prose that stays in sync on every page that includes it.

Snippet IDs are dot-separated names, such as authoring.build-check . Each entry points to a plain .md or .mdx file and declares its variables: authoring.build-check: file: ../snippets/build-check.mdx variables: command: { type: string, required: true } The snippet file uses <Var name="command" /> in prose: <Callout label="Check the result">Run <Var name="command" /> after editing. Confirm the HTML page and Markdown twin contain the same resolved snippet text.</Callout> A page includes it with literal values: <Snippet id="authoring.build-check" values={{ command: "npm test" }} /> See a variable resolve The example project has a second snippet with two variables: payment.request-prep: file: ../snippets/request-prep.mdx variables: product: { type: string, required: true } header: { type: string, default: Idempotency-Key } Its source file contains ordinary MDX prose: For <Var name="product" /> requests, choose a unique <Var name="header" /> and provide the amount in minor currency units. The guide supplies product and leaves header at its declared default: <Snippet id="payment.request-prep" values={{ product: "Payments" }} /> Readers and agents get resolved text in their respective page formats: For Payments requests, choose a unique Idempotency-Key and provide the amount in minor currency units. The real snippet also includes a nested retry note. It inherits product from the outer snippet. See example/snippets/request-prep.mdx and example/content/create-payment-guide.mdx in the repository. This page uses that snippet below, so the published HTML and Markdown exercise the same expansion. Check the result: Run npm test after editing. Confirm the HTML page and Markdown twin contain the same resolved snippet text. Values can be strings, numbers, or booleans. A variable can also list allowed values with enum , such as tier: { type: string, enum: [free, pro] } ; its default must be one of them. Snippet defaults, project variables, page variables, and invocation values apply in that order. Set project variables in the top-level variables mapping of docs.config.yaml , and page variables in a page's variables frontmatter: variables: product: Payments Unknown names, missing required values, wrong types, and recursive includes stop the build. The document manifest lists snippet IDs used by each page. For this slice, snippets use inline <Var /> in prose. Code blocks are never changed by string replacement. Put headings in the page, and use absolute or doc: links inside snippets. These limits avoid ambiguous anchors and broken relative links until their adapters are built. Component attributes <Snippet> is a standalone empty element in a page or registered snippet. <Var> is an inline empty element inside a snippet file; using it directly in a page fails the build. Element Attribute Required Meaning <Snippet> id Yes Registered snippet ID. <Snippet> values No Literal mapping of invocation values. <Var> name Yes Variable declared for that snippet. The included Markdown and supported MDX components render in both HTML and Markdown. Nested snippets work, but recursive includes fail. API embeds need page-level headings and cannot be placed inside snippets. Keep headings in the page, and use absolute or doc: links in snippets. Check the shared text Build your project and open each page that includes the snippet. Confirm that HTML and Markdown both contain the resolved text and that no variable tags remain. Change the snippet source and rebuild; every including page should receive that change. If validation fails, correct the named variable, include, or type before publishing. Templates — A template is copied into a new page once; a snippet is shared prose that stays in sync on every page that includes it.

documents.summary: Create a documentation site, scaffold your first page from a template, and preview its HTML and Markdown.
documents.text: This quickstart takes you from installing Shoalrun to your own working documentation site. You will scaffold a page from a template, complete its draft, put it in the sidebar, and read its HTML and Markdown output. Private alpha: Your GitHub account needs access to the private @shoalrun/cli package. You do not need access to the framework source repository. Prerequisites Install Node.js 22.12 or newer and npm. Use the npm that comes with Node.js; Shoalrun sets no separate npm version. The commands below use a POSIX shell, such as Bash or Zsh. Authenticate to GitHub Packages with a classic personal access token that has read:packages . Enter it at the password prompt; keep it out of files you commit: npm login --scope=@shoalrun --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com --auth-type=legacy Your account also needs permission to read the package. A token scope alone does not grant package access. Start your own project Install an exact version of the private alpha and initialize the minimal starter: mkdir my-docs cd my-docs npm init -y npm install --save-exact @shoalrun/cli@0.1.0-alpha.2 --@shoalrun:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com npx --no-install shoalrun init . Diagrams build without Chrome. The starter puts docs.config.yaml and content/ in your project. Initialization refuses to overwrite starter files, and preserves unrelated files such as the package manifest and lockfile. Preview the starter: npx --no-install shoalrun dev docs.config.yaml site-dist --port 8765 Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ . You should see the Acme handbook example with a welcome page and an installation page. Press Ctrl+C to stop the preview before continuing. Create a page Start new pages from a template. From the same my-docs/ directory, scaffold the built-in how-to template: npx --no-install shoalrun scaffold how-to -n content/first-page.mdx \ --id guide.first-page --title 'Your first page' The command creates draft frontmatter and a body with prompts for outcomes, steps, checks, and recovery. It derives the slug /first-page and refuses to overwrite existing files. Use a registered project template when your team has one; create a page explains the choices. Open content/first-page.mdx . Set updated to today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Replace its generated summary with Find the installation guide and check its Markdown page. Keep access.policy set to draft while completing the prompts. For this small walkthrough, replace the template body below the closing frontmatter delimiter with this completed example. It keeps the introduction, actions, and verification together: Completed template body Find this handbook's installation instructions and their Markdown copy. This page is for readers exploring the example documentation site. ## Before you begin Run the local documentation preview and open its home page. No account or credentials are needed. ## Complete the task 1. Open Setup in the sidebar. 2. Choose Install Acme to open the [ installation guide ](doc:guide.install) . 3. Read the example version command. Acme is fictional; do not run it. ## Check the result The installation page shows an example command: `acme --version` . Open `/install.md` on the same local server and find that command there too. ## Handle common failures If the page does not load, restart the preview and check its printed address. If the installation page is missing, restore the minimal starter's install file. ## How it works for agents The Markdown page contains the same instructions and version command. Its installation link points to `/install.md` . ## Next steps Read the [ installation guide ](doc:guide.install) in either format. ## Editorial evidence The minimal starter's `content/install.mdx` supplies the page and example command.
