documents.title: Project status
documents.summary: What Shoalrun can do today, what I want to add next, and where its limits are.

headings.title: What I want to add next

documents.text: Shoalrun is a private prototype for publishing documentation for people and agents from the same source. This public site is built with it. The compiler and CLI are available as an invite-only alpha package; there is no public package release. What works today One source, two reading formats. Markdown and supported MDX components produce a browser site and a Markdown copy of every page . Generated indexes, manifests, and section resources help agents discover and read the content without running the site’s JavaScript. Structured authoring. Templates, reusable snippets, custom metadata, and composable configuration support guides and reference pages. Stable page IDs connect links, cards, navigation, and related reading. Recipes and cookbooks combine reusable instructions into complete workflows. Agent authoring tools provide project discovery, source context, draft previews, and local validation for your existing coding agent. Rich documentation pages. Built-in components include tabs, callouts, tables, code walkthroughs, steps, timelines, and API embeds, with defined Markdown output. Diagrams render D2 and Mermaid syntax as SVG during the build; Pele renders the Mermaid diagrams. Markdown retains the diagram source and explanation. Reader controls. File trees have expandable folders and keyboard navigation. Collapsible groups join related disclosures without gaps. Authors can synchronize related tabs and add captions or expanded viewing to images . Configurable sites. Themes, palettes, layouts, headers, and footers shape the presentation. Navigation tabs organize larger sites into sections. Explicit versions and languages publish separate page variants, while reader views tailor navigation and marked content to different audiences. API documentation. OpenAPI sources supply reference pages, named examples, request samples, and contracts for individual operations. Authors can combine generated references with guides and review imported API content before publishing it. Search and documentation tools. Built-in search works in the browser without a model key. Optional semantic search and cited answers use your configured providers. Read-only Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools let agents search and read pages or sections. They run through a local stdio process or a public HTTP endpoint on Node or Vercel. Publishing and measurement. Local previews and checks support static publishing, with Node and Vercel serving options. Optional browser analytics and HTTP MCP analytics send events through adapters to your chosen service. Both are off by default; their guides describe the event fields, filtering, and configuration. What I want to add next Custom access control. Add connectors for customers’ own role-based access control (RBAC) systems, with consistent access decisions across HTML, Markdown, search, downloads, and MCP. These are intended additions, without a promised release date or a commitment to public package or source distribution. Current limits Prototype stability. Configuration, extension points, and output formats can still change. There is no stable release or compatibility promise yet. Component extensibility. Trusted custom components lower into shared content, with a portable authoring skill. Arbitrary executable MDX remains unsupported. Project CSS, browser modules, and configured build extensions are trusted project code. API coverage. OpenAPI and JSON Schema support is partial; check the support reference against your source. Request examples are copyable, but Shoalrun does not provide a live API explorer that sends requests. Private content. Reader views do not restrict access to published files. Shoalrun has no built-in reader authentication, and its HTTP MCP endpoint currently serves one selected public publication. Host-level authorization is a separate responsibility. Managed services. Shoalrun does not provide managed hosting, translation, or chat. Versions and translations need explicit authored variants. Optional model and analytics services need your own configuration and accounts. Automatic skill generation and general agent orchestration are deliberate non-goals . Authors remain responsible for the accuracy and usefulness of their documentation. Related reading Reference while working Evaluate agent tasks against your docs — Evaluate realistic tasks against the built documentation. Connect an MCP client — Configure and test the implemented stdio documentation tools. Related topics Non-goals — Distinguish deliberate scope limits from deferred features. Changelog — Check implemented capabilities and the remaining release work. Navigation, page layouts, and browser analytics — Check the private prototype's capabilities and remaining release limits.

documents.title: Templates
documents.summary: Create and edit page starting points, then scaffold drafts from them.

headings.title: Create or edit a project template
Choose formatting enforcement for your project

documents.text: A template supplies the starting page for a new one: commented frontmatter and a body of prompts. It tells authors and agents what to write, in what order, and what to delete. scaffold copies the template once and fills in the draft fields. The result is an ordinary page that authors can change. Editing a template later affects future drafts, not pages already scaffolded. Use a snippet when the same prose must stay shared across several pages. Templates guide the initial draft; they do not enforce a permanent page structure. Built-in templates These ship with the CLI and require no templates configuration. Their names are available in every project unless a project overrides them. Template Page type Use it for tutorial tutorial Learn by following one guided exercise that builds something. Built in. how-to how-to Complete a specific task from a known starting state and verify the result. Built in. reference reference Look up exact syntax, fields, options, errors, and limits. Built in. explanation explanation Understand a concept, its context, design choices, and tradeoffs. Built in. The four primary built-in templates are inspired by the Diátaxis documentation framework : tutorial, how-to, reference, and explanation. Choose by the reader's need. A tutorial teaches through a controlled exercise; a how-to helps someone accomplish their own task; reference supplies facts; explanation develops understanding. The older guide and troubleshooting templates remain available for compatibility. Existing pages keep their types, IDs, and routes. Shoalrun also includes feature templates for recipes, ingredients, and cookbooks, described below. Built-in feature templates These also ship with the CLI and need no project registration. They support Shoalrun's API and workflow features rather than adding new Diátaxis categories. A recipe is a specialized how-to; an ingredient is reusable source for an action or check; a cookbook helps readers choose complete recipes. Template Page type Use it for api-reference api-reference The authored text above a generated operation page. Built in; requires exactly one known operation ID. recipe recipe A complete task page with instructions and a final success check; it can be written directly or assembled from ingredients. Built in; see recipe drafts . ingredient ingredient Reusable source instructions for one action or check, copied into recipe drafts. Built in; see recipe drafts . cookbook cookbook An authored page that lists complete recipe pages or offers them in a chooser. Built in; see recipe drafts . shoalrun scaffold recipe -n content/track-parcel.mdx shoalrun scaffold ingredient -n content/lookup-parcel.mdx shoalrun scaffold cookbook -n content/parcel-workflows.mdx A recipe can be written directly; ingredients and composition specs are optional. An ingredient can declare workflow metadata for handoff checks during recipe draft . A cookbook can use ordinary document links or the configured chooser. Project-added templates Project templates are named entries under templates in config. They are available only in projects that register them; installing the CLI does not provide these names. Use a custom name to add an outline, or a built-in name to override its starting content. A project template with the same name as a built-in takes precedence. For example, registering how-to replaces its starting outline in that project. Use a distinct name to add a choice instead. Neither registration nor overriding rewrites existing pages. Keep the four shapes distinct Each template gives the page a different writing purpose and boundary. Shape Writing boundary Tutorial Choose one reliable exercise and sample values. Show results early and at each step, offer repetition, and keep explanation brief. Link out for deeper reasoning and alternatives. How-to Address the reader's specific goal. Assume practical competence, allow conditional paths for real situations, and link out for background or complete reference facts. Reference Organize facts to mirror the product, with consistent sections and neutral descriptions. Examples illustrate behavior without becoming task walkthroughs. Explanation Develop a bounded topic through context, connections, design reasons, and perspectives. Discuss alternatives and tradeoffs without prescribing a task or cataloging fields. These boundaries are based on Diátaxis's guidance for tutorials , how-to guides , reference , and explanation . The templates are editable starting points, not a claim that a page conforms merely because its type is set. What every template gives you The primary Diátaxis templates use these authoring conventions; workflow templates keep the sections useful to their role: Commented frontmatter. Comments explain fields and give examples where useful. Fields you must fill in hold a placeholder. Optional fields are commented out, each with the case where it applies. A short introduction. One paragraph of 150 words or fewer sits under the title wi

documents.title: Try a theme
documents.summary: Preview every preset, palette, and color mode on this page, then copy the config.

headings.title: Add the previewer to a page

documents.text: Pick a shape, a palette, and a mode. This page restyles itself as you choose. Scroll down to see how each option styles the sample content, then copy the config into docs.config.yaml . Every preset works with every palette, in light or dark mode. Browse themes and palettes Preset Shape Default palette shoal Flat page with a ruled sidebar and square-cornered controls. kelp reef Rounded panels on a tinted page, with pill navigation and controls. coral ledger Technical manual with an inked masthead, monospace headings, and numbered sections. ink vice Night masthead with a sunset stripe, bold italic type, and neon rules. vice Palette Colors kelp Sea green on white. coral Coral accent over cool blue-gray neutrals. ink Black ink on warm paper with a vermilion accent. harbor Navy ink, blue links, and a yellow callout rule. amethyst Violet accents over lavender neutrals. vice Flamingo pink and aqua by day, neon on night purple after dark. docs.config.yaml theme : preset : vice palette : harbor mode : system The preview lasts until you leave the page or press Reset . It does not change the site for other readers. Your site's project CSS still applies on top of the preview. Sample content A guide page mixes prose, links , inline code , and components. Each preset styles them in its own way. Tip: Try the vice shape in dark mode. A table Use this sample to inspect table headers, cell spacing, and inline values in the selected theme. Setting Default Values preset shoal shoal , reef , ledger , vice palette Preset default Any built-in name, or a custom palette mode light light , dark , system A code block docs.config.yaml theme : preset : reef palette : amethyst mode : system Tabs Light Dark System Light Readers always see the light set. Dark Readers always see the dark set. System The site follows each reader's system setting, with an optional toggle. The build then publishes every preset and palette under /assets/themes/ , so the previewer works on a static host. Sites that don't use the component don't publish those files. documents.title: Themes
documents.summary: Pick a site shape, pair it with a color palette, and choose how light and dark mode behave.
documents.text: The theme setting controls how the HTML site looks. It has five keys, and each has a default: docs.config.yaml theme : preset : reef # site shape palette : harbor # colors mode : system # light, dark, or system toggle : true # reader switch for light and dark mode fonts : system # optional: turn off the preset's bundled fonts Omit theme to keep the default: the shoal preset, the kelp palette, the preset's fonts, and light mode only. An unknown value fails the build. To see every combination on a real page, open Try a theme . Start with a preset. Change the palette if its colors don't fit your brand. Set the mode if readers need dark mode. Use project CSS for anything else. Presets A preset sets the shape of the site. It controls layout, corner radii, and type, and how panels, navigation, and cards look. Each preset has a default palette. Any palette works with any preset. Preset Shape Default palette shoal Flat page with a ruled sidebar and square-cornered controls. kelp reef Rounded panels float on a tinted page. Navigation items and controls are pills. coral ledger A technical manual with an inked masthead, serif body text, monospace headings, numbered sections, and hard-edged cards. ink vice A night masthead with a sunset stripe, bold italic display type, neon section rules, and cards that glow on hover. vice Presets change CSS only. Page markup, URLs, and Markdown twins stay the same. Fonts Each preset ships its own fonts, so the site looks the same on every operating system: Preset Body Headings Code shoal Inter Inter System monospace reef Figtree Figtree System monospace ledger Source Serif 4 JetBrains Mono JetBrains Mono vice Figtree Jost System monospace The fonts are Latin variable fonts under the SIL Open Font License. The build copies them to /assets/fonts/ with their license files. A browser downloads only the faces a page uses, and the page preloads its body font. Characters outside the Latin set use the system fallback. Until a font arrives, the page uses a local font resized to match it. Text doesn't shift when the bundled font loads. Agents read the Markdown twins, which load no fonts. To use system fonts only, set fonts: system . Each preset then falls back to its system font stack. Use your own fonts Set any of body , headings , and code . A role you leave out keeps the preset's font. headings defaults to the body font. docs.config.yaml theme : preset : reef fonts : body : family : Acme Sans files : - ./fonts/AcmeSans.woff2 - { file : ./fonts/AcmeSans-Italic.woff2 , style : italic } headings : Acme Display code : family : Berkeley Mono files : [ ./fonts/BerkeleyMono.woff2 ] family is the name CSS uses. A plain string, such as headings: Acme Display , names a font without shipping files. Use it for a font that project CSS loads, or one installed on readers' machines. files lists local .woff2 , .woff , .ttf , or .otf files, relative to the config file that declares them. The build copies them to /assets/fonts/project/ . File names can use letters, numbers, dots, dashes, and underscores, and two files can't share a name. Each file can set style ( normal or italic ) and weight , such as 400 or "100 900" . The default weight, "100 900" , suits variable fonts; give each static file its own weight. A missing file, an unsupported format, or an unknown key fails the build. Check that your font license allows web embedding. Fonts set here become the --font-body , --font-heading , and --font-code CSS tokens , each followed by a system fallback. Load order The HTML page links stylesheets in this order. Later files override earlier ones. /assets/site.css , which imports the base tokens and header styles. /assets/theme-preview.css follows it, on pages that use the theme previewer . /assets/theme.css , for a preset other than shoal . /assets/palette.css , generated for any palette or mode other than kelp in light mode. /assets/fonts.css , generated from theme.fonts , unless it's system and sets nothing. /assets/project.css , from site.customCss . When a site uses a non-default preset, palette, or mode, the html element carries data-theme and data-palette . The ledger and vice presets also set data-masthead="inked" , which switches header tools to light text on a dark masthead. Project CSS can target one combination: styles/project.css [ data-theme = "ledger" ] .page-head h1 { letter-spacing : 0 ; } Related reading Next steps Color palettes — Choose the colors the preset uses. Light and dark mode — Decide whether readers get light mode, dark mode, or a toggle. Go deeper CSS and theme reference — Customize tokens and selectors beyond what presets and palettes offer. Related topics Try a theme — Preview every preset, palette, and color mode on a live page.

documents.title: Troubleshooting
documents.summary: Troubleshoot a build, recover missing pages and fix document links, route collisions, MDX errors, API review digests, and diagram rendering.

headings.title: Two pages claim one identity or route
An API review digest is missing or stale
Local output works but the deployed site fails

documents.text: Run these commands from your documentation project, with SHOALRUN_CLI pointing to the compiled CLI as in the quickstart . Start by rebuilding so the error names the current source file: node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" config validate docs.config.yaml node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" build docs.config.yaml dist Config validation checks configuration; a full build also resolves content, links, routes, and API reviews. The messages below are compiler message fragments; file paths and document IDs vary by project. A page is missing Drafts and pages outside enabled publications can be excluded without a build error. Inspect both the effective config and the built page list: node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" config resolve docs.config.yaml node -e 'const m = require("./dist/documents.json"); console.log(JSON.stringify(m.documents, null, 2))' Check the page's resolved access.policy is public and its channel, version, and language match an entry in publications.enabled . frontmatter.enforced overrides page values; a draft enforced there keeps even an explicitly public page out of the build. See versions and languages . If the manifest contains the page but the menu does not, add its exact document ID to navigation (or the YAML file included there): navigation : - id : my-page doc : guide.my-page Append that entry to the existing list. Scaffolding a file does not add it to navigation. A navigation reference to an unavailable page is omitted for that publication. If publishing instead fails with unresolved scaffold placeholders cannot be published , finish every scaffold TODO and replace the draft summary before setting access: { policy: public } . An internal link fails unknown document link doc:guide.install means the target is unavailable in the linking page's publication. Check spelling against the target's id , its public access, and its publication fields. A source file in another version or language does not satisfy the link. Add the corresponding variant or link to an available page. Use doc: plus a document ID for internal links, for example [Install](doc:guide.install) . File paths are not document IDs. Rebuild after correcting the source and target. Two pages claim one identity or route Duplicate document identity means two files have the same ID and publication combination. Keep one file per variant, or assign a distinct ID to a different page. Route collision /install means different pages produce the same final URL. Check their slugs together with language, channel, and version prefixes. Output artifact collision can also mean a page conflicts with a generated resource or another output file. Resolve the source configuration; changing the output directory does not fix conflicting URLs. Versions and languages shows how prefixes distinguish editions. MDX cannot compile dynamic MDX expression has no semantic adapter means the page contains JavaScript expressions that Shoalrun cannot project into its published formats. Replace executable MDX with Markdown or one of the supported components . Put code intended for readers inside a fenced code block so it remains literal text. Component validation errors name the source file and component. Check the component's documented attributes and nesting. Ordinary MDX syntax errors can also come from unescaped braces or angle brackets in prose; use inline code for literal syntax. An API review digest is missing or stale apis.payments.publicReview.digest is missing or apis.payments.publicReview.digest is stale means the published API content needs review. Generate a local candidate: API_REVIEW_DIR = "$( mktemp -d )" node "$SHOALRUN_CLI" api review docs.config.yaml --output "$API_REVIEW_DIR" Inspect the candidate pages, contracts, source downloads, and input hashes. Copy the reported digest into that API's publicReview.digest , then run the normal build again. Source changes, selections, embeds, and source-publication choices can change the digest. Do not copy a digest from another project or bypass the review by publishing the candidate output. See Add an OpenAPI API . A diagram fails to render failed to render mermaid diagram "Review flow" (or d2 ) includes the source file and the renderer's underlying error. If it names diagram syntax, fix the code fence and rebuild. Errors such as <Diagram> needs exactly one nonempty mermaid code fence concern component structure; follow the diagram reference . Mermaid syntax renders with Pele; it does not need Chrome or Mermaid CLI. Check Pele’s compatibility guide if source from another Mermaid renderer fails. D2 uses the installed @d2lang/d2 runtime. Reinstall framework dependencies if either renderer is missing. Include the source file, diagram title, and complete underlying error when reporting a failure. Local output works but the deployed site fails A successful local build does not check the host's routing or headers. Use Check a deployed site for wrong Markdown content types, missing negotiation, discovery resources, or 404 responses. The publishing guide

documents.title: Publish on Vercel
documents.summary: Build a Vercel deployment with Markdown negotiation and correct discovery headers.
documents.text: Shoalrun can produce a Vercel Build Output API directory. It contains the compiled static site and routing rules for each published page. Vercel serves HTML to browsers and the generated Markdown twin when a request includes Accept: text/markdown . The route rules also set Vary: Accept and an HTTP Link header to the .md page. Explicit .md URLs remain available. The content negotiation guide explains the same HTTP contract for any host. This page shows how to configure Vercel specifically. Prepare your project Start with the quickstart . Your documentation repository installs the private package and keeps its own content and configuration. It needs no framework source checkout: .npmrc package.json package-lock.json docs.config.yaml content/ vercel.json Set site.origin in docs.config.yaml to your intended public HTTPS origin before release. This controls canonical and share-image URLs. Generate deployment output locally: npx --no-install shoalrun vercel build docs.config.yaml .vercel/output Generating output does not deploy it. Configure the project For host installs, commit a project .npmrc containing only the registry and an environment-variable placeholder: .npmrc @shoalrun:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} Set NODE_AUTH_TOKEN in Vercel's build environment to a GitHub classic token with read:packages , owned by an account with access to the package. Set it for each environment that should install the package, including Preview if enabled. Keep the token out of the repository. Local npm ci with this .npmrc also requires that environment variable. Set the Vercel project root to the documentation repository root and choose the Other framework preset. Add: vercel.json { "$schema" : "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json" , "framework" : null , "installCommand" : "npm ci" , "buildCommand" : "npx --no-install shoalrun vercel build docs.config.yaml .vercel/output" } Keep the build output directory setting unset: this command produces the Build Output API directory directly. If your config lives under docs/ , adjust its path. Connecting the Git repository can trigger builds on pushes; check your build budget before enabling that integration. Deploy Shoalrun's own documentation The docs repository's root vercel.json serves the site under docs/ . It runs npm ci and npm run docs:vercel using the installed package. Production and local builds use the public https://www.shoalrun.com origin in docs/docs.config.yaml for absolute page and share-image URLs. Preview builds use their VERCEL_URL instead. Public link previews require the shared page and its image to be accessible without sign-in. Vercel deployment protection can prevent crawlers from reading preview deployments. The Vercel output puts pages and discovery files in .vercel/output/static/ . Its config.json defines page routes and content types, including text/markdown for .md files and the linkset type for /.well-known/api-catalog when that file exists. Keep the entire .vercel/output/ directory together for deployment. The API catalog is optional and appears only when the project declares a public API endpoint and publishes its source. For Shoalrun's own site, npm run docs:build-all makes a complete prebuilt bundle: it compiles the pages and embeds the passages for hosted chat and search. Repeat builds reuse private passage vectors when retrieval settings and passage digests match. Only new or changed passages need embedding. The build reports embedded and reused counts. It generates answer cards from docs/config/answers.yaml when the passages, questions, chat settings, or generator code have changed; otherwise it reuses the previous verified cards. It checks passage coverage and card digests before returning. The index and cards stay inside private functions. New embeddings call the configured provider; generating cards also calls the relevance scorer and chat model. Review answers.json in the function before deployment. Deleting .vercel/output removes the local vector and card caches. The docs repository's README has the local command sequence. The hosted search endpoint uses embeddings within shared rate and daily budgets, then returns lexical results when its embedding budget is exhausted. The card cache lives in the previous local .vercel/output bundle. The command compares a fingerprint of its passage index, embedding metadata, question list, chat and retrieval settings, and compiled generator code with the new bundle. When they match, it copies the prior cards into the new private function and checks their source digests again. If the inputs changed, the old bundle is missing, or validation fails, it regenerates all cards. The final line says reused or generated . This saves card model and scorer calls on an unchanged rebuild. A fresh checkout or deleted .vercel/output has no local card or passage vector cache. Deploy without connecting GitHub You can keep building locally and deploy the Build Output AP

documents.title: What is Shoalrun?
documents.summary: A one-page introduction to Shoalrun's document-first approach, its outputs, and the current prototype.
documents.text: Shoalrun is a documentation compiler for product and API docs. It reads project configuration, Markdown and supported MDX pages, and optional local OpenAPI files. From those sources, it builds a site for people and readable Markdown pages for agents. The normal build is deterministic: it makes no model calls or network requests. Documents have an identity In Shoalrun, a document is more than a file at a path. It has a stable ID, metadata, and relationships to other documents. Navigation, page cards, and links can refer to that ID. You can move a source file without reconnecting those parts of the site. The published URL is a separate choice: changing a page's slug changes its URL and may need a redirect. That identity lets information connect across the site. A guide can link to an exact API operation, a related page, or a complete workflow without relying on where its source file lives. One source serves different readers Shoalrun builds HTML and a Markdown twin from the same accepted content. Browser components can give people tabs, diagrams, and other ways to explore an idea; their Markdown form keeps the useful content readable without browser scripts. Authors can also write a section for just one output when people and agents need different explanations. The build publishes a document manifest and discovery files so software can find the pages and their relationships. documents.title: Example writing guide
documents.summary: Adapt this site's writing guide for your own documentation and agent instructions.
documents.text: This page is an example of a project writing guide. The rules below are the house style for Shoalrun's own documentation site, and authors and agents use them through project instructions. Shoalrun does not automatically apply these rules to other projects. Adapt this example Save your team's writing guide in the project and give your agent its path in project instructions. Include reviewed examples appropriate to the page type. Configure your own Vale rules for automated checks. Design a writing guide explains how to choose useful rules and examples. Example audience and scope Write for someone trying to understand or complete a task in Shoalrun. Assume they can edit a text file; introduce framework-specific concepts before relying on them. State prerequisites when a task needs terminal, Git, API, or deployment knowledge. Page purpose and structure Choose the page type by the reader's goal and the actual content. Keep one primary purpose per page. Split substantial conceptual discussion from a procedure and connect the pages with related reading. Page type Reader goal Useful structure Tutorial Learn through a guided exercise. Outcome, prerequisites, one reliable path with sample values, visible results, and a final check. Explain only what the exercise needs; link to deeper discussion. How-to Complete a specific task. Starting state, necessary prerequisites, actions in execution order, success check, and likely failures. Put decisions before the steps they affect. Reference Look up an exact fact. When the feature applies, syntax or fields, defaults, constraints, examples, and errors. Organize facts for lookup. Explanation Understand a concept or design. The question being explained, definitions, a concrete example, reasons and tradeoffs, and links to practical tasks. Ingredient Reuse one task step in several recipes. Required inputs and prerequisites, one action with its instructions, named outputs, and an observable check. Keep the step independent of any recipe's position or neighboring wording. Recipe Complete one task from a known starting state. Outcome, prerequisites, ordered actions, failure guidance, and a final success check. Include everything needed to follow the published page on its own. Cookbook Choose between complete recipes. Explain who each path is for, what it needs, and what it produces; link to the published recipe pages. State whether choices are alternatives or can be combined. Changelog entry Understand a dated change. User-visible behavior, scope, migration when needed, and limitations. Say when a change concerns the private prototype; claim a release only with release evidence. These are editorial shapes, not mandatory heading names. Follow the template rules and adapt the outline to the reader's need. Headings in a page body start at level two because the renderer supplies the title. Do not add step numbers to authored headings. For a procedure with titled steps, use the Steps component ; it supplies the numbering in HTML and Markdown. Voice and explanations Address the reader as “you.” Use active voice and concrete verbs. Start a paragraph with its main point, then supply the reason or example needed to understand it. Keep sentences short enough to follow without breaking every thought into a separate paragraph. Name the action and its result. Replace claims such as “powerful,” “seamless,” and “easy” with behavior the reader can observe. Avoid inflated words, ceremonial introductions, repeated summaries, and invented terminology. Before Better Reason Utilize the configuration to leverage publication capabilities. “Set the channel and version in the page's frontmatter.” Names the fields and action. It is important to note that a Markdown twin is generated. “The build creates a Markdown copy of each published page.” Identifies the actor and defines the result. “Run CI to validate it.” “Run the project's automated checks. Continuous integration (CI) runs those checks when code changes.” Explains the acronym and mechanism. “Hybrid improves relevance.” “Hybrid search combines word matching and vector rankings. Whether it helps depends on the queries and ranking settings.” Defines the term and limits the claim. Define an unfamiliar term at its first useful appearance, even when the glossary also defines it. Explain acronyms before using them repeatedly. Prefer one small example to a chain of new terms. Preserve exact command, field, model, and component names in code formatting. Procedures and examples Show the starting directory, required inputs, and expected result when a command depends on them. Say which values readers must replace. Keep commands supported by source or verified behavior; do not invent flags to make an example look complete. Give each procedure step one purpose. Put the explanation beside the action it supports. Include a check that readers can perform and describe what success looks like. Troubleshooting should identify a symptom, likely cause, and concrete next a

It shows the operation contract; follow any related guides below for task steps and context. OpenAPI for this operation: Download JSON . GET /Search/parcels/{scope} List parcel records List records for an account or region. Use downloadAs to request a file; the same successful status can return JSON, CSV, or a spreadsheet. Servers https://sandbox.api.cedar-parcel.example/v1 — Sandbox https://api.cedar-parcel.example/v1 — Production Authentication Use one of these authentication options: Bearer token HTTP bearer (JWT). Short-lived service token. API key API key in header X-Parcel-Key. Long-lived account key. Parameters scope (path) Required The account or region identifier. string Default example : "region-demo" Filters (query) Optional OpenAPI calls this placeholder parameters . Send a filter expression directly in the query string, without parameters= . Query form: ?declaredValue(gt)=100 . Replace the field, operator, and value for your filter.
